# Part One

->By this, one's own good and bad fortune<-
->should be known for those who ask;<-
->and by the breath of one's own self at that time,<-
->let things like lost items be spoken of. || 28 ||<-

->On the days of the Moon, Mercury, Jupiter, and Venus,<-
->the wind moving on the left,<-
->and on the days of Mars, the Sun, and Saturn, moving on the right,<-
->is considered desirable for men.<-
->On the days of the gentle planets, moving on the right<-
->is undesirable; on the days of the cruel planets, moving on the left.<-
->The distinctions of the good and bad results of the two winds<-
->shall be told here. || 29 ||<-

->On all days, when the wind is<-
->desirable, there is health of body,<-
->gain of wealth, and sweet food;<-
->otherwise, it is the opposite for those desired things.<-

---

The location of the five elements <note>The Mahabhutas: Earth, Water, Fire, Air, and Ether</note> starting with Earth is determined by that <term>breath</term> <note>Sanskrit: shvasa</note> whose movement is understood. It is implied that all good and bad fortune of those who ask should be known through this. By the <term>wind</term> <note>Sanskrit: samirana</note> <gloss>breath</gloss> of the <term>astrologer</term> <note>Sanskrit: jyotirvid</note> themselves at that time—meaning the time of the query—the declaration of good and bad fortune is made. || 28 ||

**Regarding the days**: "Desirable" means yielding auspicious results. "Undesirable" means yielding inauspicious results. On auspicious days <note>Monday, Wednesday, Thursday, and Friday</note>, the movement of the <term>left channel</term> <note>Sanskrit: vama-nadi; associated with the lunar/cooling energy</note> is auspicious. On "sinful" or harsh days <note>Sunday, Tuesday, and Saturday</note>, the movement of the <term>right channel</term> <note>Sanskrit: dakshina-nadi; associated with the solar/heating energy</note> is auspicious. If they are reversed, it is inauspicious. "Distinctions" refers to specific details. The meaning is that the good and bad results mentioned in general will now be explained in detail. || 29 ||

**Regarding all**: This refers to all days, whether auspicious or inauspicious. "When the wind is desirable" means moving through the left channel on auspicious days and the right channel on harsh days. Regarding the phrase "and so on": [otherwise] there is conflict or quarreling with everyone, [excessive] reclining or sleep, and the [uncontrolled] release of excrement or waste. || 30 ||

<summary>This text explains how an astrologer uses their own nasal breath patterns (Svara) to answer queries, noting that the left nostril should dominate on "gentle" days and the right on "harsh" days for success. It warns that reversed breathing patterns correlate with illness, loss, and social conflict.</summary>

# Chapter Two

->If the breath is unfavorable, food will not be flavorful,<-
->wealth will not be acquired, and conflict will arise;<-
->one will not find comfort in sleep, nor will there be ease<-
->even in the discharge of waste. || 30 ||<-

->If the breath is unfavorable during the day:<-
->on Sunday, there is bodily pain;<-
->on Monday, there is a quarrel; on Tuesday, death;<-
->on Wednesday, a journey to a distant land;<-
->on Thursday, a calamity for the kingdom; on Friday,<-
->no success in any undertaking;<-
->and on Saturday, the loss of one's strength and crops,<-
->as well as disputes over land. || 31 ||<-

->If the wind <note>breath</note> flows through the left nostril for eight consecutive Sundays,<-
->one's teacher <note>Guru</note> will pass away;<-
->likewise, if it flows through the right for eight consecutive Mondays,<-
->a great illness will occur.<-
->On Tuesdays, misfortune for one's son; on Wednesdays, imprisonment;<-
->if it flows through the right for eight days of Jupiter <note>Thursday</note>,<-
->one's own death is certain; or the death of a teacher may occur. || 32 ||<-

**Regarding the breath...** This verse is intended to describe specific unfavorable results based on the different days of the week. "Death" refers to one's own, that of a kinsman, or of someone living nearby. <term>Ila-vivada</term> <note>original: "इळाविवाद"</note> refers to legal disputes concerning land. "Loss of one's strength and crops" is mentioned, and the word "etcetera" implies that other inauspicious results should also be considered. || 31 ||

**Regarding the wind...** These two verses explain the specific results that occur if the breath remains unfavorable for eight consecutive days starting from Sunday and the other planets. If the wind flows through the left <note>the lunar channel</note> continuously for eight Sundays, the death of the teacher will follow. The same logic applies to the subsequent cases. The word "continuously" should be applied to each of the seven statements.

<note>The text uses planetary names for days of the week: Bhanu (Sun/Sunday), Shitanshu (Moon/Monday), Kuja (Mars/Tuesday), Vid (Mercury/Wednesday), Dhishana (Jupiter/Thursday), Shukra (Venus/Friday), and Manda (Saturn/Saturday).</note>

# Path of Inquiry
<note>original: "Prashna Marga," a 17th-century Sanskrit treatise on natal and horary astrology</note>

If the wind <note>the breath</note> flows through the right nostril, it causes the loss of wealth acquired through Venusian means <note>luxuries, arts, or partnerships</note>. If it flows through the left, and Saturn is dominant, there is the destruction of the wife or the loss of one's residence. || 33 ||

Now, the measurement of the breath, its movement through the elements such as Earth, and the resulting effects are described:

-> For the Earth element, the length is sixteen fingers; for Water, <-
-> the length is twelve fingers; <-
-> for Fire, it is eight fingers; for Air, <-
-> it is six fingers <note>literally "two less than the previous"</note>; <-
-> and for Ether, it is known to be even less. This is declared <-
-> as the nature of the five elements <-
-> in the movement of one's own breath, <-
-> and it is equal for both nostrils. || 34 ||

"Five-foldness" refers to death. Or, alternatively, it signifies a very great illness. "Of the enemy" refers to the perpetrator. "Bondage" refers to one's own actions or the results of one's deeds. The word "Self" refers to the highest self or that which pertains to oneself. In the section beginning with "of Mars," the sequence of the eight days of the week is implied. "Loss of residence" means the destruction of the house; this is another alternative. This becomes very clear only to those who examine their breath daily, record the specific channels <note>nadis</note> of its movement, and investigate it thoroughly. || 32, 33 ||

**"Now" etc.:** By "measurement," we mean the extent of the length. "Of that" refers to the breath. "Movement through the five elements" refers to Earth and the others. "The fruit" refers to the result of that movement. Here, one should place the right hand in the middle of the bridge of the nose, exhale the breath, and examine whether the breath goes out more through the left or the right nasal channel. One must carefully and subtly understand how much length that breath possesses. Once the length of the breath is understood in this way, the movement of the Earth and other elements should be known according to the measurements to be stated.

**"Of the Earth" etc.:** "Sun" means twelve. "Elephants" means eight. "Two less than the elephant-measure" means six fingers. "Fires" means three. "Sixteen fingers" means it is not less than that. The same should be observed in other cases. Thus, it should be understood that no one's breath length will be less than these finger-measurements. Furthermore, by saying "that of Ether is less than that," and then stating that Ether is one finger, this is for the sake of purifying the traditional oral sequence. A more extensive explanation of this is found in our Kerala commentary. || 34 ||

->When the breath moves through the Earth element, it grants the clipping of wings <note>original: "paksacche"; likely a metaphor for stabilizing or grounding</note>, the entry into houses with high temple walls, and the bestowing of royal consecration.<-
->It facilitates other desired works; similarly, the Water element flowing on the left side is auspicious,<-
->governing the construction of wells and marriage; however, if it arises otherwise, it causes fear. || 35 ||<-

->The Fire element causes fear of enemies, injury from weapons, bodily disease, the burning of houses,<-
->or the fall of children and others; in such a fire, one should worship the Supreme Lord.<-
->The Air element brings fear of thieves, fleeing from one's own place, and the mounting of elephants and horses;<-
->furthermore, if the Ether element arises: || 36 ||<-

->There is the repeated attainment of instruction in mantras and the like, the consecration of deities,<-
->and initiation; yet it also brings the emergence of disease and constant, intense suffering of the body.<-

**Regarding "When the wings..." ||** The Earth element refers to the breath moving therein. It facilitates entry into houses characterized by high temple walls and enclosures. Here, the word "temple" <term>mandira: inner apartments or shrines</term> refers to the inner rooms, while "house" <term>griha: the whole structure</term> refers to the entire complex. Other auspicious acts mentioned, such as the construction of wells and marriage <term>karagraha: literally 'taking the hand'</term>, are also included. Regarding the phrase "causes fear from water," one must supply the context that this occurs when the Water element flows on the right side <note>The right nostril is solar/heating, which conflicts with the cool Water element</note>. This is because fear arising from water cannot be an auspicious result, and the original commentator has explained it thus. This result should be declared only after considering the four-fold pulse and the five lunar dates. || 35 ||

**Regarding "Fire..." ||** The text should be read as "fear of enemies" <note>original: "ari-bhaya"</note>; "arug" refers to a wound or sore. "Scorching" means burning. "Worship the Lord" means one should worship their chosen deity to negate the aforementioned inauspicious results. The phrase "fleeing from one's own place" should be understood as abandoning one's home.

# Chapter Two

Here, another authoritative scripture is also recorded:

->The *Ida* <note>The left-hand energy channel associated with the moon</note> is the left-side channel, and the *Pingala* <note>The right-hand energy channel associated with the sun</note> is the right. The one rising through the middle path is called *Sushumna*. (40)<-

->The *Ida* brings success when departing,<-
->While the *Pingala* brings success when entering.<-
->In the practice of Yoga, the middle channel<-
->Is praised, but not for other worldly activities. (41)<-

->When the "Lord" <note>The breath</note> moves in the right side, and a man<-
->Afflicted by disease asks a question while standing on the right,<-
->That man shall live long and free from illness.<-
->If a woman's body is distressed by disease while the "Lord" is in the left,<-
->And she asks from the left, she will surely be freed from sickness<-
->And live a long life. (42)<-

**"Here"** refers to the subject of predicting outcomes by examining the breath.

**"The Ida"** refers to that specific name. "Channel" <term>Nadi: literally a tube or vein, here referring to the flow of breath through the nostril</term> refers to the nostril. "Of the Moon" means it has the Moon as its presiding deity. The same logic applies to the subsequent terms. "The Middle" refers to the essence of the breath flowing equally through both nostrils. These deities and names are well-known in the Yoga scriptures. It should be understood that these three channels alone are what was indicated previously by the "movements of the sun and moon." (40)

**"In departing"** means that at the time the breath is exiting through the left nostril, one should set out from one's home. At the time the breath is exiting through the right nostril, one should enter the palace or one's destination; in short, this leads to the fulfillment of all desires. When the breath is in the *Sushumna* <note>the middle channel</note>, nothing should be done except for the practice of Yoga exercises. (41)

**"The Lord"**—the words "God" <note>original: Deva</note> and "Lord" <note>original: Ishvara</note> here refer to the Air <note>the breath</note>. If the movement of the breath and the position of the messenger <note>the person asking the question</note> are on the same side—specifically the right side for a male patient and the left side for a female patient—then one should predict firm recovery of health and a long life. "In the left" refers to a woman. (42)

# The Path of Inquiry

->If the breath <note>original: "deva," literally 'the shining one' or 'the deity,' here referring to the vital breath</note> flows through the left nostril while the inquirer stands on the right,<-
->or if the positions are reversed,<-
->the wise declare that the resulting disease will be difficult to cure. 43<-

->If the inquirer asks while the breath is moving inward,<-
->the person will live and be free from disease.<-
->But if the breath moves outward through that same path,<-
->they depart for the city of the King of the Dead <note>Yama, the god of death</note>. 44<-

->Whether on the left or the right side, if the inquiry occurs while the breath is present on that same side,<-
->the man or woman will live; this is the method established in the *Anushthana Paddhati* <note>A manual of ritual and practice</note>. 45<-

->In the absence of hearing, seeing, or remembering signs of destruction,<-
->if the messenger and the breath are in the same position, the patient lives; in the opposite case, they die. 46<-

---

**Regarding "The breath..." (Verse 43):** This means that if the side where the inquirer stands and the side where the breath is flowing are different, one should state that the disease is <term>difficult to cure</term> <note>original: "krichra-sadhya," a medical prognosis where recovery is possible but arduous</note>.

**Regarding "Inward..." (Verse 44):** Breath is indeed twofold, consisting of inhalation and exhalation. Through inhalation, the air moves inward; through exhalation, it moves outward. The first half of the verse means that if the inquiry happens while the air is moving inward via inhalation, the patient will regain health and live. The second half means that an inquiry made while the air is moving outward via exhalation grants death. In this context, "the breath" acts as the descriptor for the outward movement, and "the patient" is understood as the subject who "departs." Some interpret this to mean that if the inquirer leaves the presence of the <term>astrologer</term> <note>original: "daivajña," one who knows the divine/fate</note> by the same path they arrived, the patient will die, but that interpretation is questionable.

**Regarding "Left..." (Verse 45):** The core idea is that the messenger and the breath occupying the same side is the primary sign of life.

**Regarding "Destruction..." (Verse 46):** <term>Signs of destruction</term> <note>original: "laya-lingani"</note> refer to omens of death. The verse refers to the absence of hearing, seeing, or remembering such omens. "In the opposite case" refers to the presence of hearing, seeing, or remembering signs of destruction, or the messenger and the breath being in different positions. Alternatively, even if signs of destruction are not perceived, the messenger and breath being in different directions is the most important factor. Thus, it aligns with the meaning of the previous verse. This verse is found in the *Anushthana Paddhati*.

<summary>This text explains how an astrologer uses the flow of their own breath (Svara) and the physical position of a messenger to predict a patient's prognosis. Alignment between the breath and the messenger signifies life, while misalignment or exhalation during the query suggests death.</summary>

### If the seeker stands in front or to the left, and the breath flows through the Moon <note>the left nostril</note>, all that is asked during the bright fortnight is gained through the Moon’s movement.
### If they stand behind, below, or to the right during the dark fortnight, it is certainly gained through the Sun’s movement <note>the right nostril</note>. One should describe the seeker’s entire situation as being identical to one's own state. || 47 ||

### Whatever experience you have yourself regarding bathing, eating, sleeping, or other personal daily actions,
### That same experience should be told to the seeker as their own. || 48 ||

### Wherever the seeker is positioned, if the messenger <note>the person bringing the question</note> remains steady while the breath is flowing,
### The patient will surely live; of this there is no doubt. || 49 ||

**"In front..." etc. ||** The word "standing" is an adjective for the "seeker" (which is implied here). "From the Moon’s movement" means from the flow of the breath in the left channel <note>original: "vama-nadi"</note>. The word "standing" should also be applied to the second half of the verse. "Certainly" means for sure. "From the Sun’s movement" means from the flow of the breath in the right channel <note>original: "dakshina-nadi"</note>. The fourth line concerns the description of the "state" mentioned in other breath-related teachings. Whatever states—such as happiness or sorrow—the astrologer <term>Daivajña: one who knows the divine/fate</term> experiences, the seeker's state is similar or corresponding to that. He clarifies this very point in the next verse. || 47 ||

**"Bathing..." etc. ||** "That same" means an identical experience. Having briefly inserted this description of the seeker's state within the discussion of breath for the sake of conciseness, the author returns to the ongoing description of auspicious and inauspicious breath in the next verse. || 48 ||

**"Wherever..." etc. ||** "In whatever place," whether left or right. "While the breath is flowing" or even if it is not. "Immediately after the question." "Steady" means unmoving. || 49 ||

**"The East..." etc. ||** The phrase "should be known" is connected here. It should be understood that if the breath flows through the Earth element <note>original: "prithivi-bhuta"</note>, the lost object is in the Eastern direction from the seeker's house, and so on. "In that very spot" means exactly where it was originally; it is not actually "lost" <note>i.e., it is misplaced rather than stolen</note>. This specifically concerns questions about lost items <term>Nashta-prashna: inquiry into lost or destroyed objects</term>. One might worry that this contradicts verses like "Buried in the earth...", but there is no room for such doubt here. Those verses did not specify the divisions of directions, whereas this one does; thus, there is no mutual contradiction. Alternatively, let this be another method. What is the harm in that? In the science of astrology <term>Jyotish-shastra</term>, many different options/methods are applicable everywhere for the sake of making predictions. As will be said later: "Clarity comes from the agreement of two or three methods." Furthermore, in all scriptures, regarding rules, options—

### Page 30

On auspicious days during the bright fortnight <note>the waxing moon</note>, the left channel <note>the Ida nadi, associated with the moon</note> grants success. On inauspicious days during the dark fortnight <note>the waning moon</note>, the other channel <note>the Pingala or right nadi, associated with the sun</note> is more effective for achieving goals. || 51 ||

If one leaves the house while the lunar breath is active and enters the battlefield while the solar breath is active, they will be victorious even if they are a coward, provided they keep the enemy on their "empty" side <note>the side where breath is not currently flowing</note>. || 52 ||

If one leaves the house with the solar breath and enters the battlefield with the lunar breath, or if the enemy is positioned on their "living" side <note>the side where breath is flowing</note>, even a hero will meet his destruction. || 53 ||

Thieves, enemies, kings, gamblers, and litigants—these are harmless when positioned on one's "empty" side, but are remembered as terrifying when they stand on the "full" side. || 54 ||

In disputes, gambling, war, bathing, eating, and sexual intercourse; in legal dealings, moments of fear, or during a retreat, the solar channel <note>the right nostril</note> is highly praised. || 55 ||

In journeys, giving charity, marriages, putting on new clothes or ornaments, in auspicious ceremonies, making peace, or entering a new place, the left channel <note>the left nostril</note> is highly praised. || 56 ||

---

This principle is observed in practice. It is also followed in the Vedic rituals. Why then should there be any objection to it in Astrology, which is a limb of the Vedas? This is especially true regarding specific predictions. Enough on this point. || 50 ||

**Regarding "On auspicious days..." :** This is an elaboration of the previous point. || 51 ||

**Regarding "From the house..." :** "In the field" refers to the battlefield. This verse reiterates what was said earlier: "The left channel is auspicious for departure." It suggests that this should be applied specifically to war. The instruction to "keep the enemy on the empty side" is the key rule. "Empty" means devoid of air flow. The word "side" refers to that specific direction or portion of the body. || 52 ||

**Regarding "If one leaves..." :** This is stated as the opposite of the previous verse. Although the meaning is implied by the former, it is stated here to reinforce the point, following the logical method of showing both the positive rule and the negative consequence. || 53 ||

**Regarding "Thieves..." :** "Dasyus" refers to thieves and similar people. "Gamblers" are those who play with dice. "Litigants" are those engaged in verbal disputes. "Harmless" means they are unable to cause trouble. One should always keep all these people on the side where the breath is empty. One should personally remain on the side where the breath is full. The secret is that by doing this, victory in all matters is achieved without effort.

**Regarding "In disputes..." :** The "Solar Channel" refers to the time when the breath is moving through the right side. "Gambling and war" and "bathing and eating" are treated as paired activities in the grammar here. || 55 ||

**Regarding "In journeys..." :** The "Left Channel" refers to the time of breath movement on that side. There might be a doubt here: earlier texts stated that the Pingala <note>right channel</note> is auspicious for entering, while the current text says the left channel is praised for entering. This conflict is addressed by considering the specific context of the entry.

<summary>This page details the "Swarodaya" system of breath divination, explaining how the flow of air through the left (lunar) or right (solar) nostril determines success in war, litigation, and daily rituals. It emphasizes the tactical advantage of positioning enemies on the "empty" side of one's breath flow.</summary>

## Chapter Two

> If the breath is in the right nostril when seeing a pregnant woman, the child is male; if the breath is in the left side, it is a girl. If the breath flows in neither, the offspring is non-viable <note>literally "unreal" or "bad" offspring, likely referring to a stillbirth or lack of conception</note>. || 57 ||
>
> When asked "What is in my womb?", if the pregnant woman has breath flowing: it is a male if on the right, a female if on the left <note>original: "virane bhage" - the side without breath</note>, and twins if the breath flows in both. || 58 ||
>
> If one leaves the house while the breath is in the Moon <note>the left nostril</note> and reaches their destination when it is in the Sun <note>the right nostril</note>, even a difficult task will be achieved without effort. || 59 ||
>
> Regarding the question of an enemy's arrival: if the wind <note>original: "matarishvani"</note> is in the left, they will not come—this is established even without saying. If it is otherwise <note>in the right</note>, they are coming. || 60 ||
>
> In a physical contest <note>term: "angayuddha" - wrestling or hand-to-hand combat without weapons</note>, if the question "Will I win or be defeated?" is asked: if the breath is in the "full" side <note>the active nostril</note>, there is victory; otherwise, there is defeat. || 61 ||

In this context, the solution is applied by dividing the subjects. For sharp or aggressive actions like war and disputes, or for general entry anywhere, the Pingala <note>the right channel</note> alone is the giver of auspiciousness. However, for performing auspicious deeds like giving charity or marriage, the Ida <note>the left channel</note> alone is beautiful/auspicious for entry. This is how it should be explained.

Furthermore, the word "and" <note>original: "ca"</note> follows a different order in the connection regarding "entry into a treaty." Those who know the truth desire the connection to be interpreted either as "in an auspicious treaty" (coordinated) or as separate categories. If interpreted separately, "auspicious" refers to deeds other than the specific auspicious acts mentioned. Thus, the specific mention of certain auspicious acts is to emphasize their importance.

The phrase "clothing, ornaments, and jewelry" <note>original: "vastralankara-bhushanam"</note> is a compound. Mentioning "ornament of the cloth" is intended to convey the extreme beauty of the garment. Thus, just as with cruel acts like war and disputes, the Moon-nerve <note>left nostril</note> is not auspicious when putting on clothes suitable for such occasions; rather, the Pingala <note>right nostril</note> is. Therefore, the separate mention of ornaments and jewelry is not a flaw in the text. Let us leave this detailed explanation here. || 53 ||

**Regarding "The Pregnant Woman" (Verse 57):** Even without a formal question, if there is a desire to know, the truth should be told based on observation. The connection is: if in the left part, the child is a girl. "Non-viable offspring" means a lifeless child.

**Regarding "In the Womb" (Verse 58):** "In the Virana" means in the side devoid of breath. "If in both" refers to when the breath exits both nostrils equally and subtly. When it is subtle, it is the Sushumna <note>the central channel</note>.

**Regarding "Leaving" (Verse 59):** It should be understood that the words "Moon" and "Sun" are indicators for the flow of breath in the left and right nostrils respectively.

**Regarding "The Enemy" (Verse 60):** "Otherwise" means in the right. "Established even without saying" implies the logic of elimination <note>original: "parishesha-nyaya"</note>.

**Regarding "Physical Contest" (Verse 61):** A physical contest is a fight done for the sake of testing skill or for amusement without enmity. The "full side" refers to the side where the breath is currently flowing.

# Prashna Marga: The Path of Inquiry

-> Page 32 <-

Preparing for battle, departing on a journey, or entering the fencing arena <note>original: "khallurika"; refers to a traditional martial arts gymnasium or arena</note> is auspicious when the breath flows through the left nostril <note>original: "ida"</note>. However, if the breath flows through the right <note>original: "pingala"</note>, one should strike the opponent; if the left side of the body is active during this, victory is certain. || 62 ||

Even if one has entered the arena while the breath was in the left nostril, if the breath continues to flow only through that same side, victory will not be achieved. In such a case, the seeker of victory should position themselves toward the East or the North within that arena. || 63 ||

If the breath <note>the vital air or Prana</note> moves into the "space" element <note>original: "akasha"; implying a suspension or specific subtle movement of breath</note>, it indicates the death of a child within the womb. If, after the question is asked, the breath moves to a location other than where the vital air should be, one should predict an "untrue progeny" <note>meaning a stillbirth or deceased fetus</note>. || 64 ||

**This concludes the section regarding the states of breath.**

If the querent <note>the person asking the question</note> touches their own chest, they will quickly obtain their heart's desire. The same applies if they touch auspicious objects. Conversely, touching inauspicious objects yields a negative result. || 65 ||

***

**Commentary:**

*Regarding "Preparing for battle":* The terms "Ida" and "Pingala" here signify specific timings or states of the breath. The "arena" <note>khallurika</note> refers to the place of practice or combat. "The other" refers to the opponent. || 62 ||

*Regarding "Even if...":* "Through this" refers to the left nostril. <gloss>The grammatical substitute "enaya" is used here for "anvadesha" (reference to something already mentioned).</gloss> Within that arena, the one desiring victory should stand in the Eastern or Northern part. The intention is that by doing so, victory may still be attained. || 63 ||

*Regarding "The breath":* This also pertains to inquiries regarding pregnancy. "After asking" means immediately following the query. "Elsewhere" means in a region devoid of the vital air. "Untrue progeny" means a dead fetus. || 64 ||

*Regarding "This concludes":* This indicates that the examination of the two states of breath—which were introduced alongside timing and other factors to be observed by a composed astrologer—is now complete. Following the established order of instruction, the auspicious or inauspicious nature of the querent's touch is now being described. Because the points to be discussed regarding the "state of breath" were limited, they are included within this breath-analysis section.

*Regarding "The querent":* This verse begins a series of fourteen verses concerning the "Signs of Touch" <term>Sparsha-lakshana: the science of interpreting what a client touches during a reading</term>. Auspicious objects include items like mirrors; inauspicious objects include items like brooms. || 65 ||

->Touching the navel, nose, mouth, hair, body hair, nails, or teeth;<-

**Regarding "Touching"** (Verse 65): "Teeth" <note>original: dvija, literally 'twice-born'</note> refers to the teeth. The "ring finger" is the fourth finger starting from the thumb. "Joints" refers to the connections of the hands and other limbs. If one asks why the "mouth" is mentioned separately when the "nine openings" <note>The nine traditional openings are the eyes, ears, nostrils, mouth, and the two lower excretory paths</note> are already included: the word "mouth" here refers to the facial area excluding the cavity itself. Alternatively, it should be understood that touching the mouth cavity carries a greater fault or impurity than touching the other eight openings. || 65, 66 ||

**Regarding "East"** (Verse 67): The "Banner and the others" refers to the eight types to be described. The group of eight directions will also be described. The "results of their positions and touching" refers to the omens resulting from where these symbols reside in the directions and where they are touched on the body. || 67 ||

**Regarding "The Banner"** (Verse 68): The Banner is in the East, the Smoke is in the Southeast, and so on in order. It should be understood that these are the same eight "wombs" <term>yonis: symbolic categories used in traditional Indian architecture and divination to determine the character of a space or person</term> well-known in the *Shilpa Shastra* <note>The traditional Hindu texts on arts, crafts, and architecture</note>. || 68 ||

**Regarding "In the head"** (Verse 69): Having assigned the "wombs" to the directions, the author now assigns them to the limbs of the body through this verse. Here, the word "head" also implies the forehead. The "mouth" includes the face, excluding the nose, ears, and the skull. The "heart" represents the entire torso below the neck, excluding the hands and feet. || 69 ||

**"Standing in the direction of the Banner" etc.:** "Standing in the direction of the Banner" means standing in the Eastern direction. The four parts of the body, starting from the head and face, correspond to the Banner, Lion, and so on. The four results are the gain of wealth and so forth. "Standing in the direction of the Lion" means standing in the Southern direction. By touching the four limbs starting from the face <note>the Lion position</note>, one receives the fourfold fruits beginning with the destruction of enemies and beasts. || 70 ||

**"One shall go" etc.:** "In the Bull" refers to the Western direction. "Acquisition of the Creator's beloved" <note>original: 'dhatridayapti'</note> refers to the acquisition of knowledge <term>Vidyalabha: the attainment of spiritual or secular learning</term>. "Standing in the Elephant" means standing in the Northern direction. Thus, through these two verses, the specific auspicious results for those standing in the four cardinal directions and touching the <term>Digyoni: the bodily points corresponding to the cardinal directions</term> are demonstrated. Following this, in the next two verses, the specific inauspicious results arising from those standing in the intermediate directions <note>corners</note> and touching the intermediate points will be shown. || 71 ||

->Chapter Two<-

Even if one is situated in the direction of Smoke <note>original: "dhūma"; the South-East</note>, if they touch the areas associated with the Smoke-dog, the Donkey, or the Crow, they may encounter death, suffering, fear, the loss of their religious vows, or the destruction of their family. If one has mounted the area of the Dog, the Donkey, or the Crow and touches the Smoke-locations, that person will face disease, the loss of a son, misfortune, and the depletion of wealth. || 72 ||

If a person is situated in the area of the Donkey <note>the North-West</note> and touches the Donkey, the Crow, the Smoke, or the Dog, they will immediately encounter disputes, the loss of cattle, great injury from weapons, and illness for their wife. Even if situated in the area of the Crow <note>the North-East</note>, if they touch the Crow, the Smoke, the Dog, or the Donkey, they will face the suffering of kinsmen, the breaking of teeth <note>original: "dvija-bhaṅga"; literally the breaking of the 'twice-born' parts of the body</note>, death at the hands of the low-born, and calamity for their children. || 73 ||

One situated in the positions of the Banner <note>East</note>, the Lion <note>South</note>, or the Elephant <note>North</note> who touches the areas named Smoke, Dog, Donkey, or Crow—or vice versa—will encounter either misfortune or prosperity, but neither will be to an extreme degree. || 74 ||

---

**Regarding "Situated in Smoke" etc. —** "Situated in Smoke" means located in the South-East corner. "Fear of suffering" means dread arising from hardships. "Mounted" refers to being in the South-West corner. "In the Donkey" refers to the North-West corner. "Loss of cattle" <term>go-hati: the destruction of livestock</term>. "Great injury from weapons" means significant pain produced by a weapon. "Situated in the Crow" means located in the North-East corner. The connection is: touching the Crow, Smoke, Dog, and Donkey locations. "Breaking of the twice-born" means the loss of teeth. "Death from the low-born" is the intended connection. "Calamity for children" means a disaster involving one's son. || 72, 73 ||

**Regarding "Banner" etc. —** The meaning is that if those in the cardinal directions (East, etc.) touch the intermediate directions, or if those in the intermediate corners touch the cardinal directions, the result is neither excessively auspicious nor excessively inauspicious. || 74 ||

It is the nature of a lion that while lying down, he bends his neck and looks behind him. Similarly, the authors of the scriptures, who are as profound as lions, while explaining matters according to the instructional order, sometimes touch upon a previously explained subject again; this is indeed an ornament of the work, not a defect. If even this is not acceptable, then let this verse be read immediately after the verses beginning with "Eating at the moment of inquiry..." which concern the states within the explanation of breath. We have no stubborn insistence on this matter. || 75 ||

A "corrupt Brahmin" is indicated by those who have lost their priestly status or do not wear the sacred thread. The Moon or Venus—one of them. The Moon, Sun, and Mercury joined together. Venus...

->If Jupiter and Venus are placed in the first, fifth, or eighth houses, there is an association with Brahmins and learned men.<-
->If they are joined or aspected <note>aspected: in astrology, when one planet 'looks' at another from a specific distance, influencing its power</note> by malefic planets,<-

And here is the **Madhaviya** <note>A celebrated 14th-century astrological treatise by Madhavacharya</note> on the same:

->If the Sun is in the eighth house on a Sunday, there was surely trouble<-
->caused by a great multitude of people or by the King’s army.<-
->If the Sun is in a division of Jupiter, one should say it was by the King;<-

"Alone" means without any connection to malefic planets. It should be understood that if the Moon is alone, the specific distinction between "wicked women" and "noble women" does not apply. The same applies to Venus when joined by malefics. "With those of that nature" means with people of the same class as the planets that are aspecting or joined with the primary planet. The word "arrived" <note>original: "agata"</note>, though a past participle, is used figuratively as an adjective for the "direction." The description mentioned in the second half of the verse is from the *Sara-sangraha*. || 80 ||

**Regarding this** || The teachings from the *Prashna-Madhaviya* are stated here in seventeen verses, beginning with "If the Sun is in the eighth..." and ending with "Thus one should predict."

**The Sun** || "In a division of Jupiter" means if the Sun, situated in the eighth house, occupies a zodiacal division <note>original: "amsha"; a sub-division of a sign used for fine-tuning predictions</note> ruled by Jupiter, the trouble is caused by the King himself. <term>Destruction of minerals, etc.</term> <note>original: "dhatvadi-vastu-vihati"</note>: if the Sun in the eighth is in a <term>mineral division</term>, there is loss of metallic goods; if in a <term>root division</term>, loss of crops or botanical wealth; if in a <term>living-being division</term>, loss of livestock or servants. "In the past" applies to all these instances. || 81 ||

->In a reptile-division, it is a bite from such a creature;<-

->When the son of the Moon <note>Mercury</note> is in the eighth house, there is a failure of the desired work.<-
->In a vegetable-division, there is the loss of betel nut and leaf <note>Puga-tambula: a traditional sign of hospitality and social grace</note> during the rise of the house. || 85 ||<-

->In a mineral-division, a weariness of the body occurs; however, in an animal-division,<-
->there is harshness of speech or a lack of lime <note>used in the betel preparation</note> on the day of Mercury <note>Wednesday</note> that has just passed. || 86 ||<-

---

**Regarding "When the Moon is in the eighth..." :** The distinction is that if the Moon is strong, the person drank gruel; if the Moon is weak, they went entirely without food.

**Regarding "If Mars is in the eighth..." :** "Fall from position" means a slip from one's status or rank. Alternatively, it can mean a physical fall caused by a slip of the foot. "Mars" <note>original: "Ara"</note> here refers to the planet. "Injury" <note>original: "Kshati"</note> refers to a wound. The four lines beginning with "In a mineral-division" explain the specific causes of the wound. Scorpio, Pisces, and Cancer are the "reptile" <note>creeping</note> signs. A "division of those" refers to a bite from a snake, scorpion, or similar. The phrase "of Mars" <note>original: "Arasya"</note> is the correct grammatical break.

**Regarding "When the son of the Moon..." :** "Failure" <note>original: "Bhanga"</note> means an obstacle that blocks progress. There is an absence of both the betel nut and the leaf. The word "again" <note>original: "punah"</note> is used in the sense of "but." "Harshness of speech" implies an occasion where one utters harsh words. "Lime" <note>original: "Churna"</note> refers to the powder used for chewing betel. || 85, 86 ||

# Path of Inquiry
<note>original: "Prashnamarga"</note>

> If the person asking the question faces the southern direction, or if they are standing in the quarter of Yama <note>the god of death, associated with the South</note>, it will surely lead to an inauspicious result, especially in inquiries regarding longevity. || 102 ||

This refers to two distinct subjects.

> Words that begin with the elements of Ether, Air, Fire, or Earth, or those that refer to the past tense, do not bestow a favorable outcome. || 103 ||

Here follows the *Compendium of Inquiry* <note>original: "Prashnasangraha"</note>.

> The script is divided into two parts: the initial vowels and the consonant groups starting with 'Ka'. The vowels are to be known as the Life-force <note>Jiva</note> and the consonant groups as the Body <note>Tanu</note>; such is the nature of the Mother-alphabet <note>Matrika</note>. || 104 ||
> If the sentence of the inquiry begins with a vowel, it should be known as pertaining to the Life-force and is auspicious. In that case, any affliction relates to the body. If it begins with a consonant, the opposite is true. || 105 ||
> Within the consonant groups, the five letters represent Air, Fire, Indra <note>Earth</note>, Water, and the Neuter <note>Eunuch/Void</note>. In the beginning of a sentence, a neuter letter is extremely unfavorable for those asking. Air and Fire are corrupt; Indra is middling; Water is excellent. Based on the division of long and short, the groups of vowels are of the nature of Water and Indra respectively.

Regarding "This": This refers to the two preceding verses.

Regarding "Ether etc.": The classification of letters and groups into the five elements like Ether will be explained further. The past tense forms <note>original: "la-du-lu-li-to", referring to Sanskrit grammatical suffixes for the past tense</note> signify things already gone. || 103 ||

Regarding "Here": The book called *Compendium of Inquiry* was composed by the same author as the *Path of Inquiry*. The following three verses are from that work.

Regarding "Initial": Starting with the letter 'A'. The term "groups" <note>varga</note> also implies the semi-vowels and sibilants—essentially all consonants. The vowels are like water. The "Mother-alphabet" is the row of letters. "Pertaining to Life-force" concerns the lifespan. "Affliction relating to the body" refers to the increase of disease or the duration of illness. If the inquiry sentence begins with a consonant, then the opposite occurs: it signifies a defect in longevity rather than just a long illness. Within the groups (Ka, Cha, Ta, Ta, Pa), the five letters in each are respectively named Air, Fire, Indra, Water, and Neuter. The word "Neuter" <note>napumsaka</note> here refers to the fifth letter in all five groups. Air and Fire are the first and second letters. "Middling" means neither very auspicious nor very harmful. Among vowels, the short ones are named Indra <note>Earth</note> and the long ones are named Water. || 104-106 ||

### Here begins the Method of Practice.

->Where the heavy syllables fall in the middle, end, beginning, or in all positions,<-
->the classes are known as Ja, Sa, Bha, and Ma.<-
->Their presiding deities are the Sun, Wind, Moon, and Earth;<-
->they bring, in order: great disease, departure to another land,<-
->renowned fame, and prosperity.<-
->Similarly, where the light syllables fall in those positions,<-
->the classes are Ra, Ta, Ya, and Na.<-
->Their deities are Fire, Sky, Water, and Heaven;<-

->and long life. Thus it is said. || 107 ||<-

->If the speaker utters words pleasing to the ear, or auspicious words,<-
->or speaks with meaningful and fluent speech at that moment,<-
->then the seeker shall attain their desired goal. Otherwise, it is unfavorable;<-
->especially if the speaker ends their speech with a breathy aspiration <note>original: "visarga"</note>. || 108 ||<-

->By taking the first syllable of the seeker's sentence as the Ascendant <term>Lagna: the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon</term>,<-
->all good and bad results should be foretold. That method is now explained. || 109 ||<-

---

**Regarding "In the middle" etc.** A "class" <note>original: "gana," a metrical foot</note> consists of three syllables. In the middle, end, beginning, or in all positions respectively: "Ga" stands for heavy syllables <note>original: "guru"</note>, and "Ja-Sa-Bha-Ma" refer to the Ja-class, Sa-class, Bha-class, and Ma-class. The Ja-class has a heavy syllable in the middle, and so on. "Deities" refers to the presiding spirits of these metrical classes. "Great disease" and the following are the results of these four classes in order. Similarly, when light syllables <note>original: "laghu"</note> are in the middle, end, beginning, or all positions, they are the Ra-class, Ta-class, Ya-class, and Na-class. The Ra-class has a light syllable in the middle, and so on. "Immortals" refers to their deities. "Death" and the following are the results of these four in order. The division of syllables into heavy and light is well-known and therefore not explained here. || 107 ||

**Regarding "Pleasing to the ear."** "Pleasing to the ear" means providing satisfaction to the listener just by hearing it. "Auspicious" means containing words of good omen. "Fluent" means spoken without pausing in the middle or without facial distortions such as squinting the eyes. "Attains the desired" means they obtain what they wished for. || 108 ||

**Regarding "Of the seeker."** "By the first syllable of the sentence" refers to the very first letter that comes out of the seeker's mouth. "By that Ascendant" refers to using that specific sign to tell good or bad fortune. Here, the "A-group" refers to the vowels in general. The "Ya-group" refers to the semi-vowels and sibilants. Therefore, by taking the numerical value of the letter—meaning, by imagining the zodiac sign ruled by the lord of that first letter as the Ascendant. Of Mars and the other five... <note>The text cuts off as it begins to explain the planetary rulership of specific letters.</note>

### Here begin the seventy verses in the Arya meter.

-> The consonant groups starting with A, Ka, Ca, Ta, Ta, Pa, and Ya <-
-> are assigned to the Sun, Mars, Venus, Mercury, Jupiter, and Saturn. <-
-> The Moon is also specified; <-
-> one should note the first syllable uttered at the time of the inquiry. || 110 || <note>This refers to the 'Akathaha' chakra, a system where Sanskrit letters are mapped to planets to find hidden meanings in speech.</note>

-> Having identified the Ascendant from that syllable, <-
-> the gentle astrologer should gather the auspicious and inauspicious effects and speak. <-
-> Through the first, middle, and final letters of the consonant groups, <-
-> the odd-numbered signs are determined. || 111 ||

-> One should declare the zodiac sign and Ascendant; <-
-> for Mars, Mercury, and Jupiter, the even signs are found through the even-numbered letters. <-
-> This does not apply to Venus and Saturn in the same way, <-
-> nor to the Sun and Moon, as they rule only a single sign each. || 112 || <note>The Sun rules Leo and the Moon rules Cancer; unlike other planets, they do not have a pair of signs to choose between.</note>

-> From that derived Ascendant, one should predict <-
-> all good and bad fortune at the time of the query. <-
-> Because the exact time is often difficult to know, <-
-> this method should be deeply considered in many types of inquiries. || 113 ||

### This concludes the section on the syllables of the inquiry.

---

Since each planet <insert>referring to Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, and Saturn</insert> rules two zodiac signs, the following logic applies: within the five consonant groups starting with 'Ka', the first, third, and fifth letters <note>odd-numbered letters</note> indicate an odd-numbered zodiac sign. The second and fourth letters <note>even-numbered letters</note> indicate an even-numbered zodiac sign, which should be adopted as the Ascendant. However, for the Sun and the Moon, this division is not necessary because they each rule only one sign. The term "Time" <note>original: 'Kala'</note> also implies the physical position or state of the querent. Because the exact moment is "difficult to know" <note>original: 'avijnanat'</note>, the good and bad results obtained through these syllables must be "deeply considered"—meaning they must be investigated thoroughly. Alternatively, "many inquiries" <note>original: 'bahu-prashne'</note> can be read as a single compound, referring to a situation where many people are asking questions simultaneously, or when one person asks many questions at once. || 109-113 ||

**Regarding "This"** <note>original: 'Etad'</note> **:** This refers to everything stated from the beginning of the section on the "Ether" element until now.

# Chapter Two

If the messenger places their left foot forward first, it is considered auspicious; however, placing the right foot forward leads to misfortune. Similarly, the trembling of their feet brings ill fortune, while a firm and steady stance grants success. || 114 ||

If the messenger is seated comfortably and upright in a high place or on a good seat, facing the <term>astrologer</term><note>original: "daivajña" - one who knows the divine will through the stars</note>, it leads to a good result; otherwise, the outcome is unfavorable. || 115 ||

If the messenger stands up from their seat while asking the question, or if they were standing and then sit down while asking, both actions are considered auspicious. || 116 ||

If the questioner, upon coming into the astrologer's line of sight, stops repeatedly while approaching, the completion of the task will be delayed by as many days as there were stops. || 117 ||

If someone passes between the messenger and the astrologer during the consultation, it indicates that the expected help or ally for this task will not arrive. || 118 ||

This concludes the topic.

---

**Regarding "The left foot" etc. ||** "Forward" means ahead of the right foot. If the right foot is placed ahead of the left, it leads to misfortune. This refers to the movement of the feet. || 114 ||

**Regarding "Comfortably" etc. ||** The "questioner" is the subject here. A "high place" refers to an elevated area such as a pedestal or chair. "Otherwise" implies sitting uncomfortably or in a low position. || 115 ||

**Regarding "Standing up" etc. ||** The present tense is intended here; it means if one stands up *while* in the act of asking the question. || 116 ||

**Regarding "The questioner" etc. ||** "Line of sight" refers to that of the astrologer. "Approached" <note>original: "āgamat" - a specific grammatical form of the verb to come</note> refers to the movement toward the expert. "Of this" refers to the matter thought of by the questioner. || 117 ||

**Regarding "Between" etc. ||** "Between the messenger and oneself" means in the space between the questioner and the astrologer. "Passes" implies this happens at the time of the inquiry. "Non-arrival" means the failure to obtain help for the questioner. || 118 ||

**Regarding "This" etc. ||** This refers to the five verses just stated.

**Regarding "With eyes wide open":** The word *ambaka* means eye. "Opposite" refers to the manner of looking and the act of seeing. It follows that one who does not have their eyes open or who looks at inauspicious objects attains sorrow. // 126 //

**Regarding "Wet":** The phrase "wet with water" refers to the subject of clothing. "Red flowers" and so on refers to the category of objects carried. "White" describes the garment. "Fragrant and pale" describes the flowers and other items. "Attains an auspicious result" means they obtain their desired object. Auspicious materials include gold and similar items. Inauspicious materials include axes and the like. // 127, 128 //

**Regarding "This":** This refers to what was stated in the preceding two verses. //

**Regarding "The time of query":** These two verses explain the method for declaring the results. "Superiority" or "excess" is determined by both number and the weight of importance. Even if the signs are equal, one should assume the faults are more powerful. As stated in the *Madhaviya* <note>A classical Sanskrit treatise on astrology</note>: "When there is equality, the faults are indeed stronger." The reason for this is the "unfortunate nature" <term>Mandabhagyatva: the lack of spiritual merit</term> of people in the *Kali Yuga* <note>The current dark age in Hindu cosmology</note>. The word "indeed" clarifies this very point. // 129, 130 //

## Chapter Two

These matters concern the messenger. Now, the auspicious and inauspicious omens arising at the time of the inquiry shall be discussed.

> Whatever is spoken, whatever is heard, and whatever is seen at the time of a query;
> All of that should be interpreted as auspicious or inauspicious for the inquirer based on its similarity to the matter at hand. || 131 ||

This is further clarified:

> In an inquiry regarding any task, or even at the time of setting out,
> If an object that serves as a means to accomplish that task is seen, then that task will be successful. || 132 ||

> Seeing new clothes, garlands, and similar items during an inquiry about marriage <note>original: "karasangraha" - literally 'taking the hand'</note>
> Leads to success. The separation of any two things, however, indicates the failure of that goal. || 133 ||

> If one is seen inserting a finger into a hole, one should predict a blemish or scandal regarding the maiden.
> From whichever direction someone happens to arrive, it should be said that the marriage will come from that direction. || 134 ||

> Items such as a chalk-tablet <note>original: "ghutika"</note>, a book, or anything used for practicing knowledge;
> Or ornaments for a child, such as small bells or bracelets; || 135 ||

Regarding "These": These refer to signs arising at that moment. Others also specify these as "immediate occurrences."

Regarding "In an inquiry": "Based on its similarity" refers to the correspondence with these three (what is said, heard, or seen). || 131 ||

Regarding "This [is clarified]": This means it is explained through the examples shown in the verse beginning with "In an inquiry regarding any..."

Regarding "In an inquiry": "At the time of setting out" means at the start of a journey. "A means to accomplish that task" refers to something that facilitates the specific goal being asked about or intended. || 132 ||

Regarding "New [clothes]": The word "and similar" <note>original: "adi"</note> indicates other items suitable for a wedding, such as a mirror. "Of any two things": Some accept a reading here as "of those two," meaning the two garments; they say that if the cloth is torn, the marriage will not succeed. However, because a narrow interpretation is less desirable than a broad one, and because the previous verse used the word "and similar," the reading "of any two things" is superior. Since these are illustrative examples, a specific focus is not a flaw. These verses clarify the general principle stated in the previous verse by providing specific instances. || 133 ||

Regarding "In a hole": This specifically concerns an inquiry about marriage. "From whichever direction": This implies a consideration of the person's caste and other characteristics. || 134 ||

Regarding "Chalk-tablet": This concerns an inquiry about progeny and is useful in questions regarding pregnancy. || 135, 136 ||

# Chapter Two

> The flower of the ancestors <note>original: "pitṛpuṣpam"; likely referring to the Karavira or other flowers used in funeral rites</note>, sesame seeds, fire, new cloth, as well as sacrificial grass <term>darbha: a sacred grass used in Vedic rituals</term>, yogurt, and all other items gathered for the rites of the ancestors. || 145 ||
> All these substances required immediately following a death—the sight of these during an inquiry regarding longevity surely foretells death. || 146 ||
> If the inquirer is lying down or sitting while asking, it indicates an obstacle to their journey. Shifting one's weight from foot to foot or withdrawing a foot will certainly cause a delay. || 147 ||
> Standing up from a seat or moving toward a vehicle indicates the journey will be gained quickly. || 148 ||
> The clasping of hands with one another, or the arrival of someone else, or the breaking or splitting of joints—all these indicate opposition to a successful union or agreement. || 149 ||
> The sound of "Alas!" or cries of grief, sneezing, the falling
> ->of a sacred tree or a flagpole,<-
> ->the destruction of clothing, umbrellas, or footwear,<-
> ->various words signifying ruin,<-
> ->the cries of cruel animals and birds in every direction,<-
> ->the extinguishing of a lamp,<-
> ->and the falling of a full water-pot—the wise know<-
> ->these to be omens of distress. || 150 ||<-

**Regarding "The flower of the ancestors"** !! The "rites of the ancestors" <note>original: "pitṛkarma"</note> refers to the entire cycle of ceremonies from the initial funeral rites to the final sapindikarana <note>the ritual reception of the deceased into the community of ancestors</note>, including the various Shraddha offerings and the pouring of sesame seeds into the fire for the satisfaction of the departed. The substances required immediately after death include sacrificial grass, fuel-sticks, yogurt, and clarified butter. The phrase "gathered for the rites of the ancestors" serves as a qualifying description for all these items. || 145, 146 ||

**Regarding "Lying down"** !! This refers specifically to an inquiry regarding a journey. "Obstacle" means a hindrance. "Shifting weight" <note>original: "pādavyāsa"</note> refers to standing on one foot and then shifting to the other after asking the question. "Withdrawing" refers to pulling back a foot that was previously extended. The phrase "journey will be gained quickly" connects to the positive movements described. || 147, 148 ||

**Regarding "Clasping hands"** !! "Arrival" means someone coming toward the place where the inquiry is being made. The mention of "joints" <note>original: "sandhye"</note> connects to the previous verse. This section refers to inquiries regarding business or specific tasks. || 149 ||

**Regarding "Alas!"** !! Having shown examples to be observed in specific inquiries, the author now shows through this and following verses the signs to be observed in general inquiries. A "sacred tree" <note>original: "caitya"</note> is a tree that is worshipped. "Destruction" <note>original: "vikṣuti"</note> refers to ruin or falling. "Words signifying ruin" are various utterances whose primary meaning is destruction. || 150 ||

# Prashna Marga
<page-num>52</page-num>

->The sight of a cat, a water-snake, an owl, or an iguana is inauspicious.<-
->The chirping of a lizard on the left, and a sneeze on the right, lead to destruction. || 151 ||<-

->The mention of the names of the boar, iguana, rabbit, and mongoose is auspicious.<-
->However, their sight or their cries are not. For the monkey and the bear, it is the opposite. || 152 ||<-

->If, at the time of a query, one hears the sound of elephants, horses, or bulls,<-
->or if one sees them, then the querent shall obtain their desired object. || 153 ||<-

->The wise should know the following as auspicious omens:<-
->The sound of the lute, flute, drum, conch, and kettle-drum;<-
->The sound of the war-drum, singing, auspicious objects, and a beautiful woman;<-
->A courtesan, curd, unbroken rice, and sugarcane;<-
->Durva grass, sandalwood, a full water-pot, and flowers;<-
->Garlands, fruit, a maiden,<-
->A bell, a lamp, and lotuses. || 154 ||<-

**Regarding the cat, etc.** || "On the left" refers to the previous statement <note>regarding the lizard's chirp</note>. "On the right" is connected specifically to the sneeze. || 151 ||

**Regarding the auspiciousness, etc.** || Mentioning the names of the boar and others is auspicious. Hearing their sounds or seeing them is inauspicious. For the monkey and the bear, seeing them or hearing their sounds is auspicious, but merely mentioning their names is inauspicious. || 152 ||

**Regarding the elephant, etc.** || The implication is that for elephants and similar animals, there is no specific distinction regarding whether mentioning their names is particularly auspicious or inauspicious <note>unlike the specific animals mentioned in verse 152</note>. || 153 ||

**Regarding the lute, etc.** || "Auspicious objects" refers to items used in rituals. The word *Anjana* <note>original: "अञ्जना"</note> refers to a woman endowed with auspicious qualities, based on the grammatical rule "Anjat in the sense of welfare." This "welfare" implies both natural beauty and being adorned with ornaments. One should recognize these as auspicious omens. This means that both seeing and hearing these things brings good fortune. || 154 ||

### Now begins the Third Chapter

Now, the things to be observed at the time of departure <note>The moment the astrologer leaves his home to visit the client</note> are described.

> Having understood the good or bad timing arising at the moment of inquiry, one should depart at an auspicious time, such as during a favorable *Jiva-Kala-Hora* <note>A specific astrological hour or division of the day associated with the 'life-force'</note> and so on. || 1 ||

> Whatever auspicious or inauspicious omens <term>Nimitta: signs or portents observed in the environment</term> arose at the time of the inquiry, all of those must also be carefully considered during the departure. || 2 ||

This applies to matters such as longevity or marriage. For instance, in a question about longevity, seeing a funeral procession would be a sign of destruction (death); in a question about a traveler's return, hearing that someone is leaving that distant place but not coming here would be a negative sign. Conversely, hearing of a child's birth or news of a disease being cured during a longevity inquiry would be positive signs. || 156 ||

**Having understood...** || This refers to what has been demonstrated. By "thoroughly understanding," it means that through these factors like timing, auspicious results come from auspicious signs and inauspicious results from inauspicious ones. The word "alone" <note>original: "eva"</note> suggests that this can be determined even without the *Arudha* <note>The sign rising at the time of the query or the direction the client faces</note> or other advanced placements to be discussed later. || 157 ||

**This...** || In the sequence of determining results—starting from the inquiry, the departure, the path, and the arrival at the house—everything to be observed at the time of the inquiry has been shown in this chapter according to the sequence of timing and other factors. The intent is that departure and subsequent stages will be described sequentially starting from the third chapter.

->|| Thus ends the Second Chapter ||<-

**Inquiry...** || By the word "and so on" <note>original: "adi"</note> following "timing," factors like the location mentioned in the verse beginning with "By the astrologer..." are included. "One should depart" means moving from one's own house toward the house of the querent. Regarding the *Kala-Hora* <note>The planetary hour</note>: "The *Kala-Hora* is considered the twelfth part of the day. Its first lord is the lord of the weekday. Then, the lords of the subsequent hours are the lords of every sixth weekday in sequence. For the night, they start from the fifth lord from the weekday lord." This is how it should be understood. || 1 ||

**Auspicious...** || Instruments like the *Veena* <note>lute</note>, flute, or drums are auspicious omens. Cries of "Alas!" or sounds of grief are inauspicious omens. The particle "indeed" <note>original: "hi"</note> highlights that this is both logically sound and well-known in tradition. || 2 ||

# Chapter Three

->Page 55<-

If, while one is departing, their garment gets caught on something or if it falls to the ground, or if the handle of the parasol <note>The parasol or umbrella was a traditional symbol of status and protection during travel</note> held in their hand should break, it will surely lead to misfortune. || 3 ||

"Come here," "Stay," "Do not go," "Enter," or "Where are you going?"—such words spoken at the time of departure are firmly established as givers of ill fortune. || 4 ||

Stumbling with the feet against stones and the like, or striking the head against a pillar or similar object, is not desired during departure. Other such occurrences well-known among the common people should also be considered <note>The author acknowledges that folk wisdom and local traditions regarding bad luck are as valid as formal theory</note>. || 5 ||

This concludes the section on the moment of departure. Now, the things to be considered while on the road are being stated. On this point, there is another <term>Shastra</term> <note>A technical or scientific treatise</note>:

Whether it be good or whether it be evil, the fruit of actions performed in a previous life is revealed by omens to those who are traveling. || 6 ||

Regarding the arising of good or bad omens, there is indeed a distinction in the results experienced based on the different types of travelers. This has also been explained in other technical treatises according to the differences in the path and other factors. || 7 ||

One should consider the omen in relation to: oneself on the path; the King within the army; and the Deity <note>Referring to the consecrated image of a god</note> within the city...

**Commentary:**

Regarding the verse "If, while one is departing": "Caught" means getting snagged anywhere. By the use of the word "and the like," items such as walking sticks are included. || 3 ||

Regarding "Come here": Such words, whether addressed to an astrologer <note>original: "Daivajña"</note> or anyone else, are sentences that act as obstacles to a journey. || 4 ||

Regarding "Stones": The word "stumbling" is applied here as well <note>meaning stumbling against stones or striking the head</note>. || 5 ||

Regarding "This": This refers to what was said in the previous five verses. The upcoming section, starting from "performed in a previous life" and ending with "while going," consists of twenty-four verses.

Regarding "Another": "Of that" refers to one's past karma. "Reveals" means it makes it known by acting as an indicator. || 6 ||

Regarding "Good": The word "omen" <note>original: "Shakuna"</note> here also implies other types of signs or portents. There is a "distinction" or specific difference for the "doer" who experiences the result. || 7 ||

Regarding "On the path": "On the path, oneself" refers to the subject of traveling alone. "The King within the army" refers to signs seen when the army is encamped or omens seen during a military expedition. "In relation to the Deity" refers to signs affecting all the inhabitants of a city...

# Part One

->In a traveling group, the leader is the one who is superior<-
->in caste, knowledge, or age. So it is said. || 8 ||<-

->The results of omens also pertain to the past, future, and present.<-
->This should be understood from the direction of their occurrence, as stated in other scriptures. || 9 ||<-

->Starting from sunrise, the sun moves through the eight directions,<-
->beginning with the East, for seven and a half <term>nadis</term> <note>A nadi is a unit of time equal to 24 minutes; 7.5 nadis equal 3 hours</note> each, throughout the day and night. || 10 ||<-

->The results in the directions where the sun has passed, is present, or is approaching are determined accordingly.<-
->These are called "Charcoal," "Blazing," and "Smoking"; the others are "Calm." || 11 ||<-

->The results for the fifth direction from those should be declared as equal across the three periods of time.<-
->For the remaining directions, good or bad results should be spoken of according to their proximity. || 12 ||<-

->This method should be adopted everywhere for the knowledge of the past, future, and present.<-

***

The experience of those results is indicated here. Regarding the phrase *In a traveling group, the leader*: this should be considered when many people are traveling together in a company. Leadership is determined by <term>jati</term> <note>caste or birth-group</note>, <term>vidya</term> <note>knowledge or education</note>, and age. There are two views seen regarding their priority: that they are significant in the order listed, or in the reverse order. By the phrase *in the case of equality*, it is understood that if leadership or lack thereof is decided by some other reason, then caste and the rest are not the determining factors. || 8 ||

**Regarding Omens...** With the two verses starting with *Starting from...*, the author displays the teachings of other scientific treatises (<term>shastras</term>). || 9 ||

**Starting from...** Starting from sunrise, the sun's movement is in the East for seven and a half *nadis*. Then, for another seven and a half *nadis*, it is in the Southeast. One should calculate the sequence in this manner. Thus, from sunrise until the first seven and a half *nadis* have passed, the Northeast is the direction the sun has "left," the East is where the sun is "present," and the Southeast is where the sun is "approaching." This should be observed for the subsequent periods as well. Among those, the direction the sun has left gives results for the **past** (<term>bhuta</term>). The direction where the sun is present gives results for the **present** (<term>vartamana</term>). The direction the sun is approaching gives results for the **future** (<term>bhavishya</term>).

These directions—left, present, and approaching—are respectively named **Charcoal**, **Blazing**, and **Smoking**. "Charcoal" (<term>angara</term>) is so called because it is "burnt" by the previous contact with the sun. "Blazing" (<term>dipta</term>) is due to the current intense light. "Smoking" (<term>dhumini</term>) is due to the imminent burning. The other five directions are named **Calm** (<term>shanta</term>) because of the absence of solar contact. One should declare the results for the three periods of time as equal for the fifth direction from these. This means that just as in the East, one should predict the past, etc., in the West; as in the Southeast, so in the Northwest, and so on. For the remaining directions—specifically the third and seventh directions from the "Blazing" one—one should judge by proximity. The first half of the third direction gives results like the second; the second half gives results for the past like the fourth. In the first half of the seventh direction, it gives future results like the sixth; in the second half, it again gives past results like the eighth. This should be considered carefully. This terminology is also useful in sections such as "The cries of the directions."

**This...** This introduction is intended for universal application in the science of determining time.

# Chapter Three
Page 57

The King, the Prince, the Leader, the Messenger, the Merchant, the Spy, the Brahmin, and the Superintendent of Elephants—these correspond to the East and the other directions. The members of the four castes, starting with the Warrior <note>Kshatriya</note>, also correspond to the four cardinal directions. || 13 ||

Whether one is moving or standing still, in whichever direction the bird makes its cry, a meeting with a person associated with that specific direction should be predicted. || 14 ||

The meaning of this is:
->If the bird cries in the East,<-
->there will be a meeting with a King.<-
->In the South-East, with a Prince;<-
->and in the South and others, with the Leader and so on. || 15 ||<-

For those belonging to heretical sects, religious orders, or castes, a person of the same class signifies the success of the task. Conversely, if they are of a different class, they act as messengers of failure for the task. || 16 ||

Now, the arrival of those to be mentioned hereafter on the path should be understood.

***

**Regarding "The King" etc. ||** The group of eight beginning with the King is assigned to the eight directions starting with the East <note>Indra's direction</note>. The group of four beginning with the Warrior caste is assigned to the four cardinal directions starting with the East. Thus, it is understood that two figures are assigned to the cardinal directions and one to each intermediate direction. The connection is this: in whichever direction the bird is situated and cries, a meeting with the person belonging to that direction is to be predicted. This determination is not only for when one is on a journey, but also applies to inquiries <note>divination queries</note>, as indicated by the word "standing."

**Regarding "The meaning" ||** "Is being told" is the implied completion of the sentence. That is to say, by the verse that follows.

**Regarding "In the East" ||** With a King, meaning a sovereign. This also includes any member of the Warrior caste. The "Leader" refers to a commander of an army. The Merchant <note>Vaishya</note> is also implied here, because it was stated that "the Warrior and others belong to the four directions." || 15 ||

**Regarding "Heretical sects" ||** Heretics <note>Pashanda</note> are those who wear sectarian marks, such as the Buddhists <note>Shakyas</note> and others. The religious orders <note>Ashramas</note> are those of the student <note>Brahmacharya</note> and so on. The castes <note>Varnas</note> are the Brahmins and so on. "Of the same class" means similar to the seeker: a Buddhist for a Buddhist, a student for a student, a Brahmin for a Brahmin—this is how it should be seen. "Conversely" means, for example, a monk appearing for a Buddhist, or a Buddhist for a monk; a householder for a student, or a student for a householder; or a Warrior for a Brahmin, and a Brahmin for a Warrior. This matter regarding messengers is mentioned here in the section on path-omens because it is relevant to the context. || 16 ||

**Regarding "Now" ||** "Arrival" means coming towards or being brought in front of the person; this meaning is also attached.

# Prashnamarga
## Page 60

->Starting half a watch <note>A watch or 'Yama' is approximately 3 hours</note> before sunrise, the sun's heat <note>literally: 'the hot-rayed one'</note> always wanders through the eight directions during the eight watches of the day. (26)<-

->The positions are established clockwise as: Flame, Smoke, Shadow, Mud, Water, Earth, Ashes, and Burning Coal. (27)<-

->The three starting with Burning Coal <note>Coal, Flame, and Smoke</note> are considered 'Blazing' <note>term: Deeptam - intense or unfavorable</note>; the three starting with Mud <note>Mud, Water, and Earth</note> are 'Quiescent' <note>term: Shantam - peaceful or favorable</note>. The first half of the Shadow is auspicious, and the latter half of the Ashes is likewise auspicious. (28)<-

The actions to be taken if a bad omen <note>term: Shakuna - an omen, often based on bird flights or environmental sounds</note> occurs are also stated in other scriptures:

->If an unfavorable omen occurs, perform eleven breath-regulations <note>term: Pranayama</note>; if a second occurs, sixteen; if a third occurs, one should not proceed at all. (29)<-

This refers to the journey. Now, the things to be observed at the time of entering the house of the person asking the question <note>the querent</note> are stated.

---

**Regarding "Starting half a watch..."**: The connection is that the sun's heat wanders through the eight directions during the eight watches, beginning half a watch before sunrise. A watch consists of seven and a half *nadikas* <note>a unit of 24 minutes; thus 3 hours</note>. In the tenth verse, the sun's movement was described as starting from sunrise in each direction beginning with the East. Here, the specific difference is that it begins half a watch *before* sunrise. Starting from the direction where the sun is moving, the names are: 1. Flame, 2. Smoke, 3. Shadow, 4. Mud, 5. Water, 6. Earth, 7. Ashes, and 8. Burning Coal. Among these, Coal, Flame, and Smoke are "Blazing." Mud, Water, and Earth are "Quiescent." Regarding the others: the first part of the Shadow and the latter part of the Ashes are to be known as pure/auspicious. The latter part of the Shadow and the first part of the Ashes are inauspicious. 

Here, the assignment of auspiciousness to the half of the Shadow near the "Blazing" zone and the latter half of the Ashes near the "Blazing" zone might seem contrary to direct logic; however, it must be accepted because it is the scriptural injunction. In matters established by scriptural word, logic is of little consequence; otherwise, the authority of the scripture would be broken. In reality, these three verses are not found in the most authoritative manuscripts. Because the previous section ended with a concluding mark, it is clear that the subject matter from that other scripture was finished. Therefore, this is an interpolation <note>a later addition not by the original author</note>. Let us not dwell on it further. || 25-28 ||

**Regarding "Eleven..."**: If one sees a bad omen upon first departing, they should return to their own house, wash their feet, perform ceremonial sipping of water <note>term: Achamana</note>, and practice eleven breath-regulations as an atonement before setting out again. If a bad omen is seen again at that time, one should perform sixteen breath-regulations as before and set out again. If a bad omen is seen yet again, one should simply not go. The concluding mark indicates the end of the quotes from other scriptures and the observations regarding the journey. || 29 ||

# Chapter Three

->Whatever omens occur at the time of the query, or at the time of departure,<-
->or upon reaching the house of the querent, all those should generally be considered. (30)<-
->If, as the astrologer enters the house of the sick person,<-
->someone else exits through that same door, the patient may die.<-
->But if someone else enters through that same door at that moment,<-
->then the patient will surely live; so I have been instructed by my teacher. (31)<-
->When the astrologer arrives near the house of the querent to examine the query,<-

->but she is menstruating <note>original: "rajasvala"</note>, she signifies the total destruction of the family. (32)<-
->The sound of Vedic chanting, as well as the sound of "Auspicious Day" <note>original: "punyaha," a blessing recited by Brahmins</note> declarations,<-
->a fragrant scent, and a pleasant, clockwise breeze; (33)<-
->the lowing of a bull moving toward the house, and similarly of a cow;<-
->if these occur at the time of the astrologer's entry, they bring health and other benefits to the querent. (34)<-
