---

**Regarding the query...** This is an extension of previous rules. The word "generally" <note>original: "prayena"</note> indicates that the prediction should be made only after properly combining and weighing these factors. (30)

**The house of the sick...** This indicates that the timing must be simultaneous. "From here" means from the house of the patient. "Through this door" refers to the same door through which the astrologer enters. "Someone" implies anyone at all, without specific distinction. "So I have been instructed by my teacher" means this point, received through the lineage of teachers, should be considered with primary importance. (31)

**Near the house...** "From there" means from the querent's house. "While the astrologer is considering the query." "Destruction of the roots" <note>original: "unmula-vinashini"</note> indicates the destruction of all prosperity, including the lineage of the questioner. It is suspected that this verse might not be universally applicable and could be an interpolation <note>original: "prakshipta," a later addition to the text</note>. (32)

**Veda...** "Moving toward" means going in the direction of the querent's house. Hearing the words "Auspicious Day" and so on, smelling a fragrant scent, and feeling the touch of a pleasant wind at the moment the astrologer enters the house indicates the recovery of the querent's health. (33, 34)

**Beds...** "Upright" means with their legs or supports facing upward in their natural position. "Upside down" <note>original: "nyubja"</note> means facing downward or overturned. (35)

# Chapter Four

->Having observed the omens,<-
->one should begin the procedure of inquiry with devotion to the teacher. || 2 ||<-

When the time is not too close to midday or the rising of the sun, the act of inquiry should be performed while the sun is clear and bright. || 3 ||

Regarding the preparation of the materials for the inquiry ritual, the bringing forth of the lamp for the person in distress <note>The "person in distress" refers to the client or querent seeking answers.</note> is a bringer of good fortune. || 4 ||

In all inquiries, and especially in all ritual acts, one should predict the future auspiciousness based solely on the clarity of the lamp. || 5 ||

A lamp that flickers to the left, has dirty rays, sparks, or a small flame—even if supplied with clean oil and a good wick—if it quickly goes out, it speaks of "sinful" <note>original: "pāpa"; here meaning inauspicious or negative results arising from past actions</note> results. So too if it is noisy, trembling, has scattered flames, or repeatedly dies out despite being clean. || 6 ||

A lamp that has a compact flame, a tall body, is without trembling, is radiant, silent, beautiful, moving in a clockwise direction, and possesses the luster of cat's-eye gem or gold...

---

**"When not too close" etc. ||** The meaning is that at a time not too close to the sun's midday or rising, the measurement of the foot-shadow <term>Pada-chāyā: a method of determining time or astronomical position by measuring the length of one's own shadow</term> is easily accomplished. || 3 ||

**"Inquiry" etc. ||** The connection here is that the bringing of the lamp is a provider of auspiciousness. || 4 ||

**"In all inquiries" etc. ||** This refers to all questions regarding lifespan, marriage, progeny, and so on. "In all acts" refers to worship, giving, eating, and the like. || 5 ||

**"To the left" etc. ||** "Flickering to the left" means the flame does not move clockwise. "Small flame" means a short or thin flame. The description "which quickly goes out even if supplied with clean oil and wick" is an adjective for the lamp. It "speaks of sin," meaning it indicates inauspicious results produced by the ripening of negative past actions. Here, regarding "trembling," the word "of the lamp" should be understood. A direct identity between the lamp and the abstract quality of trembling is illogical; rather, it means "possessing that trembling," treating the quality and the object as one for the sake of metaphor. || 6 ||

**"The lamp" etc. ||** "Compact" means a flame that is unified and not flickering apart. "Beautiful" means it pleases the mind of the observer. "Luster of cat's-eye or gold" means it has the color of one of those two. "High-crested" <insert>this refers to the term 'ucchikha' found in the commentary</insert> means an upward-pointing flame. It indicates "Lakshmi" or prosperity, and "long-lasting" auspicious outcomes. The rest of the characteristics are the opposite of those previously mentioned. The following two verses are presented here as they are useful, even though the manuscript has some gaps <note>original: "granthapāta"; refers to missing portions of the physical manuscript</note>. || 7 ||

<meta>This page continues the technical analysis of the ceremonial lamp used in Prasnamarga (The Path of Inquiry), a classic text on Horary Astrology. It focuses on the symbolic correspondences between the lamp's components and the querent's life.</meta>

<page-num>64</page-num>
# The Path of Inquiry
<note>original: "Prasnamarga"</note>

->A lamp that appears with a high, bright flame quickly reveals radiant prosperity;<-
->the remaining characteristics should be interpreted logically, similar to the signs of fire. || 7 ||<-

->In this world, the oil is the body; the wick within it<-
->is the soul;<-
->the flame is the lifespan; its clarity or sootiness<-
->represents happiness and sorrow respectively.<-
->The vessel is the house; the wind—whether gentle or harsh—<-
->represents the nature of friends and enemies.<-
->That lamp, embodying the Great Deity,<-
->generally reveals the state of the querent. || 8 ||<-

---

**Regarding the Oil etc. ||** In this lamp, the **oil** <note>original: "sneha," which means both oil/fat and affection</note> is the **body**, meaning the physical form of the person asking the question (the querent). Based on the lightness, quantity, dirtiness, or purity of the oil, as well as any insects found within it, one should contemplate the querent's physical health—whether they are thin or stout, their complexion, or if they are suffering from parasites or similar afflictions.

By **the wick is the soul**, it is meant that if the wick climbs over another wick, it indicates a covering or obstruction of the vital breaths <note>prana</note> in the soul. If the wick is clean, it indicates clarity of intellect. This should be carefully considered. Here, regarding the word "wick-dweller" <note>vartini</note>, some say it is a single compound word "dwelling-in-its-belly" <note>tad-udare-vartini</note> based on grammatical rules regarding suffixes. Others explain the grammar through different linguistic derivations.

The **flame is the lifespan**. If the flame is steady, a long life is understood; if it is small or weak, a short life is indicated. **Clarity and sootiness** represent **happiness and sorrow** respectively: clarity of the flame indicates happiness, while sootiness indicates suffering.

The **vessel is the house**. If the vessel is large, the house is spacious; if it is clean, the house is pure. If the vessel is moved from one place to another, it suggests the querent moving from their original home to another.

The **wind**, depending on whether it is **gentle or harsh**, represents the **nature of friends and enemies**. If a gentle breeze affects the lamp, it indicates help from friends. If a harsh wind affects it, it indicates trouble from enemies.

Here, following the "Ten Chapters" <note>Dasadhyayi</note> commentary on the *Brihat Jataka*, one should observe the oil to understand the results of merit and sin (karma) and the resulting happiness or sorrow; the wick for bodily qualities; and the flame for qualities of the soul. Because of this, some scholars suggest an alternative reading: "the wick is the lifespan and the flame is the soul." However, they do not account for the contradiction this creates with the "Ten Chapters" regarding the oil being the body. Therefore, the method in the "Ten Chapters" is one way, and the method described in this verse is another. Since both are considered authoritative, we believe the final conclusion is that both perspectives should be considered for a complete interpretation. Regarding the word "reveals" <note>pishunayati</note>, it literally means "to make known" or "to indicate"...

# Chapter Four

->A flame spreading toward the East grants desired boons; in the Southeast, it brings fear of fire;<-
->In the South, it signifies loss of life;<-
->In the Southwest, there will be forgetfulness; in the West, the flame<-
->Grants peace; in the Northwest,<-
->A void flame <note>likely meaning a flickering or hollow-looking flame</note> brings death; in the North, the flame<-
->Bestows health and longevity; in the Northeast,<-
->The upward flame of the fire immediately grants<-
->The physical body its desired objects. || 9 ||<-

->If one cuts or breaks the materials prepared for the inquiry<-
->And places them in the zodiac sign occupied by Gulika <note>Gulika is a mathematical point in Vedic astrology, often considered a "shadow planet" with a malefic influence</note>,<-
->Or in the eighth house from the questioner's birth star,<-
->Immediate death is indicated, unless it is aspected by Jupiter <note>original: "Jiva-drishti"; Jupiter's gaze is considered the most purifying and protective influence in astrology</note>. || 10 ||<-

---

Regarding the phrase "indicators of the wicked," according to the lexicon, if we accept the meaning of "indicator," one must somehow interpret the connection by implying an object, such as "one who betrays oneself." In this way, the word "occurrence" must be managed by implying "having made it the subject." Otherwise, the second grammatical case cannot be justified. Alternatively, a reading ending in the seventh case should be considered for "occurrence." This would be the locative of reference. But enough of this exhausting analysis of the hermitage of debate. || 8 ||

**Regarding "East" etc. ||** "East" means spreading toward the eastern direction, granting all desired things. "Flame of the fire" is the subject to be qualified. This is an application of the rule: "The remaining characteristics are equal to the primary signs," showing that these signs should be applied to the characteristics of a lamp. "In the fire-corner" means the Southeast. This should be applied to the directions facing that way. "Forgetfulness" refers to memory loss; mental illnesses like epilepsy should also be considered here. <insert>A "void" flame provides emptiness, meaning it destroys prosperity.</insert> In the direction of the Giver of Wealth <note>the North, ruled by Kubera</note>, it is "Death-conquering," meaning it promotes health. In the section called "Shikha" <note>the Northeast</note>, the word "corner" or "direction" should be supplied as the qualifier. In some places here, the flame is described as the giver of the fruit; in others, only the fruit itself is mentioned. Sometimes the rule of the result is twofold; sometimes it is a single crest. Such variations are appropriate for the author, whose dictates are not to be questioned. The grammatical connection should be managed somehow by supplying appropriate words. Any break in the flow should be endured by closing one's eyes to it; enough with this harsh handling of delicate poetry. || 9 ||

**Regarding "For the purpose of inquiry" etc. ||** "For the purpose of inquiry" means for the act of divination. "Materials" refers to the items prepared and used for the ritual. "In the sign occupied by Gulika": here one should take the sign from the fixed zodiac as mentioned in the rule "Aries and Taurus are in the East." "In the eighth sign from the questioner": this means the eighth sign from the questioner's birth Moon. "Should place": this refers to the assistant or someone else performing the action. "Aspected by Jupiter": this is a qualifier for the sign of Gulika or the eighth sign from the questioner. The seventh aspect <note>an opposition</note> should be taken here; in other traditions, the trine aspect is also considered. || 10 ||

Regarding the verse beginning with "Pure": "Pure" means white. "Rice" is also an <term>upalakṣaṇa: a linguistic synecdoche</term> for other grains. The word "and so on" includes the collection of coconuts, betel leaves, areca nuts, and the eight auspicious items <note>The Ashtamangala: a set of eight holy objects used in rituals</note>. "Level" means free from high or low spots. "Well-cleaned and sprinkled" is an indirect reference to further decorations like a canopy, according to one's wealth. "Draw the chart"—since a specific person is not named as the subject, it may be drawn by an assistant or someone else. It is not appropriate to assume the Astrologer is the one who draws it. This is because if the Astrologer draws it, they might inadvertently be influenced by the good or bad omens observed during the drawing process. One who knows the omens of the drawing should not be the one performing the act. Therefore, the text will later say in the section on placing the gold coin: "or someone who is ignorant of the positions of the signs and planets." || 11 ||

Regarding the verse beginning with "Cubit": "Cubit measure" refers to a measurement of twenty-four inches <note>original: "hasta"</note>. In a square area of that size, one should make sixteen equal divisions using parts of six inches each. Here, in the center, with four divisions, let there be a four-petaled lotus. One should fashion it in the shape of a lotus. The other twelve divisions are to be understood as the zodiac signs starting with Aries. Starting from the southern line of the section in the Northeast corner, the signs Aries and the rest should be arranged. In this way, the sign Pisces will end up in the Northeast corner. || 12 ||

Regarding the verse beginning with "Some": This establishes that drawing with ash is indeed the traditional practice. || 13 ||

Regarding the verse beginning with "Clockwise": "Mixed or reverse order" means drawing one part clockwise and then another part counter-clockwise. This results in the "occurrence of obstacles." It does not mean the desired work will not be accomplished, but rather there will be a delay due to the presence of obstacles in the middle. || 14 ||

Regarding the verse beginning with "Thick line": A break in the line is a "destroyer" of happiness and the task at hand. || 15 ||

<summary>This page provides ritual and technical instructions for drawing the zodiac chart on the ground using rice or ash, emphasizing that the drawing should be done clockwise by an assistant to avoid biasing the astrologer.</summary>
<keywords>zodiac chart, ritual preparation, Aries, cubit measurement, omens, clockwise, ash drawing, Prashna astrology</keywords>

# Chapter Four

-> If a gentle line is drawn toward the North, wealth will surely come. <-

-> the land where the inquirer resides will be similarly low or high in those spots. || 18 || <-
-> Where there are bits of grass in the diagram, there are trees; <-
-> where it is moistened with water, there is a source of water. <-
-> Where there is a pebble, there is a stone; where there is sand, <-
-> the ground there is elevated. <-
-> Where there are *Kera* <note>original: "kera"; refers to coconut palms</note> or other trees shaped like coconut palms, <-
-> or where there is earth brought by ants, there is an anthill <-
-> on the land of the inquirer. || 19 || <-
-> From the initial touch and other actions of the one who draws the diagram, <-
-> the characteristics of the inquirer's land must be considered. <-

---

**Regarding the drawing**: "Gentle" <term>saumya: northern</term> refers to the North. "Varuni" refers to the West. "Aindri" refers to the East. "Yamya" refers to the South.

**Regarding the diagram**: "In whatever part" [the feature appears]. The place of residence, like the diagram, will be low or high in those respective parts. The specific details found in the diagram should be carefully observed and then predicted as being present in the inquirer's house. This is explained in the very next verse. || 18 ||

**In the diagram**: "Grass" refers to fallen bits of grass. "Moistened with water" means wet with liquid. "Water" refers to that found in wells, ponds, and so on. "Pebble" refers to small stones and the like. In the part where there is "sand," the ground in that area is elevated. "*Keras*" are coconut trees. "Earth-growers" are trees. In the part where there is "earth brought by ants," there is an anthill. One should announce these things by applying reasoning. An alternative reading is "on the land of the inquirer." || 19 ||

**Regarding the touch and so on**: This refers to the act of making predictions about the inquirer's characteristics based on whatever the person drawing the diagram does first—such as touching a certain spot—immediately after drawing it. This land belongs to the inquirer and is their place of residence. The interpretation follows if that hand is wearing a ring, or if the limbs are encircled by vines... <note>The text cuts off mid-sentence regarding the physical appearance of the diviner's hand.</note>

# The Path of Inquiry

->If, after drawing a diagram, the questioner gives<-
->some object to another person, then this land<-
->will pass into the possession of another. If they<-
->receive an object from another, it indicates the acquisition of another's land.<-

->If they extend their hand toward themselves and lift it,<-
->there are trees <note>original: "naga," literally "those that do not move," referring to trees or mountains.</note> present; if the fingers are extended,<-
->the hand represents trees entwined with climbing vines.<-

->The neck represents the same if ornaments are touched.<-
->Fingers without "branches" <note>meaning fingers held tightly together</note> represent trees without branches;<-
->if the hand is closed in a fist, it indicates mere stumps.<-

->If one touches the hair on the face <note>such as a beard or mustache</note> that is half-cut,<-
->one should predict the presence of thorny trees.<-
->If the nostrils or the ears are touched,<-
->there is a hole or burrow for snakes or mice.<-

->If one touches loosened hair or the hair of the face,<-
->one should point to the presence of Munja grass, Ushira, or Kusha grass.<-
->If the nose is touched, it indicates a terminal mound <note>original: "valmika," an anthill or termite mound</note>.<-

---

"Trees" is the qualifying term here. Similarly, it means "limbs entwined by vines." "Stumps" refers to trees devoid of branches, trunks, and so on. (Verses 20-22)

**Regarding the face:** "Thorny" means possessing thorns, such as the Kinshuka tree and others. "Ear" refers to the auditory passage. Regarding the touching of the nose, another characteristic will be mentioned. "A hole for snakes or mice" means a place serving as their dwelling. (Verse 23)

**Regarding the hair:** "Loosened" means having the binding fallen away; this qualifies the hair. "Born of the face" qualifies the small hairs <note>facial hair</note>. "Munja" is a specific type of grass used for priestly girdles. "Kusha" is a specific type of sacred Darpha grass. The construction is: "Upon the touching of the nose, a termite mound." "Nasa" means the nose. <note>The text notes a grammatical substitution of "nas" for "nasika".</note> Without further distinction, "nose" could mean both the external nose and the nostrils. Since the "hole" (nostril) was already mentioned, by the rule of elimination, this refers specifically to the bridge of the nose.

# Chapter Four

-> If the questioner touches their genitals, belly, or eyes, or if they wipe their face or breasts, or if they touch themselves while standing in water, the dowser should declare that the land in question contains a constant supply of rising water. If they touch a limb that is perspiring, the same result is predicted. ॥ 24 ॥ <-

-> If the armpit or the anus is touched, the water is of poor quality <note>literally "corrupted" or "foul"</note>. If the arms are raised high, there are very tall trees on the land. If the hands are held low, the trees there are very stunted <term>kharva: a term for dwarfed or short vegetation</term>. If the teeth or nails are touched, there are metals <note>such as copper, iron, or tin</note> in the earth. ॥ 25 ॥ <-

-> If the knees or other bony parts of the body are touched, the ground is filled with a network of stones and buried bones. If the navel or other depressed parts of the body are touched, the questioner's land contains pits and is supplied with small water-channels <term>kulyā: artificial irrigation ditches or small streams</term>. ॥ 26 ॥ <-

---

Some authorities suggest alternative interpretations of these results. "Touching" refers to physical contact. "The lap" <note>original: *kroḍa*</note> refers to the belly. If the genitals and other mentioned parts are touched, the questioner's site possesses excellent water. "Perspiring limb" means one's own body part covered in sweat. ॥ 24 ॥

**Regarding the armpit** etc. ॥ "Anus" refers to the rectum. "Corrupted water" is the result. "On the questioner's land" is the implied location. "Very tall" implies that the branches may also be sparse. "Stunted" means short. "Metals" refers to copper, iron, tin, and the like. "Teeth and nails" <note>original: *dantakhān*</note>. In the grammatical rule beginning with *paddannomās*, the word for tooth (*danta*) is substituted with *dat*. However, since the rule specifies this occurs before certain suffixes, and no such suffix follows here, one might ask: how can the substitution occur? Understand that the inclusion of "etc." in the rule implies similarity. This similarity is treated as if a suffix were present. Just as internal case endings are acknowledged to establish the word-status of components within a compound, here too, a "dropped" suffix is assumed based on the rule "of the suffix of the root or crude form" to allow the substitution. This is why the commentary text "the pot for cooking meat" is grammatically valid. If one objects that these substitutions are only for Vedic Sanskrit and not common usage, then consult the works of the commentator Kaiyaṭa <note>A famous 11th-century Kashmiri grammarian</note>, who holds that such usage is not incorrect in common language. If you still stubbornly persist in your objection <note>literally "a monkey's fist-grip"</note>, then we are simply justifying the ancient Teacher's words here, not necessarily using them ourselves—so please be satisfied with that. ॥ 25 ॥

**Regarding the knees** etc. ॥ If the knees or other bony parts are touched, the connection is that the questioner's land is filled with networks of stones and bones. "Filled" means pervaded by them. "Pits" refers to holes or burrows. "Channels" are small man-made streams; the land is endowed with these. ॥ 26 ॥

<header>The Path of Inquiry</header>

## With his left arm resting on his knee, holding a deer, an axe,
## and the gesture of wisdom,
## Wearing a rising serpent as a meditation band, and granting
## knowledge to the assembly of sages—I praise that Lord of Wisdom. || 32 ||

...placed above. Regarding the <term>assembly of sages</term> <note>original: rishigane</note>, this refers to the group of great seers led by the sage Shuka. Here, the locative case is used even though they are the recipients of knowledge, following the grammatical rule: 
> "Because the universe possesses manifold powers and manifold actions, and because its states are ever-changing, a particular grammatical relation is expressed according to the speaker's intent at any given time." 

<note>This quote justifies the use of the Sanskrit locative case to show the sages as the "location" where knowledge is placed.</note> The "serpent" refers to a snake. He is the one whose <term>meditation band</term> <note>a strap used to hold the legs in place during seated meditation</note> is a rising serpent. In this context, it is necessary to imagine the zodiac signs starting with Aries, the nine planets including the Sun, and <term>Gulika</term> <note>a mathematical point in Vedic astrology considered the son of Saturn, often associated with karmic obstacles</note> as the surrounding retinue. This is because their worship as such will be described in the following verse. By the word "I praise" <note>ide</note>, meditation is primarily intended. That word is used formally here, as it was introduced previously as a meditation verse. The literal meaning of the root—"praise"—should be understood in its proper sequence. || 32 ||

## The zodiac signs starting with Aries in their respective places, the planets in their resident signs,
## and Gulika should be worshipped by their own names as the surrounding retinue. || 33 ||

**Regarding "The signs starting with Aries":** They should be worshipped—the words "with water, sandalwood paste, and flowers" are understood. "By their own names" means preceded by the chanting of mantras such as "Salutations to Aries, the retinue of the Supreme Lord." By the phrase "as the surrounding retinue," the status of being a retinue must be mentally projected. They should not be joined as mere parts of a mantra. Therefore, simple forms like "Salutations to Aries" <note>Meshaya namah</note> should be adopted. Others say that the phrase "by their own names" was used specifically with this intention. In this tradition of worshipping the signs, specific genders are observed, such as "To Virgo" <note>Kanyayai - feminine</note>, and specific numbers such as "To the two Fish" <note>Minabhyam - dual</note> for Pisces. Regarding the worship of planets, others hold that the specific Vedic hymns for each, such as "By the Truth..." <note>the 'Asatyena' mantra for the Sun</note>, should also be employed. In the names for Libra, Sagittarius, and Aquarius, the word "Bearer" <note>dhara</note> should be appended, such as "Salutations to the Holder of the Scales" <note>Tuladharaya namah</note>, in accordance with established custom. || 33 ||

## After the offering to the Absolute, one should worship the Goddess of Speech and the Teachers in the Eight Auspicious Symbols
## with flowers, and likewise worship Prosperity in the lamp. || 34 ||

**Regarding "Absolute":** The <term>offering to the Absolute</term> <note>brahmarpanam</note> is the act performed at the conclusion of the worship. At its end, one worships the Goddess of Speech, Saraswati. In the <term>Eight Auspicious Symbols</term> <note>ashtamangala</note>—consisting of the white cloth, mirror, casket, book, and others placed beside the astrological chart—one should worship her by chanting "Salutations to the Goddess of Speech." "In the lamp" refers to the lamp placed in front of the chart. || 34 ||

# Chapter Four

Now, having washed the gold with water and adorned it with sandalwood paste, one should place it upon a leaf and join it with flowers and consecrated grains. <note>verse 35</note>
Then, placing it in the left hand and using the other hand, one should devotedly chant the <term>Panchakshari</term><note>The five-syllable mantra: "Namah Shivaya"</note> and other mantras one hundred and eight times. <note>verse 36</note>
Having chanted and set them aside together, one should begin the <term>Ashtamangalam</term><note>A highly specialized form of Vedic divination using 108 cowrie shells</note> ritual. Now, that ceremony is described in brief as taught by the Preceptor. <note>verse 37</note>
Having placed the <term>Rashi Chakra</term><note>The zodiacal circle or chart</note> to the right, seated on a facing-east seat, one should place one hundred and eight <term>Varatikas</term><note>Cowrie shells used as counters in divination</note> upon an unbroken wooden board. <note>verse 38</note>
Having sprinkled them with water while reciting mantras, and adorning them with scent, flowers, and consecrated grains, one should worship Lord Shiva within them, invoking Him as if in a sacred circle. <note>verse 39</note>
In the directions starting from the East, one should worship the Sun and the other planets, including the Moon, Mercury, and the Nodes <insert>Rahu and Ketu</insert>. Then, touching the shells repeatedly, one should chant one hundred and eight times <note>verse 40</note>
the <term>Panchakshari</term> and other mantras as heard from the mouth of one's Preceptor. Then, one should pray to the Deity, to one's own Preceptors, and to the Planets. <note>verse 41</note>

---

**Regarding "Now" (Atha):** The "gold" refers to a gold coin <note>original: "svarna-mudra"</note> available at that particular time. "Adorned with sandalwood"—one must supply the action "having done so." "Consecrated grains" <note>original: "akshata"</note> refers to wet rice grains mixed with three parts of other grain. <note>Commentary on verse 35</note>

**Regarding "In the left hand":** "Having placed" refers to the leaf upon which the gold coin has been set; this is understood through context. "One hundred and eight times" means through one hundred and eight repetitions. "Other mantras" refers to other sacred formulas as instructed. "Ashtamangalam" refers to the ritual about to be described. "Taught" means instructed. <note>Commentary on verses 36, 37</note>

**Regarding "Having placed":** "Having placed the zodiac circle to the right" means on the northern side of the zodiac circle. "On an unbroken" <note>original: "abhinne"</note> means on a smooth board free from cracks or splits. "One hundred and eight cowries" means cowrie shells numbering one hundred and eight. "Having placed them on the board." "With mantras" means along with the specific mantras one has received. "Sprinkled" means with water over which mantras have been recited. "Those cowries... as if in a circle" means in the manner described in verses such as "On the peak of Mount Kailasa," etc. The word division is "on an unbroken board" <note>original: "phalake abhinne"</note>. Others divide the words as "on a separate board" <note>original: "phalake bhinne"</note>, interpreting it as a board other than the one used for one's own seat. That is not a pleasing interpretation, as there is no intention here for the practitioner's seat to necessarily be a wooden board; it could just as well be a skin-mat or other material. <note>Commentary on verses 38, 39</note>

**Regarding "In the directions starting from the East":** In the eight directions of the heap of cowrie shells, starting with the East, one should worship the Sun and others in order. "Those cowries"—"touching them repeatedly" means moving one's hand over the heap of cowries in a clockwise direction. One hundred and eight—

# The Path of Inquiry

"For this person, born under this specific star <note>original: *nakshatra*</note> and bearing this name, who now inquires: regarding the past, the present, and the time yet to come; (42)

Regarding the good and bad fortunes currently being contemplated, and specifically the possibility or impossibility of acquiring wealth, children, houses, and the like; (43)

May all these matters, both auspicious and inauspicious, manifest clearly in my mind in their true essence, through your divine grace." (44)

Then, a young girl or a young boy—one who has bathed and is adorned with fresh clothes and ornaments, and who is entirely ignorant of the positions of the zodiac signs and planets—or perhaps some other suitable person, (45)

Should approach and worship the Lamp, Lord Ganesha <note>The elephant-headed deity who removes obstacles</note>, and the Lords of the Planets with flowers. Then, the astrologer should place a piece of gold along with unbroken rice and flowers into that person's right hand. (46)

Carrying these items, that wise person should circumambulate <note>walk clockwise around</note> the zodiac chart and then stand near the chart facing East. (47)

Then, the questioner should stand with hands folded in prayer <note>original: *anjali*</note>, meditating on their desired goal. The astrologer, also keeping the questioner's goal in mind, should repeatedly touch the cowrie shells <note>term: *varatikas* — small shells used as dice or counters in divination</note> while chanting the "Murtitve" hymn. (48)

After chanting this three times, he should instruct the messenger <note>the child or assistant</note> to "Place the gold." (49)

---

The prayer should be repeated 108 times. In the manner described in the following three verses, one should insert the specific birth star and name in the appropriate places. For example: "Of one born under the star Ashvini, named Narayana Sharma," and so on. (40-44)

**Regarding "Then" (Verse 45):** A "girl" means one who is unmarried. A "boy" means one who has not yet reached youth. "Adorned with clothes etc." means wearing clean white garments, marked with sacred ash or sandalwood paste, and wearing ornaments such as rings. "Approaching" means coming near the zodiac chart. "The Lamp, the Lord of Obstacles (Ganapati), and the Lords of the Heavens" refers to the Sun and the other planets. Here, the gender of the assistant is not the primary concern. The one performing the action is the one who has completed the chanting of the five-syllable mantra. "Circumambulation of the chart" means walking around the zodiac diagram three times. "Behind" means at the rear section. "Wise" implies a steady mind. "Facing East" means with eyes fixed on the zodiac chart and ears waiting for the astrologer's command.

**Regarding "Then" (Verse 48):** The "Questioner" is the one asking or their representative. "Those cowrie shells" refers to the shells consecrated by sprinkling holy water and chanting mantras. "Beginning with *Murtitve*" refers to the first verse of the *Brihat Jataka* <note>A foundational 6th-century Sanskrit text on astronomy and astrology by Varahamihira</note> which begins with the words "Murtitve parikalpitah." "Of that chanting" refers to the mantra recitation. The word "messenger" here refers to the person designated to place the gold piece. He should say, "Place it." This instruction also applies to the three-fold repetition. (48, 49)

<meta>This page continues the instructions for the ritual of Ashtamangala Prashna (Eight-Auspicious-Questioning), specifically detailing the physical actions of the messenger and the astrologer during the divination process.</meta>

# Chapter Four

At that very moment, the messenger should place the gold piece held in his hand upon one of the signs in the zodiac circle. The astrologer should then divide those cowrie shells <note>original: "varāṭikāḥ"; small shells used as counting tokens in divination</note> into three parts, starting from the north-east, and observe the omens. || 50–51 ||

Whatever auspicious or inauspicious signs were mentioned previously at the time of the initial inquiry—such as the touching of limbs or the movement of breath <term>shara: literally 'arrow', here referring to the flow of breath through the nostrils</term>—all of those should be considered here as well. Then, the messenger should measure the length of his shadow on level ground. || 52 ||

The zodiac sign in which the gold piece is placed is known as the **Arudha** <note>The 'mounted' or 'ascendant' sign for this specific query</note>. The knower of fate <note>the astrologer</note>, having identified the Arudha and noting whether the gold piece is facing upward or otherwise, || 53 ||

should announce some initial results to the inquirer. After completing the worship <insert>including the ritual dismissal of the deities</insert>, he should set aside the cowrie shells in groups of eight from the three separate locations. || 54 ||

Having determined the remaining number <note>the remainder after dividing by eight</note>, those cowrie shells must be carefully preserved. || 55 ||

The astrologer should record the Arudha, the position of the gold, the shadow measurement, and the **Ashtamangala** <note>the 'Eight Auspicious' results derived from the cowrie remainders</note>, preceded by the current month, the elapsed days of the year, and the birth star of the inquirer. || 56 ||

**At that very moment...** refers to the exact time the astrologer gives the command. "In one of the signs" refers to any of the twelve signs from Aries onwards in the zodiac circle. "Divide into three" means he should make three distinct heaps. The first part is placed in the North, the second in the Middle, and the third in the South. He should then reflect. This detail is explained by the subsequent verse. By the word "arrow" (*shara*), the movement of breath is intended. The "messenger" intended here is someone with a balanced body. "On level ground" means a patch of earth free from pits or elevations. By "shadow measurement," units such as fingers (*angula*) or barley-corns (*yava*) are also intended.

**The sign in which...** refers to the zodiac sign where the gold is placed. The phrase "by the knower of fate, the Arudha" should be read as a single concept. By the word "upwardness," one should also include factors such as the contact (or lack thereof) with flowers and grains, and the specific division of the parts. "Some results" refers to any small indication of good or bad fortune. "After completing" implies the ritual dismissal of the invoked presence. "From the three locations" refers to the heaps of cowries placed in the North, Middle, and South. "Setting aside in eights" means removing groups of eight shells until a remainder is found. "Having determined the remaining number"—at this point, a detailed explanation of the number of betel leaves, their qualities, and defects must be given immediately. Otherwise, if the betel leaves dry out, it becomes impossible to gain accurate knowledge from them. || 53–55 ||

**The Arudha...** The word "month" also implies the year. By the word "star" (*tara*), one should also include the house name, the ritual name, and so on. It should be understood that clearly recording the signs of light, the signs of the specific time, the number of betel leaves, and the nature of the betel leaves is also essential. || 56 ||

# Now begins the Fifth Chapter

## Now the calculation of the Ascendant and related matters are described

> When the exact position of the Ascendant at the time of the query is clearly understood,
> the success of the prediction is assured, as stated in other sacred sciences. || 1 ||

> When the astronomical system <note>original: "tantra"</note> is thoroughly mastered,
> when the Ascendant is known through the shadow or water-clock instruments,
> and when the meanings of the horoscopic signs are firmly grasped,
> the speech of the astrologer shall never be in vain. || 2 ||

Regarding this, the method for determining the elapsed time of the day in *nadikas* <note>A unit of time equal to 24 minutes</note> is first described:

> Having measured the shadow produced at that moment, subtract the value of the preceding mnemonic verse.
> Convert the remainder into digits <note>original: "angula"</note>, multiply by sixty, and divide
> by the difference in digits between the two verses corresponding to the shadow's length at that time.
> The resulting *vinadikas* <note>A unit of time equal to 24 seconds</note> should be subtracted from the time value of the subtracted verse. || 3-4 ||

---

"Now" (*Atha*): Following the sequence of topics such as the emergence of the query, after the initial ritual actions, it is necessary to determine the exact Ascendant and other factors required for explaining the "Sutra" <note>The thread or guiding principle of the query</note> and its clarity; therefore, this calculation is undertaken.

"When the query..." (*Prashna...*): Only when this is true [is the prediction successful]. The implication is that otherwise, it results in failure. || 1 ||

"In the system..." (*Tantre...*): When the astronomical systems such as the *Surya Siddhanta* are thoroughly understood through careful examination. The mention of "shadow and water-clock instruments" also implies other tools like bells or gongs used for timekeeping. "Horoscopy" refers to the works of sages like Parashara. When these are "firmly grasped"—meaning well-understood and memorized—then the "speech," in the form of the prediction, will not be "barren" or inaccurate. || 2 ||

"Regarding this..." (*Tatra...*): Regarding the calculation of the Ascendant. The word *nadika* here also implies its subdivisions like *vinadikas*. This explains the method to know, by the measurement of the shadow taken at that moment, exactly how many *nadikas* and *vinadikas* have elapsed from sunrise until the moment the gold <note>referring to a ritual coin or object used in the query</note> was placed.

"The shadow..." (*Chhaya...*): The section from "the shadow" to "by the digits" describes a "Rule of Three" <note>original: "trairashika"; a mathematical proportion</note> calculation. In this, the "difference in digits" is the standard measure. Sixty *vinadikas* is the result. The remainder after subtracting the upper verse value from the current shadow is the "desired quantity." The mnemonic verses begin with "When the Sun is in Leo or Aries..." as revealed in the *Jyotishashastrabodhini*. And that...

If the birth star of the querent is not obtained when the calculated Ascendant is multiplied by the <term>Kunda</term> <note>A mathematical factor, usually 81, used for rectification</note>, then one must add or subtract certain minutes of arc to arrive at the querent's birth star || 8 ||

### Chapter Five

Beginning with the sign of Aries, the correction is negative or positive according to the sequence: Lute (1), Bow (5), Eye (2), and Moon (1) <note>These are numerical code words (ka-ta-pa-ya-di system) representing specific values for the lunar correction</note>. In the Kollam era <note>The Malayalam calendar starting 825 CE</note> designated by the number "Sura-Hrasa" (1223), the conjunction of the Moon is considered powerful. || 11 ||
As the years pass in the "Subha" era, one minute of arc <term>liptika: 1/60th of a degree</term> should be added for each cycle. || 12 ||
This method for calculating the "Drig" (observed) Moon is clearly stated in the text *Kanthabharana*. That too is written here:

->The Kollam year, adjusted by the difference in minutes and the precession of the equinoxes,<-
->derived from the Sun at that time,<-
->divided by "Saumyapriya" (17), and then subtracted or added<-
->based on the sine and cosine of the Sun's position.<-
->Combined with "Shivaka" (115) and multiplied by the difference in the mnemonic sentences,<-
->then divided by "Dhanesha" (509),<-
->and added to the minutes of the Parahita Moon, results in the observed Moon. || 13 ||<-

The corrections should be applied every ten days. Here, starting from the tenth day of Virgo until the tenth day of Sagittarius, and from the tenth day of Pisces until the tenth day of Gemini, the value should be subtracted from the Moon's longitude; for the remaining six months, it should be added to the Moon's longitude. In the *Parahita* method of calculating the length of the day, only the sine of the Sun's position and the ascensional difference are taken. However, the equation of time <term>prana-kalantara: the difference between mean and apparent solar time</term> is not included. In the *Drig* (observational) method, the equation of time is also taken into account. This correction is intended to equalize the two. At the time this book was composed, the precession of the equinoxes <term>ayanacalana: the slow shifting of the Earth's rotational axis</term> was accepted as being 20 degrees; therefore, the tenth day of Virgo and Pisces was taken as the limit. The word "Arka" in numerical notation refers to the tenth part. However, due to the passage of time, the precession is now approximately 22 degrees, so it should be understood that the eighth day should be taken as the limit. Regarding the "Subha" years, the word "Subha" represents the number 47; the addition of one minute every 47 years is also only an approximation. This approximation becomes clear when examining the difference between the Moon's mean position as calculated by the *Drig* and *Parahita* methods. This actual discrepancy should be understood by skilled astronomers. Enough on this. || 10-12 ||

**Regarding "This":** *Kanthabharana* is the name of another astronomical treatise.

**Regarding "Kollam":** It is added to the minutes of the *Parahita* Moon. The term "subtracted or added" is a modifier for the Kollam year. The Kali year reduced by the "Taralahva" number is to be taken as the Kollam year. The words "Saumyapriya," "Shivaka," and "Dhanesha" represent the numbers 17, 115, and 509 respectively in numerical notation. "By the difference in sentences" refers to another mnemonic sentence. Here, the sentence beginning with "Girnahshreya"...

Thus, when the value brought by the rule of three is added to the positions of movable or dual signs, it results in "Death" <note>Mrityu</note>. When subtracted, it results in "Time" <note>Kala</note>. Both Death and Time should be recorded. The sequence for all these—Sun, Moon, Jupiter, Mercury, etc.—will be clarified in the sixteenth chapter in the 106th verse. || 23 ||

**Regarding "The Sun" etc. ||** The lords of the rising signs and the lords of the ninth-part subdivisions <note>term: "Navamsha" — a 3°20' division of a zodiac sign used for greater detail</note> for the three—Sun, Moon, and Arudha—must be specifically determined. By the qualification "aligning with observation," the author emphasizes that one should not merely accept traditional "Parahita" mathematics, but rather "Drik-ganita" <note>observational astronomy</note>. The qualification "accurate" suggests that the observational accuracy of a mathematical system should be known through one's own testing. || 29 ||

**Regarding "Another scripture" ||** The words "it is said" are implied here. ||

**Regarding "In conjunction" ||** "In the conjunction of planets" means when they meet each other. "In combustion" refers to their setting caused by proximity to the Sun. The sense is that this decision is made only through testing over many days. With that calculation, "calculate three times" means one should bring it forth after calculating with extreme precision. || 30 ||

**Regarding "Whenever" ||** "With that very system" refers to whichever of the five traditional systems <note>The five Siddhantas: Paitamaha, Romaka, Paulisa, Vasishtha, and Surya</note> is proven by direct perception to match observation. "Birth chart" <note>Jataka</note> is also an indirect reference to horary questions and other branches. || 31 ||

**Regarding "The Ascendant" ||** One should add the minutes and degrees of the calculated Ascendant to the Arudha sign. That becomes the "Precise Arudha." The phrase "precise value for that" <note>original: "sphutavaptya amushya"</note> is a grammatical breakdown. Through the substitution of the vowel 'ai' and the dropping of 'ya', it refers to "of that Arudha." || 32 ||

# Now begins the Sixth Chapter

Now, the *Sutras* <note>technical term for diagnostic threads or connections between astrological points</note> are being described.

->The *Sutra* derived from the *Arudha* <note>the sign rising at the time of the query</note> and the *Udaya Lagna* <note>the ascendant sign</note> is known as the **General Sutra**.<-
->That which is considered from the lords of those two signs is called the **Lordship Sutra**. || 1 ||<-
->The *Sutra* derived from the *Navamsha* <note>the ninth divisional chart</note> of the ascendant and the *Arudha* sign is called the **Amsaka Sutra**.<-
->That which is considered from the birth star of the ascendant and the birth star of the querent is called the **Asterism Sutra**. || 2 ||<-
->One should consider the **Great Sutra** from the *Arudha* and its tenth house.<-
->The General Sutra is of the Earth element; the Lordship Sutra is of the Water element. || 3 ||<-
->The Amsaka Sutra is of the Fire element; the Asterism Sutra is of the Air element.<-
->The Great Sutra is of the Ether element; these are the five *Sutras*. || 4 ||<-
->They should be considered with primary importance as they are composed of the five elements.<-
->If the pair of the *Arudha* and the Ascendant are both in movable signs, || 5 ||<-
->Or if one is in a dual sign and the other is in a fixed sign, it is the **Life Sutra**; thus it is of two kinds.<-
->If one of the *Arudha* or Ascendant is in a movable sign and the other is in [a dual sign], || 6 ||<-
->Or if both are in fixed signs, it is likewise the **Death Sutra**, which is also of two kinds.<-
->If one of them is situated in a movable sign and the other is in a fixed sign... || 7 ||<-

**Now [the commentary]:** "Now" means after the description of calculating the longitudes of the ascendant and other points, following the order intended for the emergence of the query.

**Regarding "Arudha" etc.:** In these two and a half verses, the means for determining the five *Sutras* are shown. The method of determination will be explained further with the verse beginning "Of the Arudha and the Ascendant." || 1, 2 ||

**Regarding "Earth" etc.:** The specific results to be determined by the fact that the *Sutras* consist of those respective elements will be explained later with the verse "The Sutra which is related to an element..." || 3, 4 ||

**Regarding "Arudha" etc.:** The method for determining the General Sutra is stated in three verses. In this context, one should understand that a movable sign signifies life, a fixed sign signifies disease, and a dual sign signifies death. The specific details regarding their combinations are [hereby] displayed.

<header>Chapter Five</header>

### Chapter Five

If both indicators are in dual signs, or if one is in each type of sign, it is a "Disease Thread." This same logic should be applied when considering the "Amsaka Thread" <note>The Amsaka Thread refers to calculations based on the Ninth Divisional chart or Navamsha</note>. || 8 ||

In a Moveable sign, the sequence is Moveable, Fixed, and Dual. In a Fixed sign, it is Dual, Moveable, and Fixed. In a Dual sign, it is Fixed, Dual, and Moveable. These represent Life, Disease, and Death respectively. || 9 ||

When the lord of the *Arudha* <note>The sign rising at the time of a query</note> and the lord of the Ascendant are the same, or if there is friendship between them, it is known as a "Life Thread." If they are neutral toward each other, it becomes a "Disease Thread." || 10 ||

If these two lords are in a state of enmity, the thread indicates death. One should also count from the constellation (Nakshatra) of the Ascendant to the birth constellation of the querent. || 11 ||

Divide that count by three. If the remainder is one, it grants life. If the remainder is two, the thread indicates disease. If there is no remainder (zero), it indicates death. || 12 ||

If both the *Arudha* and the tenth house fall in "Lunar" signs, it is a "Life-giving Thread." If both fall in "Solar" signs, || 13 ||

it is then known as a "Death Thread." However, if one of these is Lunar and the other is Solar, it becomes a "Disease Thread." || 14 ||

---

Regarding the phrase "considering the Amsaka Thread," this is an extension of the rule where the Navamsha position of the Ascendant is used instead of the sign position; this is the only distinction. || 5-8 ||

**In a Moveable sign...** This is a summary of what was previously stated. || 9 ||

**Regarding the Arudha...** "Friendship" refers to mutual planetary friendship. The same logic applies to neutrality and enmity. If a doubt arises on how to decide when mutual friendship is absent, here is the instruction: If one is a friend and the other is also a friend, it is Life. If both are neutral, it is Life. If both are enemies, it is Disease. If one is neutral and the other is a friend, it is Life. If one is neutral and the other is neutral, it is Disease. If one is neutral and the other is an enemy, it is Death. If one is an enemy and the other is a friend, it is Disease. If one is an enemy and the other is neutral, it is Death. If both are enemies, it is also Death. Here, "Great Enemy" is included under Enemy, and "Great Friend" is included under Friend. || 10 ||

**One should count...** This refers to the constellation occupied by the precise degree of the rising Ascendant. || 11, 12 ||

**Regarding the Arudha...** The classification of signs into Solar and Lunar was explained by the sage Varahamihira in his work *Brihat Jataka* (His Own Hours): "Taurus, Cancer, Aries, Sagittarius, Gemini, and Capricorn are known as Night signs; they rise by the rear, except for Gemini. The remaining signs rise by the head and are powerful during the Day." In this context, the Night signs are considered "Lunar" and the Day signs are "Solar." <note>original: "गोजाश्विकर्कमिधुनास्समृगानिशाख्याः..." - Varahamihira's classification of zodiac signs by their strength during day or night.</note>

...Analysis. "Leo, Virgo, Libra, Scorpio, Aquarius, and Pisces are the Sun's signs. The other signs belong to the Moon; these are the day and night signs." This is shown elsewhere in the Anustubh meter. || 13, 14 ||

Flesh, bone, skin, veins, and hair constitute the Earth element in the bodies of living beings. Sweat, blood, urine, semen, and saliva are declared to be the Water element. || 20 ||

Hunger, thirst, laziness, sleep, and luster are Fire; the movement of the limbs is Air. Hatred, passion, delusion, fear, and old age are Space. || 21 ||

Thus, the bodies of all living creatures are composed of these five elements <note>The *Pancha Mahabhuta*: Earth, Water, Fire, Air, and Space</note>. Elsewhere, six "Sutras" <note>In this context, *Sutras* refer to specific divinatory strings or astrological rules used in the *Prashna* (inquiry) system</note> are mentioned, while others speak of only three. || 22 ||

Two Sutras governed by the lords of the Nakshatras <note>Lunar mansions</note> provide results for the present. Others say the General Sutra indicates the past, and the future is indicated by the remaining ones. || 23 ||

->From the Ascendant to the fifth,<-
->and from the ninth to the fifth,<-
->and from the ninth back to the Ascendant,<-
->the good and bad of the past, present, and future are known. || 24 ||<-

Regarding the phrase "In the bodies of living beings," etc.: If one argues that in phrases like "movement of the limbs is Air," only diseases related to the elemental portions are being discussed and not the elements themselves, then the interpretation that the limbs are the "seat of movement" is superior. This is because of the concluding statement: "Thus, the bodies of all living creatures are composed of the five elements." || 19 || <note>The numbering follows the manuscript's internal logic where commentary refers back to previous verses</note>

**Regarding "Flesh" etc.** || Earth means that which pertains to the ground. "Saliva" refers to the water of the mouth. Passion, hatred, delusion, and fear are modifications of the mind. By the word "old age," the destruction of youth is implied. Here, if the General Sutra <term>Samanya Sutra: a primary rule in this divination system</term> pertaining to the Earth element indicates disease or death, then the presence of disease in the flesh, bones, skin, veins, or hair of the querent should be understood. However, if it pertains to the Great Sutra <term>Maha Sutra</term>, then the existence of mental states like passion and hatred, or the decline of youth, should be predicted. Here, the latter half of the verse follows the reading of the *Ratnashikha*. Those who know the truth believe that this was composed and joined by the author himself to complete the meter.

**Regarding "Nakshatra" etc.** || The "others" refer to the Amsaka and Maha Sutras. By this, it is established that if the Sutra associated with a particular time indicates disease or death, then inauspiciousness must be predicted for that specific time. Another method for knowing the division of time is stated in the following verse. || 23 ||

**Regarding "From the Ascendant" etc.** || This is also used to determine the remaining time for the results of the Sutras. If one asks, "Since the Sutras do not have a position in the Zodiac signs <term>Rashi: the twelve signs of the zodiac</term>, how can the remaining time be understood through this?"—the answer lies in the positions of the planets that lord over those specific Sutras relative to the Ascendant...

# Prashnamarga
## Page 84

->The importance of the three threads is proclaimed here<-
->by others as being supreme;<-
->this is also mentioned in the *Kanthabharana*<-
->and the results thereof are stated here.<-
->The relationship between the Arudha <note>The sign corresponding to the direction the querent is facing</note> and the Ascendant,<-
->as well as their respective Navamshas <note>The 1/9th divisional chart</note><-
->and Dwadashamshas <note>The 1/12th divisional chart</note>,<-
->should be taken here as the "Arudha-Sphuta" <note>The precise calculated point of the Arudha</note>.<-
**|| 25 ||**

It should be understood that if [the planets] are situated in the first four houses, they grant results in the present; if in the four houses starting from the fifth, they grant results in the future; and if in the houses starting from the ninth, they grant results in the past. 

If one asks how the planets rule over the *Sutras* <note>threads/formulas</note>: Mercury is the lord of the *Samanya Sutra* (General Thread). Venus is the lord of the *Adhipati Sutra* (Lordship Thread). Mars is the lord of the *Amshaka Sutra* (Divisional Thread). Saturn is the lord of the *Nakshatra Sutra* (Asterismal Thread). Jupiter, however, is the lord of the *Maha Sutra* (Great Thread). 

If one asks for the authority on this: the principle is that the *Sutras* correspond to the five elements. Since the *Samanya Sutra* is of the nature of Earth, and Mercury is the lord of the Earth element (as stated in the *Hora* verse: <note>original: "shikhi-bhu-kha-payo-marud-gunanam"</note> "The qualities of Fire, Earth, Space, Water, and Air"), the lordship of the *Sutras* is effectively established. Thus, if Mercury is in the first four houses from the Ascendant, the results of the *Samanya Sutra* should be described as occurring in the present time, and so on. 

The conclusion is that the two methods of determining time mentioned in these two verses are to be applied as alternatives. One should also consider the consistency between them. These two verses, however, are not found in some manuscript copies. 

In the description of the results of the *Sutras*, when it is said that the result of the *Jiva Sutra* <note>The Living Thread</note> is long life, the term *Jiva Sutra* implies a predominance of that thread. That is to say, if the *Jiva Sutra* is the strongest among the five, long life is predicted. Even when considering results separately by time periods, if only one thread is connected to the past, but two threads each are connected to the other two times (present and future), then the presence of both auspicious and inauspicious results in the present and future must be pointed out. There is no rule that anyone, at any time, experiences only good or only bad. We observe the experience of happiness and sorrow simultaneously in different ways. One should give predictions after reflecting on this logic. Enough on this. **|| 24 ||**

**Regarding "Of the Sutras" (Verse 25):** *Kanthabharana* refers to the astrological text of that name. The method involving the *Arudha* and the Ascendant is the same as previously described for the *Samanya Sutra*. "Body-parts" <term>Anga-amsha: refers here to the Navamsha or 1/9th division</term>. "Sun-parts" <term>Aditya-amsha: refers to the Dwadashamsha or 1/12th division</term>. The instruction is that the determination of the different *Sutras* through the Navamsha and Dwadashamsha follows the same methodology as the *Samanya Sutra*. The *Arudha-Sphuta* (calculated Arudha) is derived by the method mentioned: "leaving aside the sign of the Ascendant-degree," for the purpose of knowing the Navamsha and Dwadashamsha here. **|| 25 ||**

# Chapter Six

->If the three threads relating to the<-
->Rising Sign, the Arudha, and their<-
->ninth and twelfth divisions indicate death,<-
->and if the lords of these two signs,<-
->along with the lords of the ninth and twelfth divisions,<-
->are mutual enemies,<-
->then due to the affliction of the Three-fold Calculation, the messenger’s omens, and the current time-period,<-
->even a person without disease may die. || 26 ||<-

->If these three threads indicate life,<-
->and the lords of the divisions are friendly,<-
->and if the Three-fold Calculation, the messenger’s omens, the time-period,<-
->and the vulnerable points are all auspicious,<-
->then even one on the verge of death will not die.<-
->If these threads are mixed,<-
->one survives only through ritual actions;<-
->if the afflictions are many, life is not easily sustained. || Thus || 27 ||<-

**Regarding "Arudha..."** || The first line is a restatement of what was said previously. "Of these two lords" refers to the lords of the Arudha <note>The sign obtained by counting as many signs from the house lord as the lord is from the house</note> and the Rising Sign (Ascendant). The terms <term>Arka and Divakara</term> <note>original: "arka-divākara-śabdau"</note> are used here as technical synonyms for the numbers nine and twelve <note>referring to the Navamsha and Dwadashamsha divisions</note>. Regarding **"the time-periods etc.,"** this refers to the specific planetary periods, sub-periods, and vulnerable "gap" points active in the birth chart at that time. The phrase "even without disease" connects to the result of the calculation. || 26 ||

**Regarding "Of the threads..."** || The section ending with "death" is the counterpart to the previous verse's "even a person without disease may die." **"Through ritual actions"** refers to performing atonements, charities, or healing rites. Here, in the **"three threads,"** there is a method seen where the threads are determined by the <term>ninth division (Navamsha)</term> and <term>twelfth division (Dwadashamsha)</term>, and the work is done by analyzing the friendship or enmity of their lords with the lords of the Arudha and the Rising Sign. This is one way of explaining the "Lord-thread." However, it is more appropriate to determine them through the presiding deities, as mentioned in the general description of the threads. The use of the word "if" in the verse "Arudha and Rising Sign" and the use of the word "and" in the middle of the verse "If these three threads indicate life" serve as indicators for this interpretation. This is indeed the traditional method of the lineage. || 27 ||

<page-num>97</page-num>
<header>Prashna Marga</header>

### Subject of this Verse

When the *Trisphuta* <note>A sensitive point calculated by adding the longitudes of the Ascendant, Moon, and Gulika</note> falls in Cancer, Scorpio, or Pisces, it is considered harmful in increasing order of severity. Within these signs, if it falls specifically in the constellations of Ashlesha, Jyeshtha, or Revati, the *Trisphuta* becomes particularly dangerous. || 28 ||

If the *Trisphuta* falls in the final *Navamsha* <note>A 9th-part subdivision of a sign, roughly 3 degrees and 20 minutes</note> of Cancer, Scorpio, or Pisces, it predicts the death of the querent within a year, a month, or a day, respectively. || 29 ||

### Another Text on this Subject

->From Aries, from Leo, and likewise from Sagittarius,<-
->the groups of four signs are respectively known as<-
->Creation, Preservation, and Destruction. From Aries,<-
->the constellations likewise follow this order.<-
->The nine subdivisions (Navamshas) function like the signs.<-
->In the junctions of signs and constellations known as "junction-points,"<-
->and in the 88th division and others,<-
->the *Trisphuta* is not auspicious. || 30 ||<-

**Regarding "This"**: Following the established order of the manual, the results of the *Trisphuta* are now being described.

**Regarding "Cancer, etc."**: In increasing order, Scorpio is more harmful than Cancer, and Pisces is more harmful than Scorpio. This means that within these signs, the later constellations and the later *Navamshas* carry a greater degree of affliction. "Final division" refers to the last *Navamsha*. If the *Trisphuta* stands in the fourth quarter of Ashlesha, Jyeshtha, or Revati, death should be predicted for the querent in a year, a month, or a day, respectively.

**Regarding "In this"**: This verse and the subsequent text from another source are not found in many manuscripts. The reality is that the author of the *Prashna Marga* <note>A 17th-century classical treatise on Horary astrology from Kerala</note> likely did not include this in his original composition. The "four signs starting from Aries" represent the Creation section. Moveable signs are signs of creation. The commentary explains that "Ashwini, Rohini, Punarvasu, etc., are the constellations of creation." Because this is useful for determining the *Trisphuta* and is found in some manuscript copies, it is included here.

**Regarding "From Aries"**: The four signs starting from Aries are the Creation section; from Leo, the Preservation section; from Sagittarius, the Destruction section. "From the Goat" means from Aries. "Signs" refers to both zodiac signs and lunar mansions (Nakshatras). The *Navamshas* are treated like the signs. This implies that the classification of Creation, etc., applies to the subdivisions as well. **"Destruction-sign"**: *Naja* means destruction. *Riksha* means sign or constellation. "Sign-junction" refers to *Gandanta* <note>The "knot-end" or spiritual/karmic junction between water and fire signs</note>. By the word "Destruction," one should understand the signs and constellations belonging to that section. The "88th division" is calculated from the birth division of the querent. By the word "and others," one should include the 22nd *Drekkana* <note>The 8th house subdivision associated with death</note> and the 8th house. || 30 ||

# Chapter Six

->If the Triple Point <note>Trisphuta: A sensitive point calculated by adding the longitudes of the Ascendant, Moon, and Gulika</note> falls in the final ninth-part <note>Navamsha: A 3°20' subdivision of a zodiac sign</note> of Cancer, it brings death within a year.<-
->If it falls in the final part of Scorpio, death occurs within a month;<-
->and if in the final part of Revati <note>The last of the 27 lunar mansions, located at the end of Pisces</note>, it brings death within a day. || 31 ||<-

->If the Triple Point is multiplied by nine and then by twelve <note>This refers to calculating the Dwadashamsha or twelfth-part position</note>, and it falls on a "junction of signs" <note>Rishi-Sandhi: The volatile borders between water and fire signs</note>,<-
->or if it falls on the birth star or its trines <note>The 10th or 19th stars from the birth star</note>,<-
->it certainly indicates death for the person asking the question. || 32 ||<-

->Between the sign and the ninth-part of the Triple Point, whichever is stronger determines the timing of the encounter with the birth Moon.<-
->However, if the Triple Point falls in the ninth-parts of Aries, Leo, or Sagittarius, it indicates a very long life. || 33 ||<-

->If the Triple Point is joined by Gulika <note>A mathematical point representing the son of Saturn, usually considered malefic</note> or other cruel planets, it is not auspicious.<-
->If the person born under that specific star is present in the house, a disease should be predicted for them.<-

**Regarding "Cancer etc."**: This verse repeats what was previously stated regarding the signs of Cancer, Scorpio, and Pisces. || 31 ||

**Regarding "The Triple Point"**: "By twelve" means multiplying by twelve. After multiplying by nine, all whole signs should be discarded. This means the degrees and minutes alone should be multiplied by twelve. The result is the "Ninth-Twelfth" position. "Junction of signs" specifically refers to the final ninth-parts of Cancer, Scorpio, and Pisces. The word "Birth" refers to the birth star <term>Nakshatra: The lunar mansion the moon occupied at birth</term>, and "its trines" refers to the secondary and tertiary birth stars. || 32 ||

**Regarding "Of the Triple Point"**: "Strength" refers to the greater mathematical power. "By that" means by the stronger sign. "Birth Moon" refers to the sign occupied by the Moon at the time of the person's birth. || 33 ||

**Regarding "Joined"**: This refers to the person asking the question or their relatives. "Born of that" means someone born under the star indicated by the Triple Point. The "Nine Evils" are mentioned as: "Vipa, Ushna, Vishti, Gandanta, Lata, Ekargala, Vaidhrita, Gulika, and Ahishiras—these nine flaws are progressively more powerful." **"Well"** <insert>referring to the calculation</insert> is an indirect reference to the creation of the segments, the creation of the stars, and the creation of the ninth-parts. || 34 ||

<note>The "Triple Sensitive Point" (Trishphuta) is a calculated longitude combining the positions of the Ascendant, the Moon, and Gulika (a mathematical point representing Saturn's son).</note> By the term <term>stars of danger</term><note>original: "vipat-pratyara-vadha-nakshatras"</note>, we refer to the 3rd, 5th, and 7th stars from the birth star. The order is changed here to highlight that the "Star of Destruction" (the 7th) carries the greatest defect, while the "Obstacle Star" (the 5th) is less severe. They "bring harm" during their respective major or minor planetary periods. Similarly, benefics "bring good." **Regarding the verse "Those..."**: Of this degree. <term>Multiplied by nine</term><note>original: "dhighna"</note>. <term>By the fixed number</term>, meaning twenty-seven. Divide and count the remainder starting from the star occupied by the Triple Sensitive Point. The star arrived at is the <term>Star of Death</term><note>original: "Mrityubham"</note>. Death of the querent may occur when a planet transits that star. Furthermore, the <term>Quadruple Sensitive Point</term><note>the Trishphuta plus the position of the Sun</note> and the star it occupies is also a Star of Death. Some say the Star of Death should be known from the ninth-division (Navamsha) of the Quadruple Sensitive Point, just as with the Triple Point. That should also be considered for the sake of consistency. If there is "subsidence of illness," meaning the querent recovers, then the Quadruple Sensitive Point "enters a relative," meaning the misfortune transfers to a kinsman of the querent born under that star. 

The procedure is as follows: Set down the Triple Sensitive Point, multiply by nine, discard the signs, double the degrees, multiply those and the minutes by nine, and divide by twenty-seven. The remaining number of degrees should be used for counting from the Triple Point's star. Note this detail: if there are remaining minutes, the next whole number after the degree count should be taken. This determination of the time of death is necessary only when the Triple Sensitive Point indicates the presence of a fatal defect. || 41 ||

One must also examine the relationship of these points to the "angles" <note>Kendras</note> and other houses. By multiplying the longitudes of the Ascendant, Moon, and Gulika by nine, one should respectively derive the <term>Prana, Deha, and Mrityu Sphutas</term> <note>the calculated points for Life-force, the Physical Body, and Death</note>. || 44 ||

If they are in mutual trines <note>120 degrees apart</note>, it means they share a <term>Trikona</term> relationship. <unclear>That word...</unclear>

# Prashna Marga
## Chapter on Disease and Death

->If these three <note>referring to the vital points: Prana, Deha, and Mrityu</note> are situated in mutual trines <note>1st, 5th, or 9th positions from each other</note>,<-
->they cause great disease.<-
->If they aspect each other, they cause delusion; if they are conjoined, they cause death,<-
->especially if this occurs within the trines of Cancer <note>the signs Cancer, Scorpio, and Pisces</note>. || 45 ||<-

->Multiply the Ascendant <term>Lagna: the rising sign</term> by five and add Gulika <term>Gulika: a mathematical point in the sky considered the son of Saturn</term> to find the Vital Breath <term>Prana</term>.<-
->Multiply the Moon by eight and add Gulika to find the Body <term>Deha</term>.<-
->Multiply the Sun by seven and add Gulika to find Death <term>Mrityu</term>.<-
->If the Vital Breath is numerically greater, there is disease; if the Body is greater, there is recovery;<-
->if Death is greater, then death occurs, especially when these points coincide with the birth star<-
->or the constellations of Ashlesha, Revati, or Jyeshtha <note>original: "Sarpa, Paushna, and Indra"</note>. || 46 ||<-

->When these three are added together, the resulting sign is found.<-
->If the Sun and other planets occupy that sign,<-
->one should predict calamities for the father and others; if Saturn and Rahu are there,<-
->predict the death of the querent.<-

---

<meta>Commentary follows</meta>

The term "trines" here refers specifically to the three Navamshas <note>the ninth-part divisions of a zodiac sign</note>. The connection is that if they are joined in the trines of Cancer, they certainly grant death. "Aspected" refers to a mutual aspectual relationship. "Conjoined" implies they occupy the same zodiacal sign. || 45 ||

**Regarding "The Ascendant..."**: This section explains another method for calculating the longitudes of Vital Breath <term>Prana</term>, Body <term>Deha</term>, and Death <term>Mrityu</term>, and the results derived from them. The author of *Prashna Marga* <note>a 17th-century Kerala treatise on horary astrology</note> previously described this method using the formula "From the Ascendant, Moon, and Gulika..." "Vasas" refers to the number eight. "Munis" refers to the number seven. The phrase "when it reaches the birth star" implies when the Death point <term>Mrityu-sphuta</term> coincides with it. The same applies to its position in the constellations of Ashlesha, Revati, or Jyeshtha. || 46 ||

**Regarding "When added..."**: This summarizes the upcoming teaching that "when the Sun and others are joined with the Triple-Longitude..." <term>Tri-sphuta: the sum of Prana, Deha, and Mrityu</term>. The connection is that if Saturn and Rahu <note>original: "Sa-manda-ahau"</note> are situated in the sign resulting from the Triple-Longitude, one should predict the death of the querent. Here, "Manda" refers to Saturn excluding Rahu. If Saturn <note>the son of the Sun</note> is in that Triple-Longitude sign, one should predict the destruction of the messenger sent by the querent. || 47 ||

->The astrologers say that if Mandi is in a favorable sign, it is auspicious; but if in the sign of Ketu <note>original: "shikhini," referring to the South Node of the Moon</note>,<-

**Regarding "Gatasuta" etc. ||** "Gatasuta" refers to the life-breaths <note>pranas</note> elapsed in the day. By the word "Prokshana," the number 562 is understood through the system of letter-numerals <note>Katapayadi system</note>. The procedure here is as follows: Set down the time elapsed in the day, convert the ghatikas <note>units of 24 minutes</note> into vighatikas by multiplying by 60, then multiply those by six to get the breaths <note>pranas</note>, and divide by "Prokshana" (562). The quotient gives the signs. The degrees and minutes should be derived as usual by multiplying the remainders by thirty, etc. This result should be subtracted from the longitude of Mandi. If the result falls in the birth star of the questioner, death is predicted for the questioner; if not, death should be predicted for whichever of the questioner's kinsmen was born under that star. The word "iti" <note>thus</note> signifies the conclusion of the quote from another text. || 48 ||

**Regarding "Samharagam" ||** "Samharagam" refers to the term "Trisphuta" found in the verse beginning with "Cancer, Scorpio, and Pisces." By the word "Samhara" <note>Destruction</note>, the signs and stars of that specific segment are to be taken. "Dehamshaka" <note>Body-division</note> refers to the 88th division <note>the 88th amsha</note>. By the word "etc." <note>adi</note>, the "Vipat" <note>danger</note> star and others are included. "By rule" means with certainty. || 49 ||

**Regarding "Srishti" <note>Creation</note> ||** "Decans etc." refers to the divisions of the Decan, Hora, Navamsha, Trimshamsha, Dwadashamsha, and the Sign itself. It is applied here that the fortune or misfortune of the six relatives—father and so on—should be told respectively by the lords of the signs occupied by the lords of those divisions. With good qualities, the benefics...

The destruction of four-legged animals (livestock) should be predicted; one should reflect on this using logic.

**Regarding the defects and inauspiciousness:** Weakness and other such states are the defects. Placement in favorable houses and such are the virtues. When the Moon is in a trine to the specific degree of the Tri-Sphuta, the presence of these omens indicates death. One should also consider if these omens occur in the house adjacent to the querent. || 56 — 60 ||
