# Chapter Six

Fever is a burning in the body and head, specifically caused by the Sun <note>original: "Ushnatejas," the one of hot radiance</note>. Diarrhea is caused by the Moon <note>original: "Sudhabhanu," the nectar-rayed one</note>, while a wound or ulcer is caused by Mars <note>original: "Bhumiputra," the son of the Earth</note>. || 61 ||

For Mercury <note>original: "Jna," the wise one</note>, there is a paralysis of speech and mind. For Jupiter <note>original: "Guru," the teacher</note>, there is a loss of control over the eyes, pain in all limbs, and mental confusion. || 62 ||

Swelling is caused by Venus <note>original: "Shukra"</note>. For Saturn <note>original: "Manda," the slow one</note>, there is a contraction of the hands and feet. For Rahu <note>original: "the ascending node"</note>, a fall is cited, and for Ketu <note>original: "the descending node"</note>, a disease or wound is mentioned. || 63 ||

If a patient's illness occurs when the planet is joined with the <term>Trisphuta</term> <note>A sensitive mathematical point in the horoscope calculated by adding the longitudes of the Ascendant, Moon, and Gulika</note>, or with the lord of the Trisphuta's division, then their death is certain. || 64 ||

By bringing the remaining time of the <term>Dasha</term> <note>planetary period</note> from the constellation of the Trisphuta, one should predict the results until the end of the year based on the remaining <term>Ghatikas</term> <note>units of time equal to 24 minutes</note>. || 65 ||

The lords of the constellations related to the Trisphuta, if they occupy unfavorable houses, or if their lords are debilitated, combust, or associated with <term>Mandi</term> <note>a malefic mathematical point</note>, they bestow inauspicious results. || 66 ||

In this matter of calculating the planetary periods for a query, there is another school of thought. That too is written here:

->From the constellation of the query and the Trisphuta, calculate the planetary periods according to the rules.<-
->Also from Mandi, in reverse order,<-
->using the elapsed time in units of measure.<-
->Among these three methods, one should be selected.<-

**Regarding "Fever" etc.!!** "Joined with" means occurring in conjunction with a planet. In the absence of that, it refers to the lord of the division. One should understand that the diseases mentioned in the verses starting with "Fever in the head" are generally what follow. || 61–64 ||

**Regarding "The Period" !!** This is a translation of two verses from another text starting with "By the remaining units of the Trisphuta." One should predict the results until the end of the year by calculating the periods from the remaining units of the <term>Trisphuta constellation</term>. "Lords of the root" refers to the lords of the constellations of "Execution," "Obstacle," and "Misfortune" <note>Vadha, Pratyari, and Vipat—specific unfavorable stars in the 27-star system</note>. || 65, 66 ||

**Regarding "In this matter" !!** That refers to the alternative school of thought.

**Regarding "The Query" !!** "In reverse from Mandi" means the planetary period should be calculated using the units of time already elapsed in the constellation where Mandi is located. Furthermore, the planetary period of the constellation lord should be applied below that. This is what is explained by the word "elapsed." In a query regarding auspicious or inauspicious matters, one of the three mentioned periods should be chosen according to what is appropriate. Whether for a yearly or monthly [prediction]...

# Now begins the Seventh Chapter

### Now, the results of the Ashtamangala <note>A specialized numerological divination using 108 cowrie shells</note> are described.

> One should indicate the past results from the object placed on the left, the present from the middle, and the future results from the object on the right. || 1 ||
> The lower, middle, and upper parts of the body correspond to the right, middle, and left positions respectively. If an even number appears in a body part, one should predict a disease associated with the specific planet ruling that part. || 2 ||

Inquiry <term>Prashna: A branch of astrology where a chart is cast for the moment a question is asked</term> is of two types: for knowing the results of a year, and for knowing the results of a month. In the former, the years of the planetary period <note>Dasha</note> should be multiplied by three to arrive at the number of days. For example, the Sun's period would be 18 days <note>Original: 6 years x 3 = 18</note>, and so on. In the second type (monthly), the years of the planetary period should be multiplied by four to determine the days. For example, Venus would be 5 days, and so on. The phrase "derived from the Moon" suggests an alternative view: that the periods should be calculated only from the Moon's longitude at the time of inquiry, and not from the "Tri-sphuta" or "Mandi-sphuta" <note>Calculated sensitive points in the horoscope</note>. This is the established doctrine. || 67 ||

->Thus ends the Sixth Chapter of Prashna Marga.<-

---

**Now:** Following the sequence of topics starting from the emergence of the query, and after describing the results of the "Tri-sphuta" <note>The sum of the longitudes of the Ascendant, Moon, and Gulika</note>, the results of the Ashtamangala are now described in their proper order.

**From the left:** "From the left" means from the north, as the Ashtamangala ritual must be performed facing East. If the numbers are arranged in units, tens, and hundreds places, then the "left" refers to the digit in the hundreds place. || 1 ||

**The lower:** "Right and so on" refers to the Right, Middle, and Left. The specific diseases associated with the planets will be explained later.

**In the positions:** "The Sun and others" refers to the verses beginning with "Arka" <note>Sun</note>. "The Banner and others" refers to the sequence starting with "Dhvaja" (Banner) and "Dhuma" (Smoke). "The Eagle and others" refers to the sequence of "Tarkshya" (Eagle) and "Marjara" (Cat). The five elements are shown in the verse "Dhvaja and Simha are Earth," etc.

# Chapter Seven

### The Distribution of Planets and Elements

When the remainders of one or more are found in the three positions, the Sun and other planets, the Banner and other symbols, the Eagle and other creatures, and the five elements follow in sequence. (3)

The Sun, Mars, Jupiter, Mercury, Venus, Saturn, the Moon, and Rahu <note>The ascending node of the Moon</note> are the rulers in order. The symbols are the Banner, Smoke, Lion, Dog, Horse, Donkey, Elephant, and Crow. (4)

The creatures are the Eagle, Cat, Lion, Dog, Snake, Rat, Elephant, and Bull. The Banner and the Lion are considered of the Earth element; the Elephant and the Bull are of the Water element. (5)

Smoke is Fire; the Donkey is Air; the Dog and the Crow are of the nature of Ether <note>The celestial space or void</note>. (6)

### The Effects of the Planets

The Sun brings the attainment of desired objects, fame, victory, honor from kings, and respect from assemblies, districts, and villages. (7)

Mars causes fear from thieves, kings, weapons, and fire, as well as from the deities Skanda and Bhairava. It brings quarrels, fever, and diseases of the bile, blood, veins, and eyes. (8)

Jupiter brings auspicious arrivals born of the grace of gurus, deities, and priests. It grants fine silk, gold, elephants, horses, and the birth of children. (9)

Mercury <note>Literally "Born of the Cold-Rayed One" (the Moon)</note> causes fear from dogs, cows, and deer, the anger of Vishnu, and ailments like scabies, skin diseases, and fevers resulting from the imbalance of the three humors. (10)

Venus <note>Literally "Son of Bhrigu"</note> brings the acquisition of ornaments, clothes, and beds, the happiness of women, and delicious food. It grants gains from agriculture, cows, and buffaloes. (11)

---

<margin>Note on interpretation</margin> By the number located in the northern part <note>the left side</note>, one should understand the planets, the animal origins (Yonis) such as the Banner, the Eagle, and the specific elements, and then predict the results for the **past** as will be described. Similarly, by the middle number, predict for the **present**; and by the southern <note>right side</note> number, predict for the **future**. (2-6)

**Regarding "Desired Objects":** Here, although "the Moon" is mentioned generally in the planetary assignment, the specific mention of the "Full Moon" in the description of results implies that if the Moon is waning on the day of the inquiry, the experience of happiness and prosperity will not be complete. Thus, the Teacher <note>the author of the original treatise</note> indicates that beyond the mere calculation of numbers in the *Ashtamangala* <note>an eight-fold divination system</note>, the specific strength or weakness of the ruling planets must be considered to determine the results. This is only logical; otherwise, if predictions were made solely by numbers, the specific assignment of planets like the Sun and others would be useless. Therefore, based on the strength or weakness of the planets obtained from those numbers, and their favorable or unfavorable positions, one must skillfully apply the specified results.

### **On Health and Prosperity**

After directing the results of the eight planets ending with Rahu, their agency in producing these results was established. However, this is not the case for the Banner and the other symbolic omens. Therefore, these do not have the "doership" or agency of results like the planets do. Rather, they are merely indicators <note>suggesting that these omens are signs of fate rather than active causes</note> of the acquisition of their respective specified results. For this very reason, in the consideration of results spoken of regarding planets, one must investigate the strength and weakness of the planets who are the "doers," and deliberate on specifics such as their favorable or unfavorable positions. Among the four omens, any one may be taken as the sign. To indicate this, the cat eating the rat is mentioned first, and the seizing of a snake by a partridge or hawk is mentioned second. In the phrase "seizing of a rabbit," the word "dog" carries over from the previous context, meaning the seizing of a rabbit by a dog. The word "or" <note>original: "vā"</note> expresses an alternative, clarifying that there is no strict requirement for the sequence of these omens. If these omens are actually seen by the inquirer, the severity of the ill-fortune is understood to be greater. <note>Commentary on verses 23–25</note>

### Chapter Seven

The lunar days <note>Sanskrit: tithis</note> starting from the first day of the bright fortnight are determined by the remainder of the "Sāra" <note>A technical numerical code used in this system</note>. The stars and weekdays are determined from the remainder of "Sapta" (seven), and the Zodiac signs from the remainder of "Priya" <note>Another numerical code</note>. || 33 ||

The nine planets are to be known from the remainder after dividing by nine. Similarly, the five elements <note>Earth, Water, Fire, Air, and Ether</note> are known from the remainder after dividing by five. || 34 ||

The Zodiac sign of the querent <note>the person asking the question</note> and their birth stars are determined; if these align [unfavorably] here, then certain misfortune for the querent must be predicted. || 35 ||

If the combinations of these lunar days and other factors result in "Death-dealing" <note>Mrityu</note> or "Burnt" <note>Dagdha</note> yogas, the practitioner should predict calamity for the querent. If "Nectar" <note>Sudha</note> and other auspicious combinations arise, the results are good. || 36 ||

If the numbers in all three positions <note>Left, Middle, and Right piles of shells</note> are even, death will occur. If the numbers in the Left and Middle positions are even, a great illness follows. || 37 ||

<note>Commentary:</note> The words *Nīla*, *Sāra*, and *Priya* represent specific numerical values based on their syllables. In the two verses starting with "The Zodiac sign of the querent," the method for declaring results based on these is explained. The method for determining "Death-dealing" combinations was previously shown in the section on determining auspicious and inauspicious time.

**Regarding "In all three positions"**: Some raise a doubt regarding the lack of practical application for the statement "in the Left and Middle." They argue that since one starts with 108 cowrie shells <term>Varāṭikā: small shells used as counters or currency</term> and divides them into three piles, then removes multiples of eight from each, the remaining total must be a multiple of four (4, 12, or 20). Therefore, they claim it is impossible to have even numbers in the Left and Middle while having an odd number in the Right.

To this, some experts offer this resolution: if the *sum* of the numbers in the Left and Middle positions is even, a "great illness" is the result; this would happen even if both the Left and Middle were odd. However, this is actually a flawed conclusion <note>Sanskrit: apasiddhānta</note>. According to the rule "when odd numbers remain," odd numbers are naturally auspicious.

Others argue: "This is not a flawed conclusion. The auspiciousness of odd numbers and the inauspiciousness of even numbers is established by scriptural injunction. Therefore, this specific rule should also be accepted as an injunction."

Yet others interpret it to mean that if there is an even number in *either* the Left or the Middle position, a great illness is the result. The text says "in the Left and Middle," not "in *both* the Left and Middle." They believe it is better to interpret it as "in one or the other" to ensure the rule has a practical application, rather than assuming "both" and making the rule impossible to fulfill.

Finally, others say that for the sake of the comprehensiveness of the science, defining characteristics even for impossible scenarios is a traditional scholarly practice; therefore, there is no harm. This is why descriptions of "rain-god omens" <note>Parjanya-lakṣaṇa</note> are given even when they don't occur. The great teacher Varāhamihira <note>A famous 6th-century Indian astronomer and polymath</note> also explicitly supports this view. Because...

> Multiply the middle number and divide it by the auspicious days.
> If the remainder is zero, the querent <note>the person asking the question</note> faces death; if the remainder is two, there is gain of children and cattle. || 38 ||
> If the remainder is four, there is loss of kinsmen; if six, the querent suffers from disease.

> Having set down three places, multiply the left position by two, the middle by three,

> add the numbers for *Chalangam* (3) and *Daivatam* (18). In the dark fortnight <note>Krishna Paksha, the waning moon</note>, add these and divide by *Bhuja* (28).
> When Jupiter is in the resulting sign, and the remainder is multiplied by *Priyanaga* (78) and *Nata* (60),

The author says: "I have calculated the retrogressions and other movements according to the ancient scriptures. How can Mercury and Venus ever be in the fourth house from the Sun?" Regarding this, the solution offered by some—that due to differences in time, Mercury and Venus could indeed be in the fourth sign from the Sun—will never find a place in the minds of mathematicians skilled in logic. Therefore, enough of this deliberation on a subject that cannot withstand scrutiny; I shall stop here. || 37 ||

**Regarding the verse "Multiply the number..."** In the case of odd numbers, although even numbers generally indicate inauspiciousness, specific results are mentioned for each even remainder. For odd numbers, because such distinctions are absent, <unclear>the statement is general</unclear>. Even though the same number might be obtained through multiplication and division as before, the process is started because a difference in the number occurs when the remainder is odd. In reality, since no specific results are prescribed there, it is proper to say the process is started merely for the sake of variety. The words "Auspicious" and "Day" <note>Shubha and Dina</note> refer to numbers derived from the <term>Katapayadi system</term> <note>An ancient Indian alphabetic code where letters represent numbers</note>. Even if the number five were used instead of forty-five as the multiplier, the result would not change, and the work would be simpler. However, some teachers accept this more laborious process because it develops the intellect of the student. Therefore, it should be noted that teachers demonstrate this kind of procedural sequence in other places as well. Others believe that "the middle number" refers to the middle digit when three places (units, tens, hundreds) are imagined, and the number formed by the tens place is what is used here. Thus, it should be understood that the number will always be greater than ten.

**Regarding the verse "Having set down..."** 1. *Chalangam* (3), 2. *Daivatam* (18), 3. *Bhuja* (28), 4. *Priya* (2), 5. *Naga* (8), 6. *Nata* (60), 7. *Veda* (4)—these words represent numbers based on the letter-code. <term>This is for calculating the precise longitudes of Saturn and Jupiter at the time of death</term>. The meaning is that in a yearly inquiry, if Saturn reaches the calculated longitude and Jupiter is in the resulting sign within a year (or within a month for a monthly inquiry), then the death of the querent will certainly occur. || 40-42 ||

# Now begins the Eighth Chapter

---

Now, the results based on the Arudha <note>The "Arudha" is the zodiac sign corresponding to the direction the questioner is facing or a gold token placed on the zodiac chart</note> and other factors are stated.

The Arudha, the Rising Sign <note>Udayalagna</note>, the Navamsha <note>The ninth-part subdivision of a sign</note> of the Rising Sign, the Chatra <note>The "Umbrella" sign, a symbolic protective sign calculated from the Sun's position</note>, the sign corresponding to the limb touched <note>Sprishtanga</note>, and the sign occupied by the Moon—these six signs are to be considered in the work of divination. || 1 ||

**The Eight Auspicious Symbols**: One who has thoroughly studied the science of astrology should indicate all results in accordance with that science. If one predicts results with pride, thinking "all results predicted by me based on the strength of the scientific tenets will surely come true," they will become an object of ridicule. The second half of the verse explains that the truth of the predicted result does not come from pride. The science has many facets; the realization of the true path depends entirely on the grace of the Preceptor <note>Guru</note> and the favor of the Divine. Furthermore, the occurrence of omens <note>Upashruti</note> and the signs of the moment, their comprehension, and the determination of results based on them follow the path of truth only through the Preceptor's grace and Divine favor—this is the secret. In the process of bringing forth the Eight Auspicious Symbols, the method of determining results was told through the lunar day <note>Tithi</note>, the day of the week <note>Vara</note>, the asterism <note>Tara</note>, and the zodiac signs. It was not done through the nine planets or the five elements. The capacity of planets to give auspicious or inauspicious results is frequently mentioned; as for the elements, it is shown in this very chapter that "among the elements, the Earth is auspicious," etc. The verse "If there are even numbers in all three places..." is not seen in some manuscripts. If following those manuscripts, there is no room for the aforementioned doubts or for following complex and difficult paths to resolve them; those who follow such versions should remain satisfied with that. || 43 ||

->Thus ends the Seventh Chapter in the Prashnamarga.<-

**Regarding "Of these" (Verse 2):** This refers to the six factors previously mentioned. Regarding the "auspicious or inauspicious states," the cause and effect here are not intended to be strictly sequential. The layout follows the requirements of the poetic meter. In a beneficial combination, the "auspicious state" arises from the ripening of previous good karma <note>original: "shubha-karma-vipaka"</note>, leading to health and other blessings. The same logic applies elsewhere. There is an alternative reading: "due to the strength of the inauspicious or auspicious state." This means that in a mixture of good and bad combinations, the prediction should be made based on whichever influence—the auspicious or the inauspicious—is stronger. Determining results based on the prevailing strength in a mixed situation is both logically sound and well-established; this principle should be applied everywhere. || 2 ||

**Regarding "Whichever bodily sign" (Verse 3):** "In that limb" refers to the specific body part associated with that zodiac sign, according to the rule: "The head, face, etc., are the limbs of Time." <note>This refers to the 'Kalapurusha' concept where Aries is the head, Taurus the face, etc.</note> || 3 ||

**Regarding "Arudha" (Verses 4-5):** 1. The lord of the Arudha, 2. the lord of the Ascendant <term>Udaya-lagna-adhipa: the ruler of the rising sign at the time of the question</term>, 3. the Moon, and 4. the Sun—if these four and the lords of the signs they occupy are fully empowered, one should predict a state of complete prosperity in wealth, progeny, and so on for the consultant <term>Prichchaka: the person asking the astrological question</term>. If they are weak, a state devoid of wealth and progeny is indicated. If they have entered their signs of fall <note>Debilitation</note> or the divisions of enemy planets, then one must also predict misfortunes such as trouble from enemies and disease. || 5 ||

**Regarding "Lord of the Arudha":** The weakness of the lord of the Arudha and the strength of the lord of the eighth house <note>original: "ashtama-adhipa"</note> at the time—

# Chapter Eight

->When the Lord of the Arudha <note>The sign rising at the time of a query</note> and the Lord of the Benefic sign<-
->possess strength, while the Lords of the sixth, eighth, and twelfth houses<-
->are devoid of strength,<-
->then comes the arrival of all manner of good fortune. (6)<-

There are two sets of seven states <term>Avasthas: developmental stages of a planet that determine its potency</term> for the planets; similarly,
the state of the petitioner <note>The person asking the astrological question</note> should be considered, as stated in other authoritative scriptures. (7)

In neutral, friendly, own, Moolatrikona <note>a specific favorable zone within a sign</note>, exaltation, enemy, and debilitation signs,
the seven states of the planets occur, starting from "Extreme Infancy" and so on, in sequence. (8)

Extreme Infant, Infant, Youth, Young Adult, King,
Old, and Dead—these are the conditions in order, based on their positional differences. (9)

A planet that has just risen from the Sun <note>emerged from combustion</note> is an "Extreme Infant."
For seven days it remains an "Infant," and after that, it becomes a "Youth." (10)

It is a "Young Adult" at the start of retrograde motion, and a "King" while moving retrograde.
When approaching its setting <note>becoming obscured by the Sun's light</note> it is "Old," and when its rays are lost in the Sun, it is "Dead." (11)

Thus, the two-fold states of the planets are described for the sake of the petitioners.
Among the Lords of the Arudha, the Ascendant, and the Chatra <note>an auxiliary mathematical point in Prashna</note>, the period <term>Dasha</term> of the strongest one prevails. (12)

---

In the past, present, or future, the possibility of calamity should be predicted [based on these strengths]. The strength of the Lord of the Arudha and the Lord of Fortune <note>9th house Lord</note>, combined with the weakness of the Lords of the 6th, 8th, and 12th houses, indicates the time for the arrival of all prosperity. (6)

**Regarding the States:** The seven states of planets, from Extreme Infancy to Death, occur sequentially based on their placement in seven types of signs, from neutral to debilitated. One must also determine the seven-fold states by another method. "Just risen from the Sun" means for about one day after the end of its combustion <note>original: "maudhya-avasana"</note>. "After that" means prior to the start of retrograde motion. The "start of retrograde" is the beginning of the decrease in speed. "Approaching its setting" refers to roughly seven days before the start of combustion. (7-11)

**Thus:** "Among the Lords" refers to the three specific controllers mentioned. This is a grammatical selection. "Of the strongest" means the one with the most power. In this world, it is well known that an "Extreme Infant" lacks even the ability to speak; an "Infant" is attached to play; a "Youth" is focused on the pursuit of knowledge; a "Young Adult" is attached to women; a "King" has an abundance of attendants; and an "Old" person... <note>The text cuts off here, likely describing the inability to perform actions</note>

# Prashna Marga
## The Path of Inquiry

The natural characteristics of the various stages of life—such as infancy and the rest—which are well-known in this world, <note>The text refers to the 'Avastas' or states of planets which mirror human life stages.</note> including the youth's **attachment to women** <unclear>and so forth</unclear>, are considered to be the same as the planetary periods (*Dashas*) in this context. (13)

If the planet ruling the day of the inquiry is situated in its sign of exaltation <note>The sign where a planet is at its maximum strength.</note> or its exaltation subdivision (*Amsha*), or if the Ascendant of the inquiry (*Arudha*) happens to be the exaltation sign of that day-lord, then the practitioner should predict health and long life for the querent. If the opposite is true, death must be predicted. (14)

If the Ascendant falls in **Leo**, the diseases will involve the stomach and eyes, soul-agony, or illnesses caused by heat. In **Cancer**, there will be diseases of the chest, tongue, and mouth, as well as loss of appetite and water-borne diseases (edema). (15)

In the signs of **Mars** (Aries and Scorpio), there will be diseases of the head and eyes, fevers, ulcers, and scabies. In the signs of **Mercury** (Gemini and Virgo), there will be obstructions of the breath (asthma), and diseases of the nose and skin. (16)

When the Ascendant is in a sign of **Jupiter** (Sagittarius and Pisces), there will be mental confusion and ear ailments. In a sign of **Venus** (Taurus and Libra), there will be diseases of the generative organs, loss of appetite, and water-related maladies. (17)

In the signs of **Saturn** (Capricorn and Aquarius), one should predict mental confusion, physical exhaustion, and impaired excretion. If these signs are associated with or aspected by **Rahu** (the Serpent), one should also mention scabies and intense itching. (18)

These results should be stated as a certainty only when the Ascendant is joined by malefic planets. (19)

<margin>Regarding the power and states: for a dead person, fainting and so forth. When there is a difference in the two types of states, a choice or a combination of both should be ordered according to logic. These are the "natural characteristics" mentioned in the description of the states.</margin>

**Regarding "Exaltation" (Verse 14):** The positioning of the lord of the day within its exaltation sign or subdivision, or the Ascendant being the exaltation sign of the day-lord, bestows health and other benefits. Conversely, the lord of the day being in its sign of fall (debilitation) or the Ascendant being the sign of its fall indicates death.

**Regarding "Leo" (Verses 15-19):** Here, specific diseases are shown based on the rising sign (*Arudha*). Since Rahu does not own a sign, the diseases of scabies and itching are mentioned when Rahu aspects or joins the sign-lord. If Rahu is present, the diseases of that specific sign plus the itching/scabies must be predicted. One might argue: "Since an Ascendant is always present, does this mean every inquiry must result in a disease, even for a healthy person?" This is not so. The phrase **"When the Ascendant is joined by malefic planets"** means these results occur by rule only when malefics are present. If a healthy person asks a question and there is no malefic influence, the disease should not be predicted. The essence is that even in a question about health, these diseases only manifest if malefics are involved.

# Chapter Eight

->The combination of the signs and divisional charts of the Arudha and the Rising Sign with the sign and divisional chart of Mandi causes disease; many such combinations cause death. || 20 ||<-

->From the Pitcher, downward from the corner of Shiva;<-
->From the Night-walker, the body of the Ocean moving upward;<-
->From the End of the Vedas, the tip of the Fire;<-
->From the corner of the Wind, for the others, it is horizontal. || 21 ||<-

---

Regarding the previous verses ending in the seventh case <note>referring to Sanskrit grammatical locative case</note>, some teachers claim that this should only be predicted when there is a combination with malefic planets. That is not correct. Because if that were the rule, the word "this" would be unnecessary, and the sentence structure would be forced. || 15–19 ||

**Regarding "Arudha" etc.!!** The combination of the degrees of the Arudha and the Rising Sign refers to these four: 1. The Arudha sign, 2. The Rising sign <term>Udaya Lagna: the sign rising on the eastern horizon at birth</term>, 3. The Arudha <term>Navamsha: the 1/9th divisional chart used for fine-tuning predictions</term>, and 4. The Rising sign's Navamsha. The "combination" refers to the connection of these four with the sign and Navamsha of Mandi <note>Mandi is a "shadow planet" or mathematical point considered inauspicious in Vedic astrology</note>. A combination of many of these indicates disease. Here, the Arudha Navamsha should be understood through the "Gold Placement" <note>Svarnasthilya: a specific ritual or divinatory method of placing gold to determine a point</note>, not by the calculated Arudha longitude. This is because the text does not explicitly say "take the calculated Arudha" here. The knowledge of the "Gold Navamsha" should be performed according to the verse that follows. || 20 ||

**Regarding "The Pitcher" etc.!!** "The Pitcher" <note>Kalasha</note> refers to Aries, Gemini, and Leo. "The Body of the Ocean" <note>Sindhukaya</note> refers to Libra, Sagittarius, and Aquarius. "From the End of the Vedas" <note>Vedanta</note> refers to Cancer, Scorpio, and Virgo—these are to be understood by <term>Aksharasankhya: a system of coding numbers into letters</term>. Having divided one sign into nine parts, the Navamsha of that segment where the gold was placed should be taken. Among Aries, Gemini, and Leo, the counting of segments should be done downward starting from the Northeast corner <note>the corner of Shiva</note>. Similarly, for Libra and the others, it should be taken from the Southwest corner <note>the corner of the Night-walker/Demon</note> as stated. 

In this verse, the words "Pitcher" and "Body of the Ocean" are in the nominative case, "End of the Vedas" is in the ablative, and "Others" is in the locative; thus, there is a break in grammatical consistency <note>the author is critiquing the poetic quality of the verse</note>. This must be tolerated because the teacher's primary intention was to explain the Navamsha. Even with this inconsistency, there is no lack of clarity. Rhetoricians have stated clearly that it is impossible to completely avoid poetic flaws everywhere. The connection of the words must be inferred somehow by adding appropriate words. 

In reality, this verse—which contains a corrupted reading that obstructs the intended meaning—was likely not composed by the original Teacher. Rather, it was interpolated <insert>inserted later</insert> by some poor poet. This is why it is not seen in many ancient manuscripts. Therefore, in the phrase "take the calculated Arudha here," it is more appropriate to interpret the word "here" as excluding the knowledge of the Arudha Navamsha. One should not object that this makes the calculation of the "Gold Navamsha" useless. We accept that objection. If one asks, "Then what is the status of the traditional necessity of knowing the Gold Navamsha?" the truth is that the tradition is its own authority. Or rather, let the scholars search for a way to justify it. Enough of this. || 21 ||

# Prashna Marga
### Page 112

If the *Gandanta* <note>A "junction point" or spiritual knot, specifically the transition between water and fire signs, considered highly inauspicious</note> degrees of either the *Arudha* <note>The zodiac sign corresponding to the direction the questioner is facing or a chosen point of focus</note> or the Ascendant are occupied by malefic planets, or if such degrees rise in the 8th house from the *Arudha*, death is likely to occur. || 22 ||

If the *Arudha* falls in Pisces and is aspected by malefic planets, the questioner is "lame" <note>Metaphorically stuck or physically impaired</note>. If the *Arudha* is Scorpio or Cancer, one should predict a fall into a well or similar pit. || 23 ||

One should arrange the signs on the ground starting from the East, as previously instructed. Trees and other features should be indicated based on the strength of the planets occupying the *Kendras* <note>The four "angles" or pivot houses: 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th</note>. || 24 ||

Mountains, trees, plantains, thorny bushes,
Bamboo, betel nut, and coconut;
Forests of palmyra trees—
These are assigned to the signs according to their respective lords. || 25 ||

**Regarding "Arudha" etc.** || If the *Gandanta* occurs in the calculated point of the *Arudha*, the Ascendant, or the 8th house, death must be predicted. In this context, the *Swarna-Navamsha* <note>A specific 1/9th division of a sign used for fine-tuning predictions</note> should be taken. Some authorities suggest that for the 8th house, one should calculate the specific *Navamsha* degree corresponding to the degree of the Ascendant. || 22 ||

**Regarding "Arudha" etc.** || The phrase "aspected by malefics" applies to both Scorpio and Cancer in this context. || 23 ||

**Regarding "From the East" etc.** || Even if no planets are present in the *Kendras*, if the signs occupying those angles are strong, one should predict the presence of trees associated with those signs in the respective directions. Furthermore, if planets are strong even when located outside the *Kendras*, the presence of trees should be understood based on the sign they occupy and their planetary lordship. The strength of the signs and planets (such as being in an exaltation sign) should be determined as stated. 

The arrangement follows the method of Varahamihira <note>A famous 6th-century Indian astronomer and polymath</note>: "Starting from the East, Aries and the following signs are placed two by two, with the dual signs in the corners." This means the 2nd house from the *Arudha* is East, the 3rd is Southeast, and so on. 

The specific characteristics of signs and planets will be explained shortly. The author of *Ratnashilaka*, however, composed a half-verse—"I shall now describe the trees according to the signs and planets"—simply to complete the meter of the poem. We do not know why he did this. The primary intent of the great teachers is to explain the subject matter, not merely to fulfill poetic meter. This path is well-trodden in many scientific treatises. 

A pause at the half-verse is accepted even in the Vedas. Therefore, even in the recitation of the *Samhitas*, the text is heard with a break at the end of both halves. A continuous reading is not accepted. Thus, in our view, it is not necessary to compose half-verses or transform prose into verse just to fill a meter. On this matter, the learned scholars who follow the established systems of the Shastras are the final authority. || 24 ||

**Regarding "Mountains" etc.** || "Forests" refers to groves, clusters, or wooded areas. || 25 ||

# Chapter Eight

->If the rising sign faces upward, it brings prosperity and growth to the querent.<-
->If it faces downward, it leads to decline; this is declared in the *Krishniya* and other works. || 26 ||<-

->If the rising sign or the *Hora* <note>A division of a sign equal to fifteen degrees, or half a sign</note> faces upward<-
->during a query, it brings success to the person.<-
->The others <note>those facing downward or sideways</note> should be known as fruitless,<-
->unless they are associated with or aspected by benefics. || 27 ||<-

->If the Ascendant faces upward, those undergoing childbirth,<-
->traveling, or commencing a task, or those asking a question,<-
->will experience great elevation in wealth, valor, fame,<-
->and status.<-
->If the rising sign faces downward, one will be deprived of all<-
->wealth and such; one might even be abandoned by friends<-
->and the querent may fall from a vehicle or high place. || 28 ||<-

**Regarding "of the Arudha"**: This is demonstrated by two verses from the text *Krishniya* <note>An ancient South Indian treatise on Horary astrology</note> and others. By the statement "Those freed by the Sun and others are upward, downward, or sideways-facing," one should understand the distinction between the upward-facing, downward-facing, and sideways-facing nature of the zodiac signs. || 26 ||

**Regarding "If upward-facing"**: For a "person"—here the gender is not intended to be specific <note>The term 'nara' or man is used generically for any human querent</note>. "Success" means the achievement of the desired goal. "The others" refers to the downward-facing and sideways-facing *Horas*. Even if they are downward or sideways, [success may occur] if they are associated with or aspected by benefics. || 27 ||

**Regarding "In the upward-facing"**: "Departed" means one who has set out while the sign was facing upward. The terms "those commencing a task" and "those asking" are not to be connected as adjective and noun in a restricted grammatical agreement <term>Samanadhikaranya: coordinate relation where words refer to the same thing</term>. If they were, the definition would fail to apply to questions other than birth, travel, or commencement of work, or to natal horoscopy. In the second half of the verse, the word "querent" should be taken to imply the newborn and others, and the word "Arudha" should be taken to imply the Ascendant; interpreting them in a non-coordinate relation <term>Vaiyadhikaranya: words in different grammatical cases or referring to different subjects</term> is not a great difficulty. Therefore, rather than a narrow definition, a broader application is better; since there is no logical reason for restriction, the non-coordinate interpretation is superior. "Elevation of status" for an ordinary man means becoming a royal minister and the like; for a crown prince, it means becoming a King. As an opposite to the meaning of the fourth line <note>which mentions falling and loss</note>, one should predict the gain of kinsmen and the acquisition of vehicles in the first half. || 28 ||

->Between "Deha" and "Mrityu," it leads to disease; between "Prana" and "Mrityu," it causes delusion. || 39 ||<-

->If the divisions <note>Vargas</note> of the waning Moon, Saturn, Mars, or the Sun<-
->are situated in the Ascendant, they bring death, disease, loss of wealth, and other evils<-
->to the petitioner. If these belong to Mercury,<-
->where is the strength of intellect? But if they belong to the full Moon,<-
->Venus, or Jupiter,<-
->they bring health, wealth, children,<-
->and the attainment of desired goals. || 40 ||<-

When [the gold piece] is placed in the middle of the flowers and grains and is facing downwards, it should be interpreted through logic. Regarding the sloping toward the East and other directions: the four results starting with long life follow in order. "Naisvam" means poverty. There is no difference in result based on the specific variations of the corners. || 36 ||

**Regarding this** || By the word "Ascendant and others" <note>Lagnadi</note>, the inclusion of Gulika, the Moon, Prana, and others is intended. ||

**Regarding Mandi**... The four starting with Gulika in Moveable signs grant life and health. In the case of the conjunction of the three, the Navamsha is not to be considered. The results for Prana and others brought by the "Lagna and Moon" method are different; this, however, is another matter entirely. || 37—39 ||

**Regarding the waning Moon**... "Divisions" <note>Vargas</note> refers to the signs and other subdivisions. "Ascendant" <note>Vilagna</note> refers to the rising sign. "Of Mercury" <note>Vidas</note> means of the planet Mercury. This implies a Mercury not conjoined with malefics. If conjoined with malefics, the destruction of intellectual capacity and other such results should be predicted. This is an elaboration of what was stated in the verse beginning "When the divisions of benefics are in the Ascendant." || 40 ||

# Chapter Eight

If the Ascendant <note>The *Lagna*, or the sign rising on the eastern horizon at the time of inquiry</note> or its ruling planet is associated with "hot" elements, the querent will suffer from fever and other bile-related illnesses <note>original: *pitta-ruk*; referring to the Ayurvedic humor associated with heat and metabolism</note>. There will also be a burning of the house, especially if the sign is a "poisonous division" <note>original: *visha-vyanjana*; specific degrees of the zodiac considered toxic or harmful</note>. || 41 ||

If the zodiac sign corresponding to the Ascendant's Navamsha <note>The ninth-part division of a sign, used for finer detail</note> is occupied by a benefic planet, the querent's past time has been auspicious. If occupied by a malefic planet, it has been inauspicious. || 42 ||

When the Moon occupies the sign of the Ascendant's Navamsha, the loss of an iron vessel indicates death. If the Moon occupies the sign of the *Mandyamsha* <note>The division associated with Gulika/Mandi, a sensitive point related to Saturn and bad luck</note>, the breaking of an earthen pot similarly indicates death. || 43 ||

->Through the planets occupying or<-
->aspecting the signs of Death, Breath, and Body,<-
->one should predict the gain or loss of<-
->the specific objects associated with those planets.<-

**Regarding the Ascendant:** "Associated with heat" refers to the hot seasons/times explained in the commentary on the second chapter. The "poisonous division" refers to the *Visha-Drekkana* <note>A 10-degree subdivision</note>. These are: the first division of Aries, Cancer, Leo, Virgo, Sagittarius, and Capricorn; the last division of Scorpio; and the middle division of the remaining five signs. This is understood from the verse: "Patha, Trikutuka, Rogam, Pathya, Ratri... these are the poisonous divisions of Aries and the others." Here, "Patha" and the following words represent numbers according to the *Katapayadi* system <note>An ancient Indian alphanumeric code used to store numbers in easily memorizable words</note>. || 41 ||

**Regarding the sign:** "Ascendant" here refers to the *Udaya-Lagna* (the rising sign at the moment of the question). || 42 ||

**Regarding the Ascendant [Navamsha]:** If at the time of the query the Moon is in the Navamsha sign of the Ascendant, the destruction of vessels made of iron, copper, etc., is a sign of death. Regarding the phrase "similarly in the *Mandyamsha* sign," some versions of the text read "if the Ascendant itself is in the *Mandyamsha* sign." Others explain that if the Moon moves into the Ascendant's Navamsha sign shortly after the query, the loss of a metal vessel occurs; if it moves into the *Mandyamsha* sign, the breaking of an earthen pot occurs—both are definitive signs of death. Practitioners of divination should consider all these possibilities, as the scriptures approve of various methods of reflection. || 43 ||

**Regarding Death, Breath, and Body:** Here, the "Death, Breath, and Body" signs mentioned in the verse beginning with "Mandi and the Moon" should be taken. "Gain" leads to good results and "loss" leads to calamity, respectively. The definitions of objects [associated with planets] should be looked up in Varahamihira’s *Hora* <note>The *Brihat Jataka*, a foundational text of Indian astrology</note> in the chapter on terminology. For example, "from copper, copper and lead," or "copper, gems, and gold," etc. These include items like "nails and teeth" or "grass, gold, and wool." These objects are determined by the planets occupying or aspecting the three signs: Death, Breath, and Body. The characteristics should be described based on the lords of these signs. || 44 ||

It references Varahamihira's classical system to link specific physical objects to planetary influences during a divination.</summary>

# Chapter on Definitions: Dashadhanasika and Others
# Or as stated elsewhere by them

->Copper and other metals, beginning with the nails and ending with grass<-
->If these do not belong to the master of the house. || 44 ||<-

->The results of those points calculated via the Ascendant, the Moon, and Gulika<-
->Namely Prana, Mrityu, and Sharira, are now being proclaimed. || 45 ||<-

->Among Prana, Mrityu, and Sharira, if Sharira <note>The "Body" point</note> is numerically greatest, there is relief from disease.<-
->If Prana <note>The "Breath" point</note> is greatest, there is great illness; if Mrityu <note>The "Death" point</note> is greatest, death occurs. || 46 ||<-

->If the Mrityu point falls in the constellations from Jyeshtha to Revati,<-
->Or in the individual's birth star, death is certain.<-
->If Mrityu, Prana, and Sharira increase in value in that specific order, it is auspicious. || 47 ||<-

->Some also consider the numerical superiority of the degrees of the Ascendant, Moon, and Gulika.<-
->That method is also written down here. || 48 ||<-

->If the Ascendant's degree is greatest, illness increases; if the Moon's degree is greatest, there is relief.<-
->If Gulika's degree is greatest, death occurs—this is determined by the elapsed time in Ghatikas <note>A unit of time equal to 24 minutes</note> and so on. || 49 ||<-

->When the Prana point is joined or aspected by the lords of Death and Time, or by malefic planets,<-
->The death of the querent <note>The person asking the question</note> should be predicted; however, its association with the Moon is auspicious. || 50 ||<-

---

**Regarding the Ascendant...** "Are being proclaimed" refers to what is stated in the following two verses. || 45 ||

**Regarding Prana...** "Numerical superiority" is determined by the Sign. If the Signs are equal, then by the Degree. If the Signs and Degrees are equal, then by the Minute. "In the birth star" refers to the birth constellation of the person asking the question. || 46, 47 ||

**Regarding the Ascendant...** Whichever portion has more elapsed units of time <term>Ghatikas: traditional Indian units of time</term> is considered "greater." By the phrase "consideration of superiority," and the specific reference to the previous verses, the calculation of the Navamsha <note>The ninth divisional chart</note> positions and the rule regarding "Mrityu in Jyeshtha" are applied here as well. Thus, the second verse should be understood as an illustration of this principle. This is why the naming of these points as Death, Body, and Breath is meaningful. || 48, 49 ||

**Regarding the Lords of Death and Time...** Here, "Prana" is derived from the "elapsed time of the question." "Death" and "Time" are derived from the "passed units of time." "Malefics" refers to the influence of cruel planets. The word "associated" implies that Prana is joined or aspected by the points of Death, Time, or malefic planets.

# Chapter Seven

When the sign of the Arudha <note>The sign rising at the time of a query or the sign occupied by the Ascendant lord</note>, its subdivision, the lords of the Ascendant and its subdivision, and the Moon’s subdivision are joined by the Moon, these eight factors indicate the time of death and bestow mortality. (51)

When Rahu <note>The North Node of the Moon, often associated with shadows and sudden events</note> is in the Ascendant, there is suffering from thieves and enemies; if the Sun is there, death occurs; if the Moon, bodily pain. This is the result of the Sun-Moon-Rahu cycle. (52)

The results of the planetary hours <term>Kala-hora: a system where each hour of the day is ruled by a specific planet</term> should be spoken to cause great amazement in the petitioner. For the sake of building trust, these are written down here according to the tradition. (53)

If the query occurs during the planetary hour of the Sun, a king or ruler arrives. In the Moon's hour, a woman arrives. In the hour of Mars <note>original: "Bhumiputra," son of the Earth</note>, there is an arrival of those carrying weapons. (54)

In the hour of Mercury, there is an arrival of a scholar or a messenger. In Jupiter's hour, the arrival of an excellent Brahmin <note>a member of the priestly or scholarly class</note>. In Venus's hour, the arrival of a woman of the merchant class. (55)

In Saturn's hour, the arrival of a merchant, or perhaps a servant or a Buddhist monk. If these planets are in the "angles" <term>Kendra: the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses of a birth chart</term>, one should state this as a certainty. (56)

-> This concerns the rising sign and related matters <-

If the sign associated with the Moon's subdivision at the time of the query is occupied by a benefic <note>a favorable planet like Jupiter or Venus</note>, the future time is said to be auspicious. If joined by a malefic, it is inauspicious. (57)

***

Regarding the life-force: By the eight factors—the Arudha sign, the Ascendant, their subdivisions, their respective lords, and the Moon's subdivision—the combination for the time of death is death-bestowing. (50, 51)

**Regarding the Ascendant:** The cycle of the Sun, Moon, and Rahu was previously shown in the fifth chapter, starting with the phrase "with two and a half measures of time," etc.

**Regarding Time:** Having fulfilled the promise to "speak of these results later in the eighth chapter," a small portion of the results is written here solely for the purpose of amazing the person asking the question. (53)

**Regarding the Sun:** In the verse starting "of the Moon," the phrase "in the planetary hour" carries over. The "arrival of those with weapons" is connected to the hour of Mars. "In Mercury's" refers to the hour belonging to Mercury. These lords of the planetary hours must be in the "angles" from the rising sign. "With certainty" means with total conviction. The "arrival" happens either at the time of the query, shortly thereafter, at the site of the query, or at the petitioner's house.

**Regarding this:** Now, something is being said regarding the subject of the Moon's subdivision.

**Regarding the sign named:** The distinction between auspicious and inauspicious results will be demonstrated immediately hereafter. (57)

# Path of Inquiry
## Page 120

Jupiter, when placed in its debilitated Navamsha <note>original: "nichabhanshagah"; referring to the 1/9th divisional sign where a planet is weakest</note>, grants children and creates wealth. Venus provides clothing and women, while Mercury brings victory in disputes. || 58 ||

The full Moon grants the acquisition of pleasing objects. The Sun, however, causes the anger of deities and kings. Mars <note>original: "Bhumija," literally "Son of the Earth"</note> || 59 ||

causes useless conflict and disputes over land. Saturn <note>original: "Suryaputra," literally "Son of the Sun"</note> causes the destruction of agriculture, servants, and cattle. || 60 ||

Rahu <note>original: "Phani," the Serpent</note> brings fear from outcasts, head diseases, poison, and snakes. Ketu <note>original: "Shikhi"</note> causes trouble from ghosts, and Gulika <note>original: "Mandi"</note> causes harassment from enemies. || 61 ||

If Mercury is joined by malefic planets, he causes defeat in disputes. The waning Moon causes mental agony to the petitioners. || 62 ||

The time for these results is determined by the number of the Navamsha in months; this same method applies to the Navamsha of the Ascendant. The results should also be told according to the "Actions of the Moon" <note>original: "Sudhabhanu-kriya," a specific system of 60 lunar states</note> at the time of inquiry. || 63 ||

This has been written by Jiva <note>The author, Govinda Bhattathiri, often referred to as 'Jiva'</note> as it should be told to the petitioner. || 64 ||

Assign the "Actions of the Moon" in groups of five to each sign starting from Aries. One should declare the results for all matters based on these. || 65 ||

If the Moon is auspicious at the time of inquiry, it grants good results. Likewise, if the Moon is situated in an inauspicious state, the inquiry will yield bad results. || 66 ||

---

**Commentary:**
Regarding the verse beginning with "Jupiter": The time for the result is the number of months corresponding to the Navamsha. If the Moon is in the Aries Navamsha, it is the first month; if in Taurus Navamsha, the second month, and so on. <margin>If in the first Navamsha of its occupied sign, it is within one month; if in the second, within two months.</margin> Fortnights should also be considered in this way. This same method applies to the Ascendant's Navamsha. The specific results like "Jupiter grants children" and the timing "months according to the Navamsha" are indicated here. || 58 — 63 ||

Regarding the "Actions": "Actions of the Moon" refers to the sixty specific lunar states. Their results are well-known, starting from "An ascetic fallen from his station" and ending with "One who is healthy and at ease," as described in three famous verses. This result was spoken by Jiva <note>referring to Brihaspati/Jupiter as the traditional source of wisdom</note> in the *Brihaspati Hora*. By assigning five "Actions of the Moon" to each sign starting from Aries, every six degrees of a sign constitutes one...

# Prashna Marga
## Chapter on Longevity

One should first examine the lifespan, and only afterwards declare the characteristics of the destiny. For what is the use of describing the traits of mortals who have no life remaining? || 3 ||
<note>original: "āyuḥ pūrvaṃ parīkṣeta..." This is a foundational principle in Indian astrology: there is no point predicting wealth or marriage if the subject's life is about to end.</note>

According to such sayings, the determination of longevity must be performed first. This is done through the planets, starting with the lords of the Ascendant <term>Lagna: the rising sign at the moment of the query</term> and the Eighth House <term>Ashtamasha: the house associated with death and longevity</term>. || 4 ||

Longevity is now specifically considered first. Whether this inquiry concerns a healthy person or one who is ill— || 5 ||

This distinction must be made through the planets, as stated in other authoritative scriptures. || 6 ||

-> If the Lord of the Ascendant is in a quadrant, is truly strong, <-
-> and is in a movable sign and a movable division, <-
-> then the question concerns a healthy person. But if the <-
-> Lord of the Ascendant is in the twelfth or sixth house, <-
-> is in a fixed sign, and is devoid of strength, then the <-
-> inquiry concerns one afflicted by a great disease. If the <-
-> factors are mixed, then like the ebb and flow of the tides, <-
-> one should predict the alternating subsiding and <-
-> increasing of the illness. || 7 ||

---

### Further Commentary from Other Texts

**Regarding Longevity** (Verse 3): The reason for the statement in the first half of the verse is demonstrated by the second half. || 3 ||

**Regarding "According to..."** (Verse 4): The phrase "it is established" should be understood as the conclusion here. || 4 ||

**Regarding Longevity** (Verse 5-6): The meaning is that the distinction between a query about a healthy person and a sick person is determined according to the methods mentioned in other scriptures. || 5, 6 ||

**Regarding the Lord of the Ascendant** (Verse 7): There are four characteristics indicating a query about a healthy person: the Lord of the Ascendant being in a quadrant <term>Kendra: houses 1, 4, 7, or 10</term>, being strong, being in a movable sign, and being in a movable <insert>navamsha</insert> division. Conversely, there are four characteristics indicating a query about one afflicted by a great disease: being in the twelfth or sixth houses <note>houses of loss and sickness</note>, being weak, and being in a fixed sign. The implication is that if these factors are mixed as far as possible, there will be occasional relief and occasional intensification of the disease. || 7 ||

**Regarding "Further..."**: This refers to the subject of determining results based on the specific placement of the Lord of the Ascendant.

<summary>This page establishes that an astrologer must first calculate a subject's lifespan before making other predictions and provides specific planetary combinations to determine if a client is asking about a healthy person or a chronic illness.</summary>

# Chapter Nine

->If the Lord of the Ascendant <note>The planet ruling the first house, representing the self.</note> is in its sign of exaltation, the person will be wealthy, courageous,<-
->a conqueror of enemies, and possessed of preeminent splendor.<-
->They will be endowed with self-respect. If the planet is in its own trine <note>term: Moolatrikona; a specific favorable placement for a planet.</note>,<-
->they will possess fine clothing and ornaments, and attain happiness. | 8 |<-

->In the fourth house <note>The house of home and comforts.</note> or in its own sign, one's enemies are destroyed,<-
->and there is joy through wife, children, wealth, and kinsmen.<-
->If the planet is in an enemy's sign, there is constant illness, and loss of<-
->children, friends, and wife, as well as trouble from kings, ministers, or thieves. || 9 ||<-

->If the planet is in its sign of fall <note>term: Neecha; the weakest position for a planet.</note>, there is suffering from enemies, travel to<-
->foreign lands, loss of position, loss of wealth, and misery.<-
->If it is combust <note>term: Mudha; hidden by the sun's rays.</note> or joined with malefic planets or Gulika <note>A specific mathematical point in the sky considered harmful.</note>, the person suffers<-
->impairment due to kings or enemies, goes to another land, or dies. || 10 ||<-

->If the Lord of the Ascendant and the Lord of the Eighth House are both in their signs of fall,<-
->or if both are combust,<-
->the querent will be broken-hearted, deprived of happiness,<-
->and their body will be constantly afflicted by pain.<-
->They will have a short life, lose their position,<-
->and suffer from diseases in the upper parts of the body.<-
->This should also be predicted when inauspicious planetary combinations,<-
->such as Kemadruma <note>A specific yoga indicating poverty or isolation.</note> and others, are present. || 11 ||<-

---

**Regarding "Standing in Exaltation":** From the phrase "Standing in Exaltation" up to "loss of wealth and misery," the text demonstrates five types of results based on the Lord of the Ascendant's placement in the six positions ranging from exaltation to fall. The result for exaltation ends with "endowed with self-respect." Here, the auspicious or inauspicious nature of the zodiac signs and degrees should also be considered. The half-verse beginning with "Combust" describes the results of the state of combustion and specific planetary combinations. || 8–10 ||

**Regarding "The Lord of the Ascendant":** "Gone to setting" means combust. The phrase "constantly afflicted by pain" should be applied here. Also, "moved from one's own position." "When present" refers to those conditions arising from the state of the planets at the time of the inquiry. This refers to the aforementioned "broken-heartedness" and other such afflictions. || 11 ||

->If the Lord of the Ascendant <note>Lagnadhipa: the planet ruling the rising sign</note> and the Lord of Death <note>Mritipa: the ruler of the 8th house</note> are joined together,<-

**Regarding "The Lord of the Ascendant" etc.** "Joined together" means meeting anywhere in the chart. This verse describes three specific combinations that grant long life. The word "Thus" <note>original: "iti"</note> indicates the conclusion of the passage cited from another text beginning with "standing in exaltation."

**Regarding "The Querent" etc.** This verse demonstrates six signs of death for a healthy person. Even if the person asking the question shows no signs of illness, death should be foreseen if these conditions are met. "The Lord of the Birth Star" <note>Nakshatresha</note> is understood through the sequence: Sun, Moon, Mars, Rahu, Jupiter, Saturn, Mercury, and Ketu as the respective lords of the stars beginning with Krittika. One yoga <note>astrological combination</note> occurs when the Lord of the birth star is the ruler of the house occupied by Gulika. The phrase "the querent himself standing in the 8th house" should be applied here. "In his own" means his personal 8th house. "Placed in the money" refers to the 8th house of the querent. "The three" refers to the birth star, the star at the time of the query, and the star occupied by Gulika. If the lords of these three are placed in the 8th house from the birth sign, it must be considered a sign of death.

# Chapter Nine

->Long life and the journey through this world are the two purposes of this science.<-
->Who can determine these with certainty? Perhaps Vasistha or Brihaspati <note>Vasistha and Brihaspati are legendary sages and preceptors of the gods, representing the pinnacle of astrological knowledge</note>. || 15 ||<-
->How much less can ordinary men do so, especially in this Kali Age <note>The current dark age in Hindu cosmology, characterized by a decline in spiritual and intellectual capacity</note>?<-
->The understanding of one's worldly journey is called the "Body" of this science by the wise. || 16 ||<-
->The understanding of lifespan is called the "Life-breath" of Horoscopy <note>original: "Hora"</note>. || 17 ||<-

->The Ascendant <note>original: "Lagnam"</note>, the Lord of the Ascendant, the Eighth House of Death, its Lord, and the Moon:<-
->These are indeed the tools for understanding the loss of life.<-
->One must contemplate them according to their strengths and weaknesses, such as the influence of beneficial or malefic planets. || 18 ||<-

->Placement between malefic planets, or the aspect and conjunction of non-beneficial ones,<-
->These are the "faults," while the opposite are the "virtues" for the body of the Ascendant.<-
->The conjunction or aspect of its own Lord is also a virtue.<-
->The virtues and faults of the Eighth House are to be judged exactly like those of the Ascendant. || 19 ||<-

***

**Regarding "Life" etc.** || "Journey" <note>original: "Yatra"</note> refers to one's conduct and livelihood during the span of life. In the Kali Age, there is a natural scarcity of wisdom and enthusiasm among people. By using a "rhetorical implication" <note>original: "Arthapatti-alankara"</note>, the text emphasizes that while it is difficult for humans to fully grasp lifespan and worldly destiny, it is not entirely impossible. If it were impossible, the very commencement of this scientific treatise would be useless, striking at the very root of the study. A Great Teacher would not engage men in a task that is completely unachievable, nor would he encourage enthusiasm for such a pursuit. Therefore, the secret meaning of this statement is that those <term>learned in the science of light (Astrology)</term> <note>original: "Jyotish-shastra-vedyaih"</note>, being encouraged to give predictions, must proceed with extremely subtle investigation, fueled by faith and devotion to the Divine, the learned, and the Teacher. || 15–17 ||

**Regarding "The Ascendant"** || The <term>Ascendant</term> <note>original: "Lagnam"</note> refers to the rising sign. "Death" refers to the Eighth House. Among the five tools mentioned for calculation: the aspect of a benefic, conjunction with a benefic, and planetary strength are the three "virtues." Their opposites are "faults." By the word "etcetera," one should include conditions such as being placed between benefics or malefics. The author shows this generally here and will explain it specifically in the following verses. || 18 ||

**Regarding "Malefic"** || The word "Body" <note>original: "Vapushah"</note> should be applied to both cases. The "Body" is the Ascendant. For the benefics, these three—placement in the middle, aspect, and conjunction—are virtues. Having thus described the virtues and faults of the Ascendant and the Eighth House, the virtues and faults of the Lord of the Ascendant will be described in the next verse. || 19 ||

The faults of the Lord of the Ascendant <note>The planet ruling the rising sign</note> are: association with or aspect from malefic planets, being situated between malefics, combustion <note>being too close to the Sun</note>, placement in an enemy’s sign, placement in its sign of debilitation, or being eclipsed. Its virtues are: placement in its sign of exaltation, its own sign, or a friend’s sign; association with or aspect from benefic planets; being situated between benefics; and retrograde motion. || 20 ||

The virtues and faults of the Lord of the Ascendant are the same for the Lord of the 8th House <note>The house associated with longevity and death</note>. However, placement in a quadrant <note>The 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses</note> is a fault for the Lord of the 8th House, whereas it is a virtue for the Lord of the Ascendant. || 21 ||

For the Moon, the faults are: placement in the 6th, 8th, or 12th houses; association with, aspect from, or being placed between malefics; being waning; and placement in its sign of debilitation <note>Scorpio</note>. Its virtues are: being full; being placed between, associated with, or aspected by benefics; placement in a quadrant from Jupiter; placement in its exaltation sign; and especially its association with Jupiter. || 22 ||

Placement of malefics in the 11th, 6th, and 3rd houses is said to grant long life. This is indicated by Varahamihira <note>A famous 6th-century Indian astronomer and astrologer</note> himself in the verse beginning with "Jupiter and the Moon..." || 23 ||

# Prashna Marga
## Page 128

->The zodiac sign rising at the moment of the query and the sign occupied by the questioner are both referred to by the term 'Lagna' (Ascendant).<-
->In works such as the *Krishniya*, it is stated that the results of a query must be predicted based on both of these.<-

->The Fixed Wheel <note>Sthira Chakra: a conceptual map of the zodiac fixed to the cardinal directions on the ground</note> remains on the earth,<-
->while the Moving Wheel <note>Chara Chakra: the actual celestial sphere that rotates in the sky</note> moves through the heavens.<-
->By means of these two wheels,<-
->the results should be declared for those who inquire at the start of a session. || 27 ||<-

->Just as a fortune-teller should indicate good or bad fortune for the questioner<-
->based on the Rising Sign and the Arudha Sign,<-
->they should likewise do so for the messenger <note>The person sent to deliver the query</note> based on the 12th houses and 11th houses from those two signs. || 28 ||<-

->Furthermore, the results of the twelve houses should be judged from whichever<-
->of those two signs (Rising or Arudha) is stronger at that time.<-
->Similarly, matters such as the self, the father, and so on, are examined<-
->through the planetary significators <term>Karaka: a planet that acts as a symbolic representative for a specific area of life</term> beginning with the Sun. || 29 ||<-

In the *Krishniya* <note>An authoritative ancient text on horary astrology</note>, the specific application of these two is explained. Thus, it says:

->A query is considered to be of two types, depending on the prominence of the Rising Sign or the Arudha.<-
->Even if a questioner is moving about at the time of sunrise, the Rising Sign takes precedence. || 30 ||<-

***

Regarding the verse beginning with "At that time" (*Tat-kala*): The next three verses demonstrate the teachings found in the *Krishniya* and similar works. || 26 ||

Regarding "Remaining on the earth" (*Bhumistham*): This refers to that which stays on the ground. <note>The author provides a grammatical explanation for the Sanskrit term 'Bhumistham'</note>. This means the Fixed Wheel is drawn on the ground according to the method where Aries and Taurus are assigned to the East, and so on. The "Moving Wheel," also known as the Circle of Lights <note>Jyotish-chakra</note>, constantly rotates in the sky due to the force of the *Pravaha* wind. The essence is that the term "Lagna" should be understood to include both the Arudha Lagna and the Rising Lagna. "Fortune-teller" (*Daivavid*) refers to the astrologer. "From their 11th houses" (*Tadayabhabhyam*) refers to the 11th houses counted from the Rising Sign and the Arudha. One should judge from whichever of the two signs is more endowed with strength. || 27–29 ||

Regarding "In the *Krishniya*": The statement mentioned is from the text *Krishniya*.

Regarding "The query" (*Prashna*): The idea is that at the time of sunrise, the Rising Sign should be taken because of the importance of the time and because the Arudha (the questioner's position) is difficult to discern while they are in motion. This is understood through the knowledge of the science of omens and astronomy. || 30 ||

<meta>This page continues the technical discussion on horary astrology (Prashna), specifically focusing on when to use the Rising Sign (Udaya) versus the Arudha (the sign corresponding to the questioner's position) and the calculation of the 'Chhatra' or Parasol sign.</meta>

# Chapter Nine

When a questioner is endowed with knowledge <note>original: "vidyā"; likely referring to a learned or sincere seeker</note> and asks regarding travel or other active endeavors, the astrologer should declare the results based on the **Rising Sign** <term>Udaya: the zodiac sign ascending on the eastern horizon at the moment of the query</term>. || 31 ||

However, when the work is finished, or at the end of the day, or if the questioner is lying down at night, or in a place crowded with people, or regarding something held in a fist, or if the questioner is inside a house, or regarding immovable property and such matters—in these cases, the results should be considered through the **Arudha Sign** <term>Arudha: the sign determined by the questioner's physical location or a chosen point</term>. In both instances, one's own "Parasol" <note>original: "Chhatra"; a protective or covering sign used for specific predictions</note> must be considered, which is explained as follows: || 32, 33 ||

->**The Calculation of the Parasol Sign**<-

When the Sun <note>original: "Mārtāṇḍa"</note> is in Taurus or Libra, or the four signs following them, or when it reaches Aries, Gemini, or Taurus in order, these are the "Paths" <note>original: "Vīthi"</note>. However many signs the Rising Sign is from the Arudha, that same number of signs counted from the "Path Sign" becomes the **Parasol Sign** <note>original: "Chhatra-bha"</note>. This applies to the fixed zodiac; in the moving zodiac, the degree of the Rising Sign <note>original: "Lagnāṃśaka"</note> acts as the coverer. || 34 ||

Because the stars are in constant motion, some sign is always rising. Nevertheless, because the Arudha represents the specific desire of the questioner, it is given primary importance here. || 35 ||

***

**Regarding "At the end of work" etc.:** "At the end of work" means at the conclusion of the action being performed by the questioner. "When the questioner is lying down" refers to their physical posture. Regarding "In the fist," it refers to the question: "Tell me what is in my hand?" If the questioner is "inside a house," it means they are situated within an interior space. In these cases, the instruction "one should declare the result through the Arudha sign" should be applied. The "Parasol" refers to the Parasol Sign, which is explained in the following verse. || 32, 33 ||

**Regarding "The Sun" etc.:** The "final signs" refer to Virgo, Libra, Pisces, and Aries. The construction is: however many signs the Rising Sign is from the Arudha, that same number of signs from the Path Sign <note>original: "Vīthi-bhavana"</note> becomes the Parasol Sign. In the "Moving Zodiac" <note>original: "Chara-chakra"</note>, the Navamsha <note>the 1/9th division of a sign</note> of the Rising Sign is the "Coverer" or Parasol Sign. || 34 ||

**Regarding "Constant" etc.:** This verse demonstrates the author's own opinion. Although a Rising Sign is always available due to the continuous motion of the celestial sphere <note>original: "Jyotiścakra"</note>, the Arudha is sometimes difficult to perceive (such as when a person stands on a boundary). However, since the method of determining it—such as by the placement of gold—is prescribed by the treatises, the author's view is that the **Arudha** holds the highest importance. || 35 ||

# Chapter Nine

> One should consider the correspondence between the immediate death-inflicting <term>Yogas</term> <note>astrological combinations or configurations</note> and the answers derived from the question. || 42 ||

This is regarding the determination of lifespan based on the question asked. Now, lifespan is being determined based on the <term>Jataka</term> <note>the natal birth chart</note>.

> When there is a correspondence between the results of planetary transits, timing cycles (<term>Dashas</term>), and the horary question, only then should the good or bad result be declared without a doubt. || 43 ||
>

>

---

The intent is expressed by the text beginning with "For wealth," etc. Since the memorization of the *Varahamihira Hora* <note>a foundational 6th-century text on Vedic astrology by the astronomer Varahamihira</note> was prescribed in the first chapter, those specific combinations are not displayed here. By using the word "correspondence," it is understood that death should be predicted with certainty only when there is agreement between the defined characteristics and the planetary configurations. || 42 ||

**"This..."**: Following the sequence mentioned in the verse regarding the path of the questioner and the one declaring the results, the contemplation of lifespan via the birth chart is also prescribed as a duty; let those desiring to learn study it in this context.

**"Planetary transit..."**: Of a "being" means of any living creature. "In this world" means in this current life. "That which is life is lifespan"—this is the arrangement. The statement from the *Amarakosha* <note>the famous Sanskrit lexicon</note> that "Lifespan is the duration of life" also refers to this. "Of this lifespan" refers to the <term>Prarabdha Karma</term> <note>the portion of past karma currently being experienced in this life</note>.

**"Necessarily..."**: "Fruit" refers to that produced by the *Prarabdha Karma*. Regarding the verse from the *Bhagavad Gita*—"The fire of knowledge reduces all Karma to ashes, O Arjuna"—this refers only to the accumulated (<term>Sanchita</term>) Karma and others, excluding the *Prarabdha* <note>the author argues that even enlightened beings must finish the life-destiny already in motion</note>. "By a Yoga" means by a means such as knowledge. "This being" refers to the living creature. "That fruit of Prarabdha Karma." || 46 ||

**"Scripture..."**: They are called "Yogas" because they "join" (<term>yojayanti</term>) one with the results arising from *Prarabdha*. By this, having defined the word Yoga, the nature and number of Yogas are told starting from their positions, etc. || 47, 48 ||
