# Prashna Marga
## Page 132

->Combinations arise from position, from the houses, from the planets, and from the combination of positions, houses, and celestial bodies.<-
->Through the union of position and house, and through the union of house and planet. || 49 ||<-
->There are six types of combinations; a seventh arises from position and planet.<-
->The "position" of planets refers to their exaltation, Moolatrikona <note>A specific favorable sign position for a planet, stronger than its own sign but weaker than exaltation</note>, and so on. || 50 ||<-
->The "houses" are said to be the Ascendant and the rest; the "planets" are the Sun and the others.<-
->In a combination declared by house, position, and planet, those factors which cause the combination— || 51 ||<-
->Whichever among them is strongest shall be the "doer" and the giver of the results. || 52 ||<-
->Longevity for humans is of two kinds: Yoga-longevity and Dasha-longevity.<-
->Yoga-longevity is that declared by combinations; Dasha-longevity is that produced by planetary periods. || 53 ||<-
->Yoga-longevity is of six types based on the six combinations; I shall now state them:<-
->Immediate-death, Misfortune, Yoga-misfortune, and likewise— || 54 ||<-
->Medium, Long, and Unlimited longevity; thus the combinations are of six kinds.<-
->The two "Immediate-death" combinations grant death before the end of a year. || 55 ||<-

**Regarding "From position" etc.** There are indeed seven types of combinations. Among them, the first is by **position**, such as "Birth in a Vargottama <note>A planet occupying the same sign in both the main birth chart and the 1/9th divisional chart</note> is auspicious," and so on. The second is by **houses** alone, such as "When the quadrants are not empty," and so on. The third is by **planets** alone, such as "Happy, performing great deeds," or "Chief of the family," and so on. The fourth is by all three together, such as "When planets are in their exaltation or own signs," and so on. The fifth is by **position and house**, such as "The rising of the Sun in the Ascendant," and so on. The sixth is by **planet and house**, such as "When planets are situated in the 6th, 7th, or 8th houses," and so on. The seventh is by **position and planet**, such as "When planets have reached seven signs," and so on. "Causes of the combination" refers to those factors that create the Yoga. Among those causes, whichever is the strongest is the actual creator of that combination and the giver of its fruit. || 49-52 ||

**Regarding "Yoga-longevity"** Longevity indicated or made known by combinations of "thirty-two years" and so on is called Yoga-longevity. Longevity produced by **Dasha** <term>Dasha: Planetary periods or cycles that determine when specific life events occur</term> is that which arises from the calculation of the periods of the planets involved. Systems such as the Kalachakra Dasha and Nakshatra Dasha are also to be understood by the word "Dasha." || 53 ||

**Regarding "Yoga-longevity"** It is of six types based on the divisions of "Immediate-death" and so on which will be described: 1. Immediate-death combination (*Sadyorishta*), 2. Misfortune combination (*Arishta*), 3. Evil combination (*Rishta*), 4. Medium-life combination (*Madhyayu*), 5. Long-life combination (*Dirghayu*), 6. Unlimited-life combination (*Amitayu*). "End of the year" means before one year of age is completed. <insert>Death within twelve years.</insert> These do not depend on the Dasha periods. The meaning is that before twelve years of age, the planetary periods (Dashas) should not be considered. <note>In traditional Indian pediatrics/astrology, early childhood mortality is seen as a result of the parents' karma or specific "Rishta" combinations rather than the child's own Dasha cycle.</note> The total is thirty-two. By the number of elements...

If the lords of the Ascendant <note>Lagna</note> and the Moon-sign are mutual enemies, or if the lords of the eighth house from them are enemies, the life is short. If they are neutral, life is middle; if they are friends, life is long. || 60 ||

The same [short, middle, or long life] is determined by the relationship between the lord of the Navamsha <note>The 1/9th divisional chart</note> occupied by the Moon and the lord of the 64th Navamsha <note>original: "tad-bhūṣā"; a sensitive point in the horoscope often linked to longevity</note>, or between the lord of the Sun's Navamsha and the lord of the Ascendant. || 61 ||

Now, certain qualities that grant longevity and fortitude are written. These include the strength of the Ascendant and the Moon, their association with benefics, and being aspected by benefics. || 62 ||

...refers to the end of seventy years; this is the intended meaning. "Of a hundred years" is the connection. # Chapter Ten Begins

### On the Investigation of the Time of Death

->Through both Horary inquiry <note>Prashna: a branch of astrology where a chart is cast for the moment a question is asked</note> and the Birth Chart,<-
->the time and circumstances of death must be considered.<-
->First, the timing and the nature of the illness are determined from the birth chart,<-
->along with the location of passing.<-
->The calculation of the time of death must indeed be performed<-
->through planetary combinations, major and minor periods,<-
->and the positions of Saturn, Jupiter, the Sun, and the Moon,<-
->as well as through the Ascendant <note>Lagna: the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon</note>. || 1 ||<-

->When specific death-inflicting combinations are present, death occurs at the end of the years specified by that combination.<-
->If the combination depends on planetary periods, then the agreement between the two must be examined. || 2 ||<-

->During the major periods, sub-periods, and transits of planets that bestow affliction,<-
->one should predict the death of men; this is the method to be used when specific combinations are absent. || 3 ||<-

---

**Now:** This indicates that since death has been determined according to the methods described in the previous chapter, but the specific time remains unseen, the investigation into that timing is now commenced.

**Through both Horary inquiry:** The word "indeed" is used for emphasis. It serves to remind us of what was previously stated regarding the results of planetary transits, periods, and horary questions. Between the two—Horary and Birth charts—one first looks to the **Birth Chart** <note>original: "Janusha"</note>. This is because the determination of lifespan based on the birth chart is considered primary. **Positions** refers to the specific placements of the planets. **Through the Ascendant** refers to the rising sign at the time of death. The meaning is that one should predict that death will occur when Saturn and the other planets are in specific signs and a particular sign is rising. || 1 ||

**When specific combinations:** Regarding the phrase "depends on planetary periods," this refers to the rule that "some combinations are dependent on the timing of planetary cycles." **Agreement** refers to the correspondence with the planetary periods <note>Dasha: planetary cycles that rule specific blocks of time in a person's life</note>. || 2 ||

**During the major periods:** If there is a combination that does not depend on a planetary period, then the calculation of the period is not strictly necessary. However, if the combination is dependent on it, then the calculation must be done to find the agreement between the two. In the absence of both types of specific combinations, death should be predicted solely through the **major periods, sub-periods, and transits** <note>original: "Dasha-Apahara-Chara"</note> of the planets. || 3 ||

It emphasizes the roles of planetary periods (Dashas), transits, and specific yoga combinations in determining when a life will end.</summary>

By the word "Gulika-pa," the sign occupied by Gulika is intended. "By these" refers to the lord of the eighth house and the others mentioned. "Among these" refers to the list ending with Rahu. "At birth" means at the time of one's delivery.

**"Of the malefics" (Papanamiti)**: "Of the wicked" means of the malefic planets. "Lords of the Go-Ma-Sa stars" refers to the lords of the *Vipat* (Danger), *Pratyari* (Obstacle), and *Vadha* (Destruction) constellations. "Ripening" (Paka) refers to the major and sub-periods. "Of two or three" refers to systems such as the Star-based <note>Nakshatra</note> or Time-Wheel <note>Kalachakra</note> systems. "At which time" means in whichever period. "Granting defects" refers to those previously mentioned starting from the Ascendant. || 5 ||

**"The defect" (Dosha iti)**: "Equal across all systems" means there is no distinction between the Star-based or Time-Wheel systems. "In the periods arising from..." means specifically in the Star-based periods <note>Nakshatra Dashas</note>. It does not apply elsewhere, such as in the Time-Wheel <note>Kalachakra</note> or other systems. || 6 ||

# Page 138
## First Part

->The period of planets that are in their sign of fall <note>original: "nichastha"; refers to a planet at its weakest point in the zodiac</note> or combust <note>original: "mudha"; rendered invisible by proximity to the Sun</note> invariably brings death.<-
->Now, the specific details regarding the Kalachakra Dasha <note>A complex system of planetary periods based on the movement of the Moon through the constellations</note> are being explained. || 7 ||<-

->If the movement goes from Pisces to Scorpio,<-
->or from Virgo to Cancer,<-
->or from Leo to Gemini, and then back to Leo,<-
->or from Sagittarius to Aries;<-
->the time of entering these signs is painful,<-
->and the subsequent period is also full of suffering.<-
->Movement that follows the natural order of signs is auspicious,<-
->but jumping across signs is inauspicious. || 8 ||<-

**Regarding the period...** "Invariably" means with certainty. The intent is that this characteristic is unfailing. Now, one might object: "Some people are seen living happily through the periods of planets in their fall or combustion. Therefore, this statement is not authoritative because it contradicts direct observation." To this, we reply: This science of Astrology is full of general rules and specific exceptions. There may be some exception in a particular individual's birth chart. Indeed, the lifespan determined by overall planetary combinations <note>term: Yoga-ayus; longevity granted by specific structural patterns in the chart</note> can override the lifespan indicated by a specific period <note>term: Dasha-ayus</note>. That must be the case here. Alternatively, in that person's chart, at the actual time of death, it will certainly occur during the period, sub-period, or minor sub-period of a planet that is either in its fall or combust within the Kalachakra, Origin, or Conception systems. Or, the word "death" in "death-bestowing" should be understood through metaphor to mean a "great calamity" equivalent to death. Furthermore, the death-dealing nature of periods is not determined by a single factor, but by many. At the time of death, there will be a convergence of two or three such indicators. "A prediction should be made clear when there is a convergence of two or three factors," is proclaimed by all the authors of the Shastras <note>sacred scientific treatises</note>. Therefore, one should not oppose this rule. The use of the word "invariably" highlights a specific, extraordinary time of affliction. || 7 ||

**Regarding Pisces...** In the sequence "Pradad" <note>a mnemonic code for the Dasha sequence</note>, the period of Mars follows the period of Jupiter; the transition between them is inauspicious, as indicated by the jump from Pisces to Scorpio. In the sequence "Tavi," the period of the Moon follows the period of Mercury; that transition from Virgo to Cancer is inauspicious. In the sequence "Male," the period of Mercury follows the period of the Sun; that transition from Leo to Gemini is inauspicious. In the sequence "Goman," the period of the Sun follows the period of Mercury; that transition back to Leo is inauspicious. In the sequence "Gadhaka," the period of Mars follows the period of Jupiter; that transition from Sagittarius to Aries is inauspicious. Movement is auspicious when it does not skip signs. Whether in direct or reverse order, movement that does not abandon the sequence of signs is beneficial. Jumping to a different sign <note>non-sequential movement</note> is inauspicious. The examples given, such as Pisces to Scorpio, illustrate this. || 8 ||

It also defends the accuracy of astrological rules by explaining that "death" can refer to major life crises and that multiple factors must align for a final prediction.</summary>

# Chapter Ten

> In the stars of the right side, the first sign mentioned in the mnemonic phrase is the **Body** <note>Sanskrit: *Deha*, representing the physical vessel or starting point</note>; the final sign is the **Soul** <note>Sanskrit: *Jiva*, representing the life force or destination</note>. In the left stars, this is reversed. || 9 ||

> If either the Lord of the Body or the Lord of the Soul is joined with a malefic planet, it brings disease. If both are joined with malefics and the planetary period <term>Dasha: a period of time ruled by a specific planet</term> is unfavorable, death is certain. || 10 ||

-> One should calculate using the right and left hands, <-
-> using the stars beginning with Hasta and others, <-

**Regarding the Body:** Among the "right stars" <note>Sanskrit: *Dakshina-tara*</note>, there are five groups of three: "Ashvini, Bharani, Krittika; Punarvasu, Pushya, Ashlesha; Hasta, Chitra, Svati; Mula, Purvashadha, Uttarashadha; Purvaphalguni, Uttaraphalguni, and Revati." These fifteen stars constitute the right stars. The other four groups of three, totaling twelve stars, are the "left stars" <note>Sanskrit: *Vama-bha*</note>. Among the five groups of right stars, for the ten stars at the beginning and end of the triplets, the phrase "He attained the peaceful shore" <note>original: *param lebhe shantam*</note> is used. For the five stars in the middle of those triplets, the phrase "The maidservant was like that" <note>original: *dasi tavad iti*</note> is used. For the four groups of left stars, for the eight stars at the beginning and end, the phrase "The cow is a tigress" <note>original: *dhenur vyaghriti*</note> is used. For the four stars in the middle, the phrase "Having obtained the curved one" <note>original: *prapyanchi iti*</note> is used. Through these four verses consisting of four quarters each, the lords of the periods are to be known. In each quarter, there are nine letters. Among these, for the right stars, the sign indicated by the first letter is the **Body**, and the sign indicated by the last letter is the **Soul**. For the left stars, the sign of the first letter is the **Soul**, and the sign of the last letter is the **Body**. Thus, in the phrase "He attained the shore" <note>original: *param lebhe*</note>, the letter 'Pa' indicates Aries <note>Sanskrit: *Mesha*</note> as the Body, and the letter 'La' indicates Sagittarius <note>Sanskrit: *Chapa*</note> as the Soul. The same logic applies to the other seven phrases. In the phrase "The cow is a tigress," the letter 'Dhe' indicates Sagittarius as the Soul, and the letter 'Va' indicates Cancer <note>Sanskrit: *Karkataka*</note> as the Body. This applies to the other seven phrases. Some verses seen in other texts regarding this system of the Wheel of Time <term>Kalachakra Dasha: a sophisticated system of timing events in Vedic astrology based on the moon's position</term> are also written here. || 9, 10 ||

**Regarding the hands:** Following the sequence of the quarters <note>Sanskrit: *padas*</note>, for one born in the first quarter of a star, the first quarter of the verse applies. For the second quarter of a star, the second quarter of the verse applies, and so on. In the side stars, such as the eight stars beginning with Rohini and Ardra, there are three rotations. In the four quarters, there are a total of thirty-six letters. Through these, three rotations of the twelve zodiac signs occur. For the stars beginning with Ashvini, using the phrase "The shore..." etc., there are two rotations starting from Aries and moving in order through to Pisces <note>Sanskrit: *Jhasha* or *Mina*</note>, which is the middle rotation. For the five stars beginning with Bharani, there are two rotations at the beginning and end...

->the demon, the arrow, the invincible one,<-
->the one-footed, the final star-protector; in this order, it is considered<-
->the four-fold set beginning with the shore.<-

From the friend <note>original: "Ali"</note> to the end, as before, in reverse order. For the Sun and Moon, the signs of Leo and Cancer are taken in reverse or by skipping the sequence. It originated at the end of Aries. Here, the years and days of the planetary periods <term>Dasha-samvatsara; the specific duration of time assigned to a planet's influence</term> of the Sun and others are to be known by the letter-number system <note>original: "Akshara-sankhya"</note> according to the phrase: "The son of the sage, the heat of the king from the presence, the sound" <note>original: "Muniputrah sannidher-nripattapo dhvanih"</note>. The elapsed and remaining portions of the first period should be brought out by the rule of three <term>Trairashika; a mathematical proportion used to find an unknown value</term>. In that calculation, the standard measure is fifteen ghatikas <note>a ghatika is 24 minutes</note>. The result is the respective years. The "desire" <note>the variable in the proportion</note> is the elapsed or remaining ghatikas in the stellar quarter <term>Nakshatra-pada; one-fourth of a lunar mansion</term>. The calculation of sub-periods <term>Apahara-anayana; the division of major planetary cycles into smaller segments</term> is not shown here for fear of becoming too lengthy. || 1--8 ||

## Chapter Ten

If four planets are situated in the trines <note>the 1st, 5th, and 9th houses</note> from the Ascendant, death occurs. Alternatively, death for men should be predicted when the sign occupied by the lord of the Ascendant, or the sign of the Navamsha <note>a 1/9th divisional chart used for precision</note> of the Ascendant, rises in the fourth house. || 32–33 ||

When two or three different factors agree, the prediction should be stated clearly. Where many indicators point to the same sign, the effects of Saturn and the other planets will be manifest. || 34 ||

By observing the mutual agreement of Saturn and the other planets, one should properly determine their status at the time of death <note>literally: "the time of dissolving into the five elements"</note>. || 35 ||

This concerns the determination of the time of death based on the birth chart <term>Jataka: natal astrology</term>. However, the time of death can also be told through a query <term>Prashna: horary astrology</term>. The paths of the positions of Saturn, Mars, the Sun, and the Moon relative to the Ascendant are now described. || 36 ||

When Saturn moves through the sign of the Navamsha occupied by Gulika <note>original: "Mandyamsha-rashi"; Gulika/Mandi is a sensitive mathematical point in a chart often associated with misery or death</note>; when Jupiter moves through the sign of the Navamsha of the Ascendant; when the Sun moves through the Arudha sign <note>the sign rising at the moment of a query</note>; and when the Moon moves through the sign occupied by Gulika— || 37 ||

These transits grant death to the querent if there is mutual agreement between them. || 38 ||

When Saturn, Jupiter, the Sun, and the Moon reach the signs indicated by the final syllables of the messenger's speech <note>the first words spoken by the person asking the question</note>, and if those signs are extremely afflicted, death occurs when that house rises. || 39 ||

---

Regarding the phrase **"Two or three"**: By this, it is clarified that the principle of "clarity through the agreement of two or three factors" does not only apply to determining the time of death, but is a general rule for all predictions in the science of Jyotisha <note>Vedic astrology</note>. The idea is that one should predict only after carefully considering the mutual agreement of Saturn and the others. || 34, 35 ||

**"This"**: This refers to what was said starting from the section on "contemplating the time of the event."

**"Through a query"**: This is explained in the following nineteen verses. || 36 ||

**"The Navamsha of Gulika"**: This refers to the sign of the Navamsha where Gulika <note>Mandi</note> was positioned at the time of the query. "Saturn and the others" refers to these four specific planets. "If there is mutual agreement" means the agreement between all four: Saturn, Jupiter, the Sun, and the Moon. || 37, 38 ||

**"The messenger"**: Among the Saturn, Jupiter, Sun, and Moon positions at the time of the query, the one that is "extremely afflicted" refers to its placement in the eighth house or other unfavorable houses, or its association with malefic planets <term>Papayoga: an inauspicious planetary combination</term>. The signs indicated by the syllables will be made clear in the verses to follow. || 39 ||

# Prashna Marga
## Page 148

The twelve vowels of the Dravidian <note>original: "Dramila," referring here to the Tamil script/language system used in Kerala astrology</note> alphabet, along with the first and last letters of the consonant groups plus 'ya' and 'ra', are to be assigned to the signs starting from Aries. The remaining six letters are also to be applied to the first six signs from Aries. **(40)**

If the Moon reaches the sign corresponding to the Navamsha <note>The 1/9th divisional chart</note> of the Ascendant (Lagna) at the time of the query, the seeker's illness will increase. If the Moon reaches the sign of its own Navamsha, there will be delusion or unconsciousness. If it reaches the sign of Gulika's <note>A mathematical point representing the son of Saturn, usually malefic</note> Navamsha, death occurs. **(41)**

If the Navamsha of the Moon and the Navamsha of Gulika are the same, and the Moon enters that sign, delusion is certain. If the Navamsha of the Sun and Gulika are combined and the Moon enters there, death occurs. **(42)**

By adding the position of Yamakantaka <note>A sensitive point in the zodiac associated with Jupiter's son, generally considered beneficial but used here to calculate the "Four-fold Sensitive Point"</note> to the three sensitive points known as Prana, Deha, and Mrityu <note>Life, Body, and Death points calculated from the positions of the Sun, Moon, and Gulika</note>, one obtains a specific longitude. When the Moon transits the constellation (Nakshatra) indicated by this sum, death is predicted. **(43)**

The Sun transiting the trines of Gulika's constellation, or the sign occupied by the Lord of the 8th House, brings death. Similarly, the constellation occupied by Gulika is known as the "Death-step." **(44)**

Count from the constellation of the "Three-fold Sensitive Point" (Trisphuta) to the trines of the serpent constellation <note>Ashlesha</note>. That number indicates the years, months, days, or ghatikas <note>A unit of time equal to 24 minutes</note> remaining until death. **(45)**

One should consider the friendship or enmity between the Lord of the Ascendant and the Lord of its Navamsha. Gulika, moving in reverse from its own sign during day or night, bestows death. **(46)**

**Regarding "The Dravidians":** The twelve vowels of the Dravidian system are from 'A' to 'Au'. The twelve consonants are the first and last of the groups: Ka, Nga, Ca, Nya, Ta, Na, Ta, Na, Pa, Ma, Ya, and Ra. 'A' and 'Ka' belong to Aries. 'Aa' and 'Nga' belong to Taurus. Thus, 'Au' and 'Ra' belong to Pisces. The remaining six letters—La, Va, Lla, Zha, Ra, and Na—are assigned to the six signs from Aries to Virgo. 'La' is in Aries, 'Va' in Taurus, and 'Na' in Virgo.

**Regarding "Ascendant Navamsha":** "Reaching the sign of its own Navamsha" refers to the sign occupied by the Navamsha of the Moon at the time of the query. **(41)**

**Regarding "Moon etc.":** If, at the time of the query, the Navamsha sign of the Moon and the Navamsha sign of Gulika are identical, then when the Moon transits there... **(42)**

**Regarding "Ascendant and Moon":** The hours of Yamakantaka are determined starting from Sunday using the mnemonic "Divyo Namyo..." <note>A traditional verse used to calculate the daily timing of Yamakantaka</note>. Having calculated the precise longitude (Sphuta) of Yamakantaka and adding it to the three points (Prana, Deha, Mrityu), the resulting "Four-fold Point" indicates the constellation where the Moon's transit signifies death. **(43)**

**Regarding "Gulika etc.":** The "serpent constellation" refers to Ashlesha. Its trines are Ashlesha, Jyeshtha, and Revati. If the Lord of the Ascendant's Navamsha is a friend to the Lord of the Ascendant, death occurs at the end of that many years; if there is great enmity, it occurs in that many ghatikas...

# Chapter Ten

->The remaining time of the Navamsha of the stronger between the Ascendant and the Moon, measured in minutes, days, months, and years, indicates the end, depending on the severity or lightness of the astrological afflictions. (47)<-

->By the remaining seconds of the Ascendant's Navamsha, converted into days, months, and years, death occurs. This happens when the lord of the Ascendant is in a house of an enemy, a neutral, or a friend, relative to the lord of that Navamsha. (48)<-

->The remaining seconds of the Navamsha that bestows death also grant the timing of death. As previously stated, this is calculated in days, months, and years based on whether the lord of that Navamsha is an enemy, neutral, or friend to the lord of the Ascendant. (49)<-

### And here is the Method of Practice.

->From the Ascendant's Navamsha, identify which Navamsha is the most harmful among the cruel planets, the Serpent <note>Rahu</note>, the point of Death, or Gulika <note>a mathematical point in the sky considered malefic</note>. Based on the intensity of that harm, one should predict death after that many days, months, or years have passed. (50)<-

---

Death occurs at the end. According to the reversal of the dream: if Mandi <note>a malefic planetoid</note> is situated in a day-sign, death occurs at night; if situated in a night-sign, death occurs during the day. However, this does not pertain to "Prashna" <note>horary astrology or divination for a specific question</note>, but rather to "Jataka" <note>natal astrology based on birth time</note>. This will be explained further. (44–46)

**Regarding "The remaining..."**: Between the Ascendant <term>Lagna; the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon</term> and the Moon, the remaining minutes <note>original: "nadis"</note> of the Navamsha of whichever is stronger determine the end in days, months, or years. Regarding "severity of affliction": if the omens of death in the query are severe, it occurs at the end of that many days. (47)

**Regarding "The Ascendant's Navamsha..."**: One Navamsha consists of fifteen minutes <note>nadis</note>. That equals nine hundred seconds <note>vinadis</note>. Use the remaining seconds there. If the lord of the Ascendant is an enemy to the lord of that Navamsha, death occurs in that many days. (48)

**Regarding "The death-bestowing..."**: The "death-bestower" refers to Mandi and others situated in the eighth house. Alternatively, it refers to the "Tri-sphuta" <note>a sensitive calculated point involving the Ascendant, Moon, and Gulika</note>, Mandi, or the "Time of Death" <note>Mrityu-kala</note>. The Navamsha occupied by these is the "death-bestowing Navamsha." As stated, the meaning is that death occurs in a number of days, months, or years equal to the remaining seconds of that Navamsha. (49)

**Regarding "Here..."**: The following three verses are from the text "Anushthana-paddhati" <note>The Method of Practice</note>. (50)

**Regarding "Cruel, Serpent..."**: "Cruel" refers to Saturn and others. "Gulika and others" includes the Tri-sphuta and similar points. Among these, identify which Navamsha is most harmful due to its unfavorable position relative to the Ascendant's Navamsha. Based on that "harmful state"—meaning the degree of affliction—if the affliction is high, death occurs after that many days have passed. (50)

# Path of Inquiry
<note>original: "Prashnamarga"</note>

->When the signs containing the Serpent, Death, or Gulika are afflicted,<-
->or if a fatal omen occurs at the time of inquiry,<-
->one should consider death when the Moon, Sun, Jupiter, or Saturn<-
->occupy the trines of that specific sign.<-
<note>Verse 51</note>

**Regarding "Afflicted"**: The word "etcetera" here includes the Three-fold Sensitive Point <note>Trisphuta</note> and others. "At the time" refers to the moment the question is asked. A "fatal omen" is a sign indicating death. In this context, the direction should be determined by the sign, such as Aries and Taurus representing the East. Among the Moon, Sun, Jupiter, and Saturn, the one that is most afflicted is considered. The connection is made when that planet occupies a trine <note>the 1st, 5th, or 9th position</note> from that sign.

---

->Starting from the stronger of the two—the Lord of the Ascendant or the Lord of the Arudha—<-
->counting to the house where the omen occurred,<-
->or to the specific Star, Decan, or Ninth-part division;<-
->whether it be the falling of a tree or the death of a living being,<-
->or the position of Gulika and similar points;<-
->death will occur in that many days, months, or years.<-
<note>Verse 52</note>

**Regarding "Ascendant"**: Between the Lord of the Ascendant <note>Lagna-adhipati</note> and the Lord of the Arudha <note>the sign corresponding to the questioner's position</note>, choose the one with more strength. Start counting from that sign, Star <note>Nakshatra</note>, Decan <note>Drekkana</note>, or Ninth-part <note>Navamsha</note>. The resulting number represents the days, months, or years. Note that in counting signs, the number will be less than 12; for stars, less than 27; for decans, less than 36; and for ninth-parts, less than 108. One should count up to the sign or star occupied by the Ascendant at the exact moment an omen (like a tree falling) occurred. The distinction for the position of Gulika <note>a mathematical point representing the son of Saturn</note> is that one counts specifically to the sign it occupies. Some suggest determining the sign based on the direction where the tree fell or the creature died (using the rule that Aries/Taurus is East, etc.). Others read the text as "Ascendant and Arudha," implying one should use the precise mathematical longitudes of both points.

---

->Death may occur when the Ascendant reaches the eighth house from the Arudha or the Rising Sign,<-
->or the house occupied by the Lord of the Eighth,<-
->or a sign with low points in the Collective Ashtakavarga.<-
<note>Verse 53</note>

**Regarding "Arudha"**: The "Total Eight-fold Points" <note>Pindashtakavarga</note> refers to the Collective Eight-fold Points <note>Samudayashtakavarga</note> used to measure the strength of houses.

# Chapter Ten

The latter half of this verse, which concerns birth, as well as the half-verse beginning with "from one's own opposite, Mandi" <note>Mandi is a sensitive mathematical point in Vedic astrology, often associated with malefic or negative influences</note>, has been explained previously. // 54 //

This refers to the subject of determining the time of death based on the nine planets. Now, certain other planetary positions regarding the time of death are being stated.

The Sun, Mars, Saturn, and Jupiter, when occupying the twelfth, the first (birth sign), or the eighth houses from the person's Moon, produce loss of wealth, exile, diseases, or fear. // 55 //

The Moon in the eighth house; Mercury and Mars in the seventh; the Sun in the twelfth; Venus in the sixth; // 56 //

Jupiter in the third; and Rahu, Ketu, and Saturn in the first house—these undoubtedly create a danger to life. // 57 //

When cruel planets <note>term: Krura-grahas (natural malefics like Mars and Saturn)</note> are situated in the first, fourth, seventh, eighth, or twelfth houses, they shine like blazing fires <note>This metaphor indicates they become intensely destructive</note>. // 58 //

The Moon in the fourth, eighth, or twelfth houses always causes misfortune. Even a waxing Moon in the first house is not auspicious on the day of birth. // 59 //

**Regarding the verse:** The "latter half" refers to the section starting with "Pindashtakavarga" and so on. "Concerning birth" means regarding the natal horoscope. It implies it also applies to the "Prashna" <note>term: Prashna (the branch of astrology dealing with specific questions asked at a particular moment)</note>. // 54 //

**This:** This refers to what was said regarding the "portion of Mandi" and so on. It is explained in the following five verses.

**The twelfth:** "Occupying the twelfth, birth, or eighth" means these positions are calculated from the sign occupied by the Moon at the time of birth. This applies to the subsequent verses as well. // 55 //

**The Moon:** "They create a danger to life." The sense is that this occurs when three or four planets are situated in this manner. "Undoubtedly" implies the result when all eight are so situated. // 56, 57 //

**In the first:** "They shine like blazing fires." This means they create a suspicion or certainty of death. // 58 //

**In the fourth:** "Birth day" refers to the birth asterism <note>term: Janma-nakshatra (the lunar mansion the Moon was in at birth)</note>. // 59 //

# Now begins the Eleventh Chapter

---

Now, the causes of death are described:
> Death occurs by fire, water, weapons, and <term>fever</term><note>original: jvrtis</note> respectively;
> Or by unknown diseases, <term>thirst</term><note>original: trut; can refer to diabetes or dehydration</note>, and hunger, according to the planets occupying the eighth house. // 1 //
> If these planets are aspected by the Sun and others, death arises from diseases of the bones and other tissues associated with them;
> Or death arises from the humors like <term>bile</term><note>Pitta</note> or fire associated with those planets. // 2 //
> Bone, blood, marrow, skin, fat, semen, and <term>nerves</term><note>original: vaddhasa; refers to the connective tissues or sinews</note>;
> These are the seven <term>tissues</term><note>Dhatus</note> declared to belong to the Sun and the other planets in order. // 3 //
> Bile, wind-phlegm, bile, wind-bile-phlegm, phlegm,
> Phlegm-wind, and wind are declared to be the humors of the Sun and the others. // 4 //

---

Now, at the end [of the previous section], the causes are stated in eighteen verses. It should be understood that this is according to the birth chart.
Regarding "respectively": <term>Jvrti</term> means fever-disease. "Unknown" means a disease that cannot be determined as being "this" or "that." <term>Thirst</term> refers to <term>Prameha</term><note>a category of urinary disorders including diabetes</note> or the lack of access to water. "Hunger" refers to the obstruction of a fast or the lack of access to food. // 1 //
Regarding "aspected in the eighth": The bones and other tissues, as well as the bile and other humors of the Sun and others, will be explained immediately. // 2 //
Regarding "Bone": Marrow is a specific oily substance inside the bone. <term>Vasa</term> is the fat that pervades the muscle. <term>Vaddhasa</term> is a synonym for <term>Snayu</term><note>tendons or ligaments</note>, a very subtle type of vessel. Although practitioners of <term>Ayurveda</term><note>traditional Indian medicine</note> do not accept fat, skin, and nerves as primary tissues, the contradiction with other scriptures is easily resolved because fat is included in muscle, skin in the "essence" <note>Rasa</note>, and nerves in the adipose tissue <note>Medas</note>. // 3 //
Regarding "Bile": Here, the phrase "are declared" applies primarily to the combination of "wind, bile, and phlegm." In other instances like "bile," it should be understood by changing the gender and number of the words to fit the context. Otherwise, the rule "a neuter word with a non-neuter..." <note>The commentator is explaining a technical point of Sanskrit grammar regarding how the verb agrees with the list of humors</note>.

# Chapter Ten

->The eighth sign in the body of Time, or the planet aspecting the eighth house,<-
->wherever it is situated at the time of birth, there a disease will arise in that limb. 5.<-

->When Saturn is conjoined with the Sun or others, the specific tissue (bone, etc.) assigned to them<-

---

Otherwise, there would be a contradiction with the grammatical rule "optionally in others." Alternatively, one should supply the words "these afflictions are proclaimed" to complete the sense. This should be considered in other similar passages as well. Some read "illustrated" instead of "proclaimed." 4.

### Regarding "In the limbs of Time"
In the limbs of Time: among those mentioned in the verse beginning with "The measure of Varaha..." <note>A reference to the *Brihat Jataka*, a foundational text by Varahamihira</note>. In whichever limb: the origin or birth of the diseases associated with that planet or sign. 5.

### Regarding "Planet..."
Here the word "quality" <term>guna: usually meaning virtue, but here referring to physical properties</term> does not denote the opposite of a defect, but rather the bodily tissues, the three humors, and the elemental fires. This is clarified by the half-verse beginning with "The tissues and..." 6, 7.

### Regarding "Saturn..."
Of those: meaning of the Sun and the other planets. In that tissue mentioned in the eighth house: the word "man" is also indicative of women. 8.

### Regarding "By the Sun..."
This should be interpreted by carrying forward the phrase "when Saturn is aspected." In the right limb: in the right part of the body. A wound: an ulcer. Arising from blood: produced from the blood. Although the word for wound <note>original: "arus"</note> is neuter in the lexicon due to its association with the word for "sore," it is used here in the masculine gender because it is modified by the masculine adjective "arising from blood." One should not argue that the adjective should be neuter, as this reading is supported by many manuscripts. Alternatively, based on the grammatical rule "gender is not strictly taught as it depends on popular usage," the masculine gender must be accepted. Or another lexicon should be sought—enough on this. In short, this applies everywhere in the natural state. Thus, the truth is that these are the symptoms of the disease causing death. If not aspected: when not seen by any planet, then cough, asthma, etc. Very long: meaning lasting for a very long time or chronic.

# The Path of Inquiry
<page-num>156</page-num>

When Saturn is joined <note>with specific planets</note>. Venus and the Moon are the water-planets. By their proportion, one may fall into hot water; or fall into a well. The phrase "if the defect is not present" <note>original: "dose asati"</note> is the word-split. Even in the absence of the aforementioned defects, death occurs in water due to the presence of the water element, the location in a water-sign, or conjunction with water-planets. Here, some split the words as "if the defect is present" <note>original: "dose sati"</note>. This means the defect occurs through conjunction or aspect with Rahu <note>the North Node</note> and Gulika <note>a mathematical point in space considered malefic</note>. This is appropriate. Only through the presence of conjunction or aspect with Rahu and Gulika is a "bad death" <term>Durmriti: an unnatural or accidental death</term> generally established. Just as Saturn's connection with the earth-element specifies the nature of death, so too does Saturn's connection with the water-element establish the specific form of death in water; this should be understood as logical.

Regarding the "Elemental Status" <note>original: "Bhuta-sthiti"</note>: "In a decanate <term>Drekkana: a 10-degree division of a zodiac sign</term>, there are three Ninth-parts <term>Navamsha: a 3.33-degree division</term>; these are joined with four 'watches' <note>Yamas</note>. In odd signs, the sequence of elements begins with Earth; in even signs, it begins with Sky <note>Ether</note>. The durations are: one and a quarter measures <note>Nadika</note>, one measure, three-quarters of a measure, half a measure, and a quarter measure respectively for the watches." Thus, the five elements are to be determined from the planetary longitudes. In one decanate, there are three Ninth-parts. In one Ninth-part (consisting of fifteen measures), there are four watches. Each watch is three and three-quarter measures long. There, in the first and third watches, the elements follow the order starting from Earth; in the second and fourth, they follow the order starting from Sky. Specifically: Earth is 1.25 measures, Water is 1 measure, Fire is 0.75 measures, Air is 0.5 measures, and Sky is 0.25 measures. This is how the elemental status is known. || 16 ||

---

> If Saturn stands in a decanate with a "Boar-face,"
> death is caused by herds of deer <note>or wild animals</note>;
> if in a "Vulture-face," then by birds.
> Even there, if there is a lack of strength, and
> conjunction with Gulika and the Sun <note>original: Bhaskara</note> occurs;
> If the lords of the house occupied by Gulika <note>Mandi</note>,
> such as the Sun and others, are weak and in unfavorable houses,
> they bring death respectively through: father, mother,
> siblings, relatives, children, or wife—or by one's own hand. || 17 ||

---

Regarding the verse "In the decanate...": The word "Saturn" should be supplied. When Saturn stands in a "Boar-face" <note>Kolamukha</note> decanate, death is connected to herds of animals. In a "Vulture-face" <note>Gridhranana</note> decanate, it is by birds. In both these combinations, the word "Gulika" also implies Rahu. Because of their conjunction or aspect, an unnatural death is indicated. Alternatively, the word "and others" <note>original: adi</note> refers to the conjunction and aspect of Rahu. "By the Suns" refers to Saturn <note>as the son of the Sun</note>. "In unfavorable houses": If the Sun and the lords of Gulika's house are weak and poorly placed, death is caused by the father. If the Moon and others are so placed, it is caused by the mother and so on. "Self" implies suicide. The classification of decanates as "Boar-faced" and so on should be understood from the Chapter on Decanates in Varahamihira's *Brihat Jataka*. || 17 ||

# Prashnamarga
<page-num>158</page-num>

Mars <note>original: "Bhumija," son of the earth</note> and Mercury cause cold fever and mental confusion. Jupiter causes diseases arising from the imbalance of the three humors <note>original: "Sannipata," a complication of Vata, Pitta, and Kapha</note> and a lack of mental clarity. || 23 ||

Venus <note>original: "Bhargava"</note> causes indigestion, swelling, burning sensations, and delusions. Saturn <note>original: "Taruninandana," son of the Sun</note> causes thirst, loss of appetite, and piercing pains throughout the body. || 24 ||

Rahu <note>original: "Ahi," the serpent</note> causes disturbances of the wind humor <note>Vata</note>, and Gulika <note>a mathematical point in space considered the son of Saturn</note> causes hiccups and headaches. These are the diseases proclaimed for the planets starting from the Sun and ending with Gulika. || 25 ||

When the Sun and other planets, or their specific divisions <note>Amshas</note>, are joined with the "Threefold Sensitive Point" <note>term: Trisphuta; a calculated point used in Vedic astrology to determine the lifespan and results of a query</note>, one should also consider those diseases which are said to bring death. || 26 ||

If the Moon is situated in the same sign as the rising degree <note>Lagnamsha</note> and the disease increases even slightly, it will surely lead to the death of the person asking the question. || 27 ||

The omen of "breaking the vessel" <note>Patrabhanjana</note> mentioned in relation to the rising sign and its divisions, and the signs associated with the Threefold Sensitive Point, should also be considered here. || 28 ||

->Here begins the Kanthabharanam <note>The "Necklace Ornament" commentary</note><-

Regarding the distinction between indigestion and swelling: Venus, being a watery planet, first causes indigestion and swelling, and subsequently causes burning sensations and delusions. Some interpret the phrase "indigestion and swelling" as connecting to the previous verse; in their view, these two are diseases of Jupiter. This is also logical, as Jupiter governs the phlegm humor <note>Kapha</note>, and indigestion and swelling are generally born of phlegm. In that case, the word "and" <note>atha</note> signifies a new beginning. Since both views are supported by logic, we believe these two terms should be applied to both planets, like a lamp placed in a doorway illuminating two rooms. || 21—25 ||

**Regarding "The Sun and others"**: These were proclaimed in the sixth chapter in the verses beginning with "Fever, heat, and so on." || 26 ||

**Regarding "The Moon"**: The meaning is that if the Moon is in the sign of the rising degree at the time of the query and the illness worsens, it leads to death. || 27 ||

**Regarding "The Rising Sign"**: The signs mentioned in the verse "If the Moon is in the sign of the rising degree," and the signs associated with the Threefold Sensitive Point mentioned in the verse "A quarrel within three days," both of these should be considered in the context of determining the signs of death. || 28 ||

**Regarding "Here"**: The following four verses are found in that source.

# Chapter Eleven

->If the Sun is the Lord of Death,<-
->there will be the arrival of a powerful person following a dispute.<-
->When death is imminent,<-
->the querent may also experience some form of quarrel. || 29 ||<-

->If it is the Moon, a woman arrives; if Mars,<-
->a craving for molasses and milk<-
->should be predicted for the patient, or indeed one should speak<-
->of the bringing of these two items.<-
->If Mercury, the arrival of a learned man; if Jupiter,<-
->of a Brahmin; if Venus,<-
->misfortune for priests or four-legged animals; if Saturn,<-
->the arrival of wicked or low-born people. || 30 ||<-

->If Death is joined with Rahu <note>original: "Phani" (the hooded serpent)</note> or Ketu <note>original: "Shikhi" (the crested one)</note>,<-
->the arrival of a beggar or a snake-charmer occurs;<-
->if Ketu is specifically there, a fall may happen<-
->when joined with Mars and the Moon.<-

**Regarding the Lord of Death...** The Lord of Death <term>Mrityupati: the planetary ruler of the specific mathematical point (sphuta) calculated to represent death</term> refers to the ruler of the sign where the death-point falls. "Of a powerful person" refers to someone who is prone to quarreling. The idea is that if either of these two signs is observed, one should declare that the death of the querent is near. The same logic applies to the following verses. || 29 ||

**Regarding the Moon...** The phrase "Lord of Death" carries over here. The construction is: "If the Moon is the Lord of Death." "The arrival of a woman" occurs at the house of the patient. "Craving" refers to the patient's desires. "Bringing" means the act of someone carrying or fetching something. Here, it refers to bringing it to the patient's house. "Of these two" refers to the molasses and milk. "If Jupiter, the arrival of a Brahmin <note>a member of the priestly or scholarly caste</note>" is the connection to be made. || 30 ||

**Regarding Death...** That "Death" <note>referring to the planetary influence</note> results in the arrival of a beggar or a snake-charmer, which serves as a sign of death; this is how the connection is made. "In that Death" refers to the calculated point of mortality. In a query regarding longevity and health, these rules starting with "The Lord of Death" are spoken; these very things become the signs of the end of sickness. However, regarding the "Lord of the Body" <term>Dehanatha</term> and "Lord of Life" <term>Prananatha</term>, these two should be substituted in place of "Death" for specific calculations. || 31 ||

# Chapter Eleven

### Chapter Eleven

Death occurs in a foreign land if the sign of death is a movable sign; on the road if it is a dual sign; and in one's own country if it is a fixed sign.
Depending on whether the sign of death is of the nature of a village, a forest, or water, death occurs in a village, a forest, or near water.
In clean places or in "barbarian" <note>original: "mleccha" - referring to foreign or non-Vedic lands</note> lands, in low-lying or elevated areas, in the houses of benefics or malefics, or in downward-facing or upward-facing signs—one should also indicate details such as lamps and other conditions at the time of death, just as one does for the time of birth, by examining this eighth house. || 34 ||

Based on the sign occupied by the stronger of the two—the lord of the Ascendant <term>Lagna: the rising sign at birth</term> or the lord of the Navamsha <term>Navamsha: a one-ninth divisional chart used for finer detail</term> of the Ascendant—one should predict death in one's own place, another's place, or on the road. || 35 ||

If that strongest planet is joined with or aspected by other planets, then the death of living beings occurs in the locations associated with the most powerful among them. These locations—such as temples, watery places, and so on—are determined by the specific nature of the signs. || 36 ||

If there is any planet that occupies the Ascendant, is joined with the lord of the Ascendant, or aspects either of them, some authorities say that death occurs in a house that is either dilapidated or newly renovated, according to the nature of that planet. || 37 ||

**On the manner of death:** Regarding the phrase "In the house of death," if it is a movable sign, death is in a foreign land, and so forth. Regarding "clean," if the house of death belongs to a benefic planet, it is in a clean place; if it belongs to a malefic, it is in a "barbarian" land. In a "downward-facing" sign, it is in a low-lying area; in an "upward-facing" sign, it is in an elevated area. The characteristics of the lamp <note>referring to whether a lamp is burning at the time of death</note> will be explained later in the section on questions regarding sexual union. || 34 ||

**On one's own birth:** The meaning is that one should determine the outcome based on whether the lord of the Ascendant or the lord of the Ascendant's Navamsha is stronger, looking at their position in movable signs, etc., and in the houses of benefics or malefics, just as described in the previous verse. || 35 ||

**Regarding "That":** This refers to the planet mentioned in the previous verse. "Among those joined or aspecting" refers to the one possessing the greatest strength. "In temples, watery places, etc." refers to the locations taught by Varahamihira <note>A famous 6th-century Indian astronomer and polymath</note> in the verse: "Temples, water, fire, pleasure-grounds, treasuries, bedrooms, and barren lands are the places in order [of the planets]." The death of embodied beings is linked to these. || 36 || <note>Likely a typo for 36 in the original print.</note>

**Regarding the Ascendant:** 1. A planet in the Ascendant, 2. one joined with the lord of the Ascendant, 3. one aspecting the Ascendant, or 4. one aspecting the lord of the Ascendant. Based on the strongest among these, death is said by some teachers to occur in houses described by Varahamihira's verse: "In a dilapidated house if Saturn is strong, in a renovated one if Mars is strong, in a burnt one if the Sun is strong," and so on. || 37 ||

## Prashna Marga <note>The Path of Inquiry</note>

## Concerning the Determination of the Place of Death.

-> Having understood the time and all other factors, and having discerned <-
-> their auspicious or inauspicious nature, <-
-> if all factors are favorable, one should predict the quick healing of disease <-
-> and a long span of life. <-
-> If all factors are unfavorable, death will occur shortly; <-
-> but if there is a mixture of these factors, <-
-> there will be a slow recovery from illness or a slow death, depending on whether <-
-> the favorable or unfavorable indications are in the majority. || 38 || <-

-> When death has been thus determined after such investigation, <-
-> one should then specify to the inquirers <-
-> the time, the diseases, and the locations of that event. || 39 || <-

-> || Thus ends the Eleventh Chapter in the Prashna Marga || <-

***

**Regarding "This" [the previous section]...** This refers to what was stated previously, such as "Death occurs in a moveable sign," and so forth.

**Regarding "Having understood"...** By the word "time" and others <note>original: "kaladi"</note>, the text includes the collection of factors such as the location, one's own breath <term>Prana: the vital breath used in divination</term>, the planetary periods, and the possibilities regarding the exit-path of the soul. "The auspicious or inauspicious nature" refers to the quality of that time and place. "Quickly" <note>original: "aram"</note> means speedily. The phrase "death will occur shortly" is the relevant connection here. "Of those" refers to the favorable and unfavorable signs. If the "good" or favorable signs are in the majority, there is a "slow" or gradual subsiding of illnesses; if the "bad" or unfavorable signs are in the majority, there is a "slow" or lingering death. || 38 ||

**Regarding "Thus"...** "Of that" refers to the death. "In the manner shown" means according to the methods demonstrated. One should "specify" or declare: "At this time, in this place, by this disease, and in this manner, death will occur." || 39 ||

-> || Thus ends the Eleventh Chapter in the Prashna Marga || <-

# Chapter Twelve

## The belly, heart, head, chest,
## thighs, face, knees, and the pair of feet
## are the limbs of the Sun and other planets;
## disease should be predicted through those planets
## that are weak or poorly situated. // 7 //

**The Sun and others**: This refers to the planets starting from the Sun and ending with Rahu <note>The North Node of the Moon</note>. Ketu <note>The South Node of the Moon</note> is not to be considered in this specific context because no specific limb has been assigned to it. Furthermore, the positions of Rahu and Ketu are fixed at a seventh-house distance from each other. If both were considered, one of them would almost always be "poorly situated," making a "healthy" reading impossible. This would contradict the traditional practice of divination <term>Prashna: the art of answering specific questions based on the time they are asked</term>. Some other teachers suggest that Rahu represents the right foot and Ketu the left foot. They also believe that even if a planet is poorly situated, if it is in a favorable division or aspected by benefits, no disease should be predicted. This view is weak, as it lacks clear scriptural authority and does not follow the tradition of the elder practitioners. This system of assigning limbs to planets must be applied consistently. // 7 //

## The head and other limbs should be assigned
## to the houses starting from the Ascendant and their lords.
## The limb associated with a house or planet
## occupied by a cruel planet is where the seeker's disease lies. // 8 //

**The head and others**: These should be placed as follows: the head in the Arudha <note>The sign rising at the time of a query</note>, the face in the second house, the chest in the third, and so on, until the two feet in the twelfth house. Similarly, the head is assigned to the lord of the Ascendant, the face to the lord of the second house, and so on. Whichever house contains a "cruel" <note>malefic</note> planet, or whichever house lord is joined with a malefic, the disease should be declared in the limb corresponding to that house or planet. // 8 //

## By the sign touched by the seeker, by the Arudha,
## or by the rising sign, one should state the location of the disease;
## for this has been explained in the context of the Arudha. // 9 //

**By the sign touched**: It has been said: "In whichever limb-sign is touched, or is the Arudha, or is rising—if that sign is joined by a sinning <note>malefic</note> planet, one should predict illness in that limb." // 9 //

## The relationship to the three humors
## was previously mentioned as taught by Varahamihira.
## Now, I shall state what is said in the *Sarasangraha*. // 10 //

**Previously mentioned**: This refers to the verse beginning with "Bile, wind, and phlegm..." <note>original: "pittaṃ vātakaphau pittaṃ"</note>. I shall explain this in the following verse. // 10 //

**Regarding "Bile" etc. ||** The humors shown according to the opinion of Varahamihira <note>A 6th-century polymath and foundational astrologer</note> are the primary ones for those planets. Those shown in the *Sara Sangraha* are the secondary or accompanying humors. For example, the Sun primarily causes bile with wind as a secondary factor, and so on. || 11 ||

**Regarding "Diseases" etc. ||** "According to their respective five elements" means relying on the power of the five elements assigned to them. The grammar here implies a cause or motive. The seasons mentioned are those corresponding to the time of the inquiry. The following two verses are quoted from other scientific treatises. || 12 ||

**Regarding "Poorly placed" etc. ||** By the word "bile," fire is also understood; as Vagbhata <note>A famous ancient Ayurvedic physician</note> says, "Bile is fire." "Water-born" refers to conditions like swelling <note>edema</note> and enlargement of the abdomen <note>ascites</note>. "Wind" refers to both the humor and the general element. The connection of planets to seasons should be understood from the words of Varahamihira, such as "The seasons starting with Late Winter belong to Saturn, etc." and "Summer belongs to the Sun and Mars." || 14 ||

**Regarding "Givers of disease" etc. ||** The tissues <term>Dhatus</term> are those indicated in verses such as "Bone, blood, etc." <note>referring to the astrological mapping of Sun to bone, Moon to blood, etc.</note>. The verse to be mentioned next is from another text. || 15 ||

# Chapter Twelve

The disease of patients should be declared based on the planet causing the illness being situated in a poorly placed <term>Dhatu</term><note>Dhatu refers to the seven fundamental tissues of the body: plasma, blood, muscle, fat, bone, marrow, and reproductive fluid.</note> or bone. Alternatively, in a query regarding disease, the illness resides in the <term>Dhatu</term><note>In this context, specific planetary divisions are mapped to bodily tissues.</note> associated with the portion of the sign <insert>the Navamsha</insert> occupied by the planet causing the disease. || 16 ||

There are various classifications for determining the different types of diseases. These are also written here as described in other authoritative scriptures. || 17 ||

Diseases are to be understood as being of two types: Innate <note>original: "Nija"</note> and Accidental <note>original: "Agantuka"</note>. Both the Innate and the Accidental are again each of two types. || 18 ||

Innate diseases arise from the body or the mind, caused by seen or unseen factors. Likewise, Accidental diseases are also of four kinds <note>The commentator clarifies this as a total of four primary categories of disease.</note>. || 19 ||

Those arising from Wind <note>Vata</note>, Bile <note>Pitta</note>, and Phlegm <note>Kapha</note>, as well as those born from their dual combinations or the triple combination of all three <note>Sannipata</note>, are proclaimed as bodily ailments. || 20 ||

These bodily diseases should be understood through the eighth house, its lord, the planet aspecting it, or the planet occupying it; the diseases caused by them are determined by their respective strengths. || 21 ||

Mental diseases, born from the impulses of anger, fear, grief, and the like, are to be known through the mutual relationship between the lord of the eighth house and the lord of the mind <insert>the fifth house</insert>, or by their presence in the <term>Trines</term><note>The 1st, 5th, or 9th houses.</note> and other positions. || 22 ||

---

**Regarding "The planet causing the illness..."** || The disease-giver is poorly situated. The "portion" refers to the <term>Navamsha</term><note>A 1/9th division of a zodiac sign used for fine-tuned analysis.</note>. || 16 ||

**Regarding "There are..."** || The subsequent seven verses are from another scripture. || 17 ||

**Regarding "Diseases..."** || Similarly, Accidental diseases are caused by seen and unseen factors; this is the arrangement. Thus, the essence is that there are four types of diseases: 1. Innate arising in the body, 2. Innate arising in the mind, 3. Accidental from a seen cause <note>e.g., an injury</note>, and 4. Accidental from an unseen cause <note>e.g., a curse or spirits</note>. || 18, 19 ||

**Regarding "Wind, Bile..."** || Among the four types shown, the first <insert>Innate bodily</insert> is explained here. "Combination" refers to the union of two humors <note>Doshas</note>. That is of three kinds: 1. Wind and Bile, 2. Wind and Phlegm, 3. Bile and Phlegm. Including the individual humors and the triple combination, it should be understood that seven types of bodily ailments are produced. || 20 ||

**Regarding "Through the eighth..."** || Of these four types, the Innate bodily ones are caused by these <insert>the 8th house factors</insert>. || 21 ||

**Regarding "Anger..."** || Innate mental diseases are described by this verse. By the word "and the like," the intention is the relationship between the lord of the eighth house and the lord of the fifth house, such as being in mutual angular positions <note>Kendras</note>. || 22 ||

Afflictions arising from curses, black magic, or physical injuries are known as "visible causes." These should be understood through the sixth house, its lord, the planet occupying the eighth house from the sixth, or the planet joined with the sixth lord. || 23 ||

When the lord of the eighth house is connected to the sixth house, these curses and similar afflictions are particularly powerful. However, afflictions arising from "invisible causes" <note>referring to karma from past lives</note> are to be understood through the "Obstruction-causing" planets <term>Badhaka: planets that hinder specific zodiac signs</term>. || 24 ||

In other texts, it is said that the types of diseases can also be identified by whatever objects are seen or heard by chance at the time of the inquiry. || 25 ||

If an object that is considered "unwholesome" <term>Apathya: food or habits that aggravate a disease</term> for a specific illness is seen or heard during the consultation, one should conclude that the patient is suffering from that particular disease. || 26 ||

->**Here follows the Heart of the Eight Branches of Medicine.**<-
<note>original: "Ashtanga Hridayam," a foundational Sanskrit text on Ayurveda</note>

The tastes are sweet, sour, salty, bitter, pungent, and astringent. Among these, the first three <note>sweet, sour, salty</note> pacify Wind <term>Vata: the biological humor associated with air and movement</term>. The three beginning with bitter <note>bitter, pungent, astringent</note> pacify Phlegm <term>Kapha: the humor associated with earth and water</term>. || 27 ||

Astringent, bitter, and sweet pacify Bile <term>Pitta: the humor associated with fire and metabolism</term>. The others <note>sour, salty, pungent</note> increase it. In brief, there are three humors: Wind, Bile, and Phlegm. || 28 ||

---

**Regarding "Curses" etc.** — Afflictions born of curses and the like are "visible" external arrivals. These are identified by the four factors: the sixth house, its lord, and so on. "Invisible" refers to the ripening of actions performed in previous births. These external afflictions are known through the "Obstruction-causing" planets. || 23-24 ||

**Regarding "Seen"** — This point should also be applied as stated. "By chance" means occurring unexpectedly. || 25 ||

**Regarding "Whose"** — The knowledge of what is wholesome or unwholesome depends on the science of Life <note>Ayurveda</note>. To provide that knowledge briefly, a passage is quoted here from the *Heart of the Eight Branches of Medicine*. || 26 ||

**Regarding "Here"** — The following two verses are located in the *Heart of the Eight Branches of Medicine*.

**Regarding "Tastes"** — The tastes like "sweet" are well-known. The first three are sweet, sour, and salty. The three starting with bitter <note>bitter, pungent, astringent</note> destroy Phlegm. Astringent, bitter, and sweet destroy Bile. The others <note>the remaining three for each category</note> nourish or increase Wind and the others. Thus, it is established that bitter, pungent, and astringent tastes are "unwholesome" for Wind-related diseases. By saying "in brief," it should be understood that when explained in detail, these humors become many-faceted. || 28 ||

> Whichever humor—such as bile and the rest—is attributed as a defect to a specific planet, the disease arising from that planet should be declared as a disorder born of that specific humor. || 29 || <note>The author refers to the Ayurvedic theory of the three humors: Vata (wind), Pitta (bile), and Kapha (phlegm).</note>
>
> Through the planetary combinations mentioned in the *Hora* and other foundational texts, when planets are aspected by malefics, one should also identify the various types of diseases arising from the misdeeds of previous births. || 30 || <note>original: "prāg-janma-durita-udbhavāḥ". > 1. If Jupiter is in the Ascendant and Saturn or Mars is in the seventh house;
> 2. If Saturn is in the Ascendant and Mars is in the seventh, fifth, or ninth house;
> 3. If Mercury and the Moon are together in a state of combustion;
> 4. If the waning Moon and Saturn are in the twelfth house;
> 5. If the waning Moon is joined with a malefic and occupies the first, eleventh, fifth, or ninth house;
> 6. If Saturn is in the seventh house joined with a malefic;
> 7. If <term>Gulika</term> <note>The son of Saturn, a mathematical point used in Vedic astrology to denote malefic influence.</note> is in the second, third, sixth, eighth, or twelfth house;

---

**Regarding "Whichever..."** || If the Sun is the cause of the disease, it is a disorder born of bile. If it is the Moon, it should be understood as a disease born of wind and phlegm, and so on. || 29 ||

**Regarding "Through the malefics..."** || *Hora* here refers to the *Brihat Jataka* of Varahamihira. By the characteristics explained in that and other texts, one determines the diseases produced by unseen causes <note>i.e., Karma</note>. || 30 ||

**Regarding "Now..."** || After describing diseases in general, the author intends to describe specific diseases, and thus first demonstrates the characteristics of insanity.

**Regarding "If Jupiter is in the Ascendant..."** || The phrase "Mercury and the Moon in combustion" is a specific compound. One should not interpret "Swanta" as the second and twelfth houses; rather, "Swanta" refers to the fifth house. There is no authority for interpreting the word "Anta" as the twelfth house here. Nor is it proper to suggest a different reading of the text, as that would contradict many ancient manuscripts. Furthermore, such an interpretation would make the combination of "the waning Moon and Saturn in the twelfth house" redundant. In the phrase "in the second, third, sixth, eighth, or twelfth," the condition "joined with a malefic" should also be applied. Otherwise, this would have been mentioned in the general section on house results. <term>Vit</term> <note>original: "vit". A technical synonym for the planet Mercury.</note> refers to Mercury. || 31, 32 ||

The causes of mental disorders <note>original: "unmada," referring to a range of psychiatric conditions or "madness"</note>, the behaviors of those afflicted, and the various classifications of these ailments are described here as they have been specified in other authoritative scriptures. || 33 ||

From excessive joy, desire, fear, or grief; from eating incompatible or impure foods; and from the wrath of teachers or deities, five types of mental disorders arise. || 34 ||

These are known as those born from the three humors <note>Vata, Pitta, and Kapha</note>, the combination of all three <note>Sannipata</note>, and those caused by external influences <note>Agantu, often referring to spiritual or providential causes</note>. Laughing, clapping hands, loud lamentation, singing, dancing, and weeping; || 35 ||

Acting out of place, flailing the limbs, a reddish or pale and thin body, strength returning after food is digested, and excessive talking—these are the characteristics of **Vata-induced mental disorder**. || 36 ||

Agitation, impatience, cleverness <note>or cunning</note>, rushing at others, threatening behavior, a desire for shade, cold food, and water, anger, and a yellowish, hot body <note>feverishness</note> [are the signs of **Pitta-induced mental disorder**]. || 37 ||

A desire for women and solitude, sleepiness, lack of appetite, speaking very little, salivation, vomiting, strength returning immediately after eating, and whiteness in the nails and eyes; || 38 ||

These behaviors of **Pitta and Kapha mental disorders** are stated in the verses in their respective order. A mental disorder showing mixed symptoms from all three humors is considered incurable and should be avoided. || 39 ||

The external causes <note>Agantu</note> are known as "seizers" <term>Graha: entities or spirits that "grasp" a person's consciousness</term>; these include gods, demons, and others. They are immortal and endowed with immense strength, speech, knowledge, and prowess. || 40 ||

In Vata-induced disorder, the drinking of medicated oils <note>Snehapana</note> is prescribed; in Pitta-induced disorder, purgation; in Kapha-induced disorder, nasal drops and emetics; and for external causes, all these actions combined. || 41 ||

All mental disorders are destroyed by the performance of prayers, fire offerings, and similar spiritual rites. || 42 ||

**Regarding joy and desire...** <note>referring to verse 34</note> There are five types: Vata-born, Pitta-born, Kapha-born, the combined type, and the external type.

The verse and a half starting with **"Laughing..."** describes the symptoms of Vata-induced disorder. The verse starting with **"Agitation..."** describes Pitta-induced disorder. The verse starting with **"Women..."** describes Kapha-induced disorder. The external causes are the "seizers" <note>Grahas</note> such as gods, demons, and serpents <note>Nagas</note>. Their names and characteristics will be explained in detail in the fifteenth chapter. Among them, the characteristics of a "God-seizer" include great strength, speech, and knowledge. ## Chapter Twelve

->There is a specific tradition cited by the ancient teachers;<-

->One should diagnose the insanity as arising from irregular eating or fasting. || 46 ||<-

->If these same planets are joined with Ketu or Mandi <note>Ketu is the South Node of the Moon; Mandi is a sensitive mathematical point in Vedic astrology associated with Saturn</note>, it arises from impure food.<-

The specific treatments for these types have been stated. "All actions" refers to all procedures starting with the drinking of medicated fats <term>Snehapana: the internal administration of medicated oils or ghee</term>. "All" implies that rituals like chanting <note>Japa</note> and fire offerings <note>Homa</note> are common to all types of insanity. The word "Thus" signifies the conclusion of the teachings from other scriptures. || 34 — 42 ||

**Regarding "Tradition" etc. ||** That specific tradition is written immediately following in these four verses. || 43 ||

**Regarding "Irregular eating" etc. ||** 1. Irregular eating <term>Vishama-ashana</term> is defined as "eating too much or too little at the wrong time." 2. Impure food refers to both the impurity of the person eating and the impurity of the food itself. 3. Fasting. 4. Fear. 5. Detachment <note>Vairagya</note> = an aversion to sensory objects caused by the shattering of one's desires. 6. Baseless anger = anger without cause. 7. Malevolent magic <term>Abhichara</term> performed by enemies. 8. Insulting a teacher = speaking ill of one's preceptor. 9. Insulting the fire; this also includes the failure to perform fire sacrifices. 10. Insulting the gods. These are the ten. Even though they arise from these ten causes, they are included within the three categories of Vata-insanity, etc. Among them, in Pitta-type insanity characterized by agitation and impatience, restraint <note>physical binding or confinement</note> must be employed. || 44, 45 ||

**Regarding "Moon" etc. ||** "Unfavorable transits" <term>Gochara-itara-gah</term> means being situated in inauspicious astrological houses. "Irregular eating" <note>Vishama-ashti</note> refers to improper consumption. || 46 ||

**Regarding "Ketu" etc. ||** "In these" refers to the Moon, Venus, and the lord of the eighth house. If Mars is in the fifth house, it arises from anger. For these insanities arising from ten causes, the use of *Kalyanaka* and *Panchagavya* clarified butter <note>medicated ghees used in Ayurveda for mental health</term> is recommended.

# Prashnamarga
## Page 172

->If malefic planets are situated in the sixth house, the illness arises from anger or black magic.<-
->If malefic planets are situated in the ninth house, it arises from the curse of a Guru <note>teacher or elder</note> or similar figures. (48)<-
->In such cases, the consumption of *Kalyana Panchagavya Ghrita* <note>a medicated ghee prepared from five products of the cow</note> and similar remedies should be prescribed. (49)<-

Now, the characteristics of *Apasmara* <term>Apasmara: traditionally translated as epilepsy or falling sickness</term> are described.

->If Saturn is in the eighth house and Rahu <note>the North Node of the Moon</note> is in a trine <note>the 1st, 5th, or 9th houses</note>, while the benefics are strong;<-
->Or if the Sun or Mars are in unfavorable positions, these yogas <note>astrological combinations</note> cause epilepsy. (50)<-

->Epilepsy is divided into twelve distinct types based on its manifestation.<-
->These types and their specific natures are now being described. (51)<-

->With limbs collapsing, the person suddenly falls to the ground, losing consciousness;<-
->Foaming at the mouth, making harsh noises, the body remains stiff for a long time.<-
->With eyes rolling, biting the teeth, turning yellow, and acting heedlessly;<-
->Obsessed with water and with a distorted face—this is the nature of epilepsy. (52)<-

**Now** || The meaning is that because of the similarity in their mental nature, the characteristics of epilepsy are described immediately after insanity.

**Saturn etc.** || "In unfavorable positions" means located in the eighth house or other such malefic houses. The Sun alone, if placed in the eighth or other bad houses, can cause epilepsy. The same applies to Mars. The first half of the verse describes one combination. Thus, there are three combinations for epilepsy mentioned here. (50)

**Divided into** || In reality, epilepsy is a single condition. However, there are twelve "messengers" <note>symbolic manifestations or spirits</note> that possess different forms. Therefore, due to these external differences, twelve varieties of epilepsy are conceptualized. The intent is to describe the general nature of epilepsy as well as the forms of these twelve messengers. (51)

**With limbs collapsing** || "Suddenly" means unexpectedly. "Limbs collapsing" means the parts of the body become loose and unable to support the person. "Makes noises" means crying out. "Rolling eyes" refers to eyes moving in a circular motion. "Obsessed with water" means being distressed by intense thirst. "Distorted face" means displaying various facial contortions. Some believe this epilepsy is caused by possession by deities <note>original: "devata-avesha-janya"</note> and is not merely a physical disease like a fever. For this reason, the primary remedies are prayers and fire sacrifices. Others, however, believe that the humors like wind <note>Vata</note> are the cause and classify it accordingly. The noble ancients even attributed living deities to stationary objects. Thus, even Sayanacharya <note>a famous 14th-century commentator</note> explained in his works that diseases like fever each have their own deity and specific forms. It is well known that Parvati is the daughter of the Himalayas. Puranic scholars say the sons of Prachetas married the daughter of the trees. Similarly, the story of the Earth taking the form of a cow to express her grief to Brahma is consistent with this worldview. (52)

### Shvasana, Malina, Nidra, Jrimbhika, and Anashana;

### One should perform a fire oblation with sesame seeds using the Sudarshana mantra or the Krodhagni mantra. || 56 ||

### For the pacification of terrible Epilepsy, one should recite a thousand repetitions for every letter of the mantra. || 57 ||

### Having consulted other texts regarding the diagnosis of Epilepsy,
### Certain beneficial medical treatments are also being written down here. || 58 ||

### A powder made from Rock Salt, *Vrischikaali*, *Kushta*, Long Pepper, and *Bharngi*;
### Should be applied to the nose <note>Nasya: the Ayurvedic practice of administering herbal powders or oils through the nostrils</note>; this is praised for pacifying acute Epilepsy in men. || 59 ||

**Regarding Shvasana etc.** || The twelve "messengers" or spirits of Epilepsy, beginning with Shvasana, are shown here by name. They manifest behaviors in the patient corresponding to their names. **Shvasana** <note>The Breather</note> causes obstruction of breath. **Malina** <note>The Soiled</note> makes the body dirty. **Nidra** <note>Sleep</note> causes excessive sleepiness. **Jrimbhika** <note>The Yawner</note> causes constant yawning. **Anashana** <note>The Non-eater</note> destroys the desire for food. The others should be understood in the same way. Regarding that Epilepsy... || 55 ||

**Regarding Pacification** || The pumpkin sacrifice is prescribed in the *Mantra Shastra* <note>The science of sacred sounds and rituals</note>. **Sudarshana** and **Krodhagni** are specific sacred mantras. Sesame seeds are the material for the fire offering. "A thousand for every letter" means repeating the mantra a thousand times for each syllable it contains. By the word "terrible," it is established that even the most severe forms of Epilepsy are pacified by this practice. || 57 ||
