# Chapter Twelve

The identification of body parts such as the head, throat, or pelvis is determined by whether the rising sign <term>Lagna; the zodiacal sign ascending on the eastern horizon</term> is movable, upward-facing, or rising by the head, and not solely by the decan <term>Drekkana; a 10-degree subdivision of a sign</term>. || 79 ||

When the nature of the sign and its subdivision <term>Amsha</term> agree in being movable and so on, that nature is used. If they do not agree, or if the subdivision is unknown, the identification is made by whether the sign is upward-facing, downward-facing, or level. || 80 ||

When a planet is extremely weak, the body part is identified by the nature of its rising. This occurs when a planet is in its sign of debilitation, or in the last portions of Virgo or the beginning of Libra, where it becomes very powerless. || 81 ||

The arrangement of body parts starting from the head across the houses <term>Bhavas</term> is now described according to the *Krishniya* <note>A classical South Indian astrological text</note>. This specific method should be adopted in the practice of horary astrology <term>Prashna; the art of answering questions based on the time they are asked</term>. || 82 ||

The head is situated in the first house; the right and left sides are determined by the portions of the sign already passed or yet to come. Then follow the ears, eyes, nostrils, cheeks, and jaws, ending at the mouth. || 83 ||

Then the neck, shoulders, arms, sides, back, heart, stomach, and ending at the waist. Then the navel, pelvis, anus, and the private organs, two by two for the remaining houses. || 84 ||

**Regarding "Movable..."** || In the verse starting with "Throat," Varahamihira <note>A famous 6th-century Indian astronomer and astrologer</note> stated that body parts are identified only by the portions of the decans. However, that applies only to natal astrology <term>Jataka</term>. In horary astrology <term>Prashna</term>, there is a distinction: if the rising sign is movable, upward-facing, and rises by the head, it indicates the head and throat. If it is fixed, level-facing, and rises both ways, it indicates the throat and shoulders. If it is dual-natured, downward-facing, and rises by the feet, it indicates the pelvis, genitals, and anus. This is the specific rule. || 79 ||

**Regarding "Sign and subdivision..."** || If the movable, fixed, or dual nature of both the sign and its subdivision are the same, the body part should be determined by that nature. If they differ, or if the subdivision is not known, it is determined by whether the sign is upward-facing, downward-facing, or level-facing. || 80 ||

**Regarding "Extremely..."** || In any sign where the Sun is placed in the subdivision of Libra, or in the final decan of Virgo, or the first decan of Libra, the body part must be determined by the manner of the sign's rising <note>e.g., whether it rises head-first or feet-first</note>. || 81 ||

**Regarding "In the rising signs..."** || Now, the arrangement of body parts starting from the head across the rising signs as described in the *Krishniya* is written here. That same method should be accepted in the work of horary astrology. || 82 ||

**Regarding "The head..."** || The arrangement of the houses is divided: up to the "mouth" for the upper body, up to the "waist" for the middle body, and up to the "thighs" for the lower body. In this system, the portion of the first house <term>Lagna</term> yet to rise represents the right side of the head. The second house is the right ear. The third is the right eye. The fourth is the right nostril. The fifth is the right cheek. The sixth is the right jaw. For the seventh house, the portion already passed is the right interior of the mouth, and the portion yet to come is the left interior of the mouth. The eighth house is the left jaw. Similarly, the portion of the first house already passed represents the left side of the head. In the same way, the middle and lower body parts are assigned...

# Now begins the Thirteenth Chapter

## Now the timing of the onset and end of illness, etc., is described.

The number of stars <note>Nakshatras or lunar mansions</note> from the one rising at the horizon <note>the Ascendant or Lagna</note> to the one where the Moon is currently situated; counting that same number of stars forward from the Moon's position will reveal the time when the illness began. || 1 ||

Or, when the Moon reaches the twelfth-division <note>Dvadasamsha</note> of the ninth-division <note>Navamsha</note> of Mandi <note>a sensitive mathematical point in Vedic astrology associated with suffering</note>; or in the sign where Mandi and the Moon are conjoined—among these, the one that is most unfavorable to the querent should be taken as the start of the disease. || 2 ||

When the Moon, Sun, Jupiter, or Saturn are in a sign corresponding to the first letter of the messenger's speech <note>a technique where the first sound uttered by a person seeking help is mapped to a zodiac sign</note> and are in a highly afflicted state, one should declare the onset of the illness. || 3 ||

Whichever direction the patient or the messenger is facing when first seen, the onset of the illness for the querent should be declared to have occurred in that direction. || 4 ||

Counting from the East to the direction where the messenger stands while asking the question; the onset of the querent's disease occurred in the watch <note>Yama, a period of 3 hours</note> corresponding to that number. || 5 ||

---

**Now...** || This means that after describing the different types of diseases, the description of the timing of their onset, end, etc., is now undertaken as it is the current relevant topic.

**The number...** || "From the rising at the horizon" means from the star rising at the time of the query <term>Prashna: the branch of astrology dealing with specific questions</term>. "The Moon" refers to the Moon's position at the time of the query. || 1 ||

**Or...** || The longitude of Mandi multiplied by nine and then by twelve becomes the longitude of the "twelfth-division of the ninth-division." In that star, or in the star of the combined longitude of Mandi and the Moon—among these three stars mentioned in the previous verse and this one—the one that is most harmful to the seeker (such as the "Vipat" or "Pratyari" stars <note>specific stars in a person's birth chart indicating danger or enmity</note>) should be selected. The illness began there. || 2 ||

**The messenger...** || The connection is: when the Moon, Sun, Jupiter, or Saturn are in the sign indicated by the first letter of the messenger's words and are in a "highly afflicted" state. High affliction refers to being situated in unfavorable houses or being weakened. || 3 ||

**Whichever direction...** || "When first seen" refers to the very first moment of the query. The determination of the onset of illness is mentioned here because it is useful for the current context of timing. This is why the word "etc." was included in the opening promise. || 4 ||

**From the East...** || "In the watch corresponding to that number" refers to the three-hour periods starting from sunrise. If the question is asked from the East, it is the first watch. Likewise, if the question is asked from the Northeast, it is the eighth watch. || 5 ||

Otherwise, if the strength is nocturnal, the onset of disease is at night. If Mercury is the indicator, it should be predicted that the exact time of the disease's onset is not known. || 8 ||

# Chapter Thirteen

When the Moon resides in the zodiac sign occupied by the Lord of the Sixth House <note>The Sixth House traditionally governs disease and enemies</note>, the onset of illness occurs. Recovery from such ailments should be predicted when the Moon enters the sign occupied by the Lord of the Fourth House <note>The Fourth House represents comfort and healing</note>. || 10 ||

One should declare the beginning of a disease at the time when the Ascendant <term>Lagna: the rising sign at the time of inquiry</term>, the Lord of the Ascendant, or the Moon are joined with or aspected by <term>Aspected: influenced by the 'gaze' or positioning of another planet</term> malefic planets. When these three receive the association or aspect of benefic planets, the disease is subdued; if even one of them is so influenced, the process of healing begins. || 11 ||

Recovery from illness occurs when the Moon passes through the sign corresponding to the <term>Dvadasamsha: a 1/12th sub-division of a zodiac sign</term> of the rising <term>Navamsha: a 1/9th sub-division of a zodiac sign</term>, or when it moves past the sign occupied by <term>Gulika/Mandi: a sensitive mathematical point in the horoscope considered malefic</term>. || 12 ||

If an illness begins while the Moon is positioned in the Eighth House <note>The house of longevity and transformation</note> relative to its position at birth, recovery will take place once the Moon has fully transited past that eighth sign. || 13 ||

# From the Ritual Manual

->One should predict the arrival of disease due to poorly placed planets,<-
->And recovery due to well-placed planets.<-
->Healing comes through mantras, sacred dance, offerings, worship, and medicine,<-
->As well as through devotion to the deities and nourishing the bodily humors.<- || 14 ||

**The Meaning of This:**

**Regarding "The Lord of the Sixth..." ||** "Occupying the sign of the Lord of the Sixth" refers to the Moon's past position there. "Entering the sign of the Lord of the Fourth" refers to its future transit into that sign. || 10 ||

**Regarding "The Lord of the Ascendant..." ||** 1. The Ascendant, 2. The Lord of the Ascendant, and 3. The Moon. When these three were influenced by malefic planets in the past, the disease began. When any one of these receives a benefic influence in the future, healing starts. The implication is that when all three receive benefic influences, total health is regained. || 11 ||

**Regarding "The Ascendant..." ||** The methods for calculating the *Navamsha* and *Dvadasamsha* were shown previously. The "Sign of Mandi" refers to the sign occupied by Gulika at the time of the query <term>Prashna: the branch of astrology dealing with specific questions</term>. || 12 ||

**Regarding "The Moon in the Eighth..." ||** "Taking the lead" means considering the Moon's transit. This refers to the period before the Moon leaves the eighth sign counted from one's birth star <note>original: "Janma Nakshatra"</note>. || 13 ||

**Regarding "Here..." ||** The following two verses are taken from the *Anusthana-paddhati* <note>A manual on ritual procedures</note>.

**Regarding "Of this..." ||** The meaning of this verse is further clarified by the verse that follows it.

# Path of Inquiry
<note>original: "Prashnamarga," a 17th-century Sanskrit treatise on horary astrology</note>

When the Moon and other planets occupy signs belonging to the most harmful among the "bad houses" <note>malefic astrological houses, typically the 6th, 8th, or 12th</note>,
->the onset of disease is caused by the anger of the deity associated with that highly afflicted planet.<-
Similarly, when the Moon and others occupy signs belonging to the most favorable among the "good houses,"
->recovery from illness should be predicted through the worship of the respective deities, such as Indra and others.<-

The time of recovery and other outcomes are now described based on the constellation <note>Nakshatra</note> at the onset of the disease.

->In the constellations of Vaishva and Saumya, recovery occurs after a month; in Vasubha, Bradhna, and Shurpa, after a fortnight;<-
->in Chitra, Amcheta, Yama, and Hari, the patient finds relief after eleven days;<-
->in Magha, after twenty days; in Guru, Bhaga, Surasrit, Budhri, and Vadhna, after seven days;<-
->in Mula and Abhiyukta, after nine days; and in Hutabhuj, Mitra, and Pushan, recovery is achieved only with great difficulty. || 16 ||<-

***

**Regarding "When the Moon and others..."**: Among the "bad houses," one identifies the most harmful sign. "The Moon and others" refers to the Moon, the Sun, and Jupiter. The "highly afflicted planet" refers to the specific celestial body whose associated lord—such as Shambhu <note>Shiva</note> for the Sun, Durga for the Moon, and so on—is angry, thus causing the start of the disease. Similarly, among the "good houses," one identifies the most favorable sign where the Moon and others are situated. "Worship" includes the performance of mantras, sacred dance, and other rites. Here, "mantra" refers to the chanting of sacred syllables; "dance" refers to the ritual performance depicting the form of the deity; "oblation" refers to the offering of sacrifices; and "medicine" refers to medicinal pills and the like. "Worship of the deity" generally refers to the service of Durga in the form of worship at the three junctions of the day <note>dawn, noon, and sunset</note>. "Nourishing the elements" refers to medical treatment that sustains the body. For the Sun and the other planets, there are seven types of remedies starting with mantras. The word "Thus" <note>Sanskrit: iti</note> indicates the conclusion of this section of the ritual manual. || 15 ||

**Regarding "The onset of disease..."**: The word "and others" following "constellation" <note>tara</note> includes factors such as the lunar day <note>tithi</note>. The word "and others" following "recovery" includes the possibility of death.

**Regarding "In Vaishva..."**: The phrase "after" should be applied to all the timeframes mentioned. A "fortnight" means fifteen days. "Eleven days" <note>literally: the number of Rudras</note> refers to eleven days. "Seven days" <note>literally: the number of mountains</note> refers to a period of seven days. "After nine days" refers to the period following the ninth day. "With great difficulty" means that the specific number of days for recovery cannot be determined. || 16 ||

### Chapter Thirteen

->If a disease arises during the constellations of Jyeshtha <note>the 18th lunar mansion</note>, Svati, Arudra, or the three "Purvas" <note>Purva Phalguni, Purva Ashadha, and Purva Bhadrapada</note>, the patient does not survive.<-
->So too if the illness begins on "Chidra" <note>vulnerable or "pierced"</note> lunar days, or on an inauspicious weekday combined with the constellations of Krittika, Dhanishtha, Bharani, or Shatabhisha. || 17 ||<-

->The onset of disease is fatal if it begins on the eighth lunar day, the New/Full Moon days, or the "Rikta" <note>empty</note> days; or on an inauspicious weekday, or during the three birth-stars.<-
->Likewise, if it begins during the "Go-masa" <note>dangerous stars categorized as the 3rd, 5th, and 7th from the birth star</note> or when the Moon is in the eighth sign from birth. || 18 ||<-
->If the sun is positioned in the constellation of the patient's birth, or in the "Dhimanya" or "Putra" stars, the disease increases. If the sun is flanked on both sides by death-dealing stars, death occurs. : 19 :<-
->In the three stars flanking the "Dhimanya" and "Putra" positions, the disease worsens. In the remaining twelve stars, the patient lives. : 20 :<-
->When the stars, weekdays, and lunar days all signify death, and the "Shula-Chakra" <note>a specific astrological diagram used to predict pain or death</note> stars align, or if five of these factors coincide from the birth-star onwards, death is certain. || 21 ||<-

---

**Regarding "Jyeshtha" etc. ||** Death occurs in the seven stars starting with Jyeshtha. In the four starting with Krittika, if they coincide with "Chidra" days or inauspicious weekdays, the onset of disease gives death. The "Chidra" days are the 4th, 6th, 8th, 9th, 12th, and 14th. As the saying goes: "The dates known as Chidra are those named for the Sun (12), Vasu (8), and Limbs (6), along with the Rikta days (4, 9, 14)." || 17 ||

**Regarding "Ashtami" etc. ||** The "Three Birth Stars" <term>Trijanmabham: the birth star and its two repetitions in the 27-star cycle</term> refer to the natal constellation and its counterparts. "Go-masa" refers to the <term>Vipat, Pratyari, and Vadha</term> stars <note>the 3rd, 5th, and 7th stars from the birth star, considered dangerous in Vedic astrology</note>. The "Eighth Moon" is the Moon situated in the eighth sign from the birth sign. The onset of disease in these is death-dealing. If there is a combination of lunar day, weekday, and star as described in the previous verse, the disease is entirely incurable. If only the defects of the lunar day etc. mentioned in this verse are present, the disease might subside or death may not be immediate. The distinction is that the disease is "Yapya" <note>manageable but chronic</note>. || 18 ||

**Regarding "Arka" etc. ||** There are three stars on each of the two sides, making six. There is one on each side of the "Dhimanya" and "Putra" stars, making six. "Increase of disease" means the lengthening of the illness and living with great difficulty. In the remaining twelve, the disease is quickly pacified. Here, the calculation must include the star Abhijit <note>an intercalary 28th star</note>. Otherwise, there would only be eleven remaining stars, not twelve. This is known as the "Shula-Chakra" <note>Spike-Chart</note>. || 20 ||

**Regarding "Tara" etc. ||** 1. The Star, 2. The Weekday, 3. The Lunar Day, 4. The Shula-Chakra star, 5. The Birth-star sequence. If these five factors are death-giving at the onset of the disease, then the death of the inquirer must be declared as certain. By "Birth-star sequence," it means the three birth stars, the Vipat, Pratyari, and Vadha stars, and the eighth moon from birth...

Now, the cause of disease is stated. On this point, there is the word of the Authorities <note>Apta: trustworthy sages or experts</note>:

The sin committed in another birth <note>a previous life</note> manifests in the form of disease. Its pacification comes through medicines, gifts, prayers, burnt offerings, and purification rituals. (29)

For those afflicted by disease, the cause of illness is conceived here in many ways: from the possession by spirits, from the movement of the planets, or from the provocation of Wind, Bile, and the rest <note>the three humors or Doshas: Vata, Pitta, and Kapha</note>. ---

"From the provocation of Wind, Bile, and the rest"—by "the rest," Phlegm <note>Kapha</note> is included. "Provocation" also implies depletion, as that too is a cause of disease...

**Regarding "Mrityunjaya" etc. ||** This too is common to all diseases. It is to be "performed" or prescribed by the astrologer. "In all sacrifices" likewise refers to the feeding of Brahmins. This means it must be performed. This applies to all rituals, not just the *Mrityunjaya* sacrifice. "Authoritative" <note>Sanskrit: *āpta*</note> means one who is a source of valid knowledge. These four verses beginning here concern the subject of the *Mrityunjaya* fire sacrifice. || 36 ||

**Regarding "Severe" etc. ||** The word "and so on" includes all diseases. Therefore, it was said "for the pacification of all ailments." "Sacrifice" <note>Sanskrit: *havanam*</note> refers to the <term>homa</term> <note>A ritual where offerings are made into a consecrated fire.</note>. The phrase "not intended solely for longevity" is meant to address the misconception held by some ignorant people who think it only increases the lifespan. || 37 ||

**Regarding "Severe Fever" etc. ||** "Life-giving" <note>Sanskrit: *sañjīvanaḥ*</note> means that which bestows life. It refers to the ritual named *Mrityunjaya*. "Eight thousand in number" <note>Sanskrit: *aṣṭasahasra*</note>: this is interpreted as one thousand and eight, following a grammatical rule where the middle term is dropped. If one performs the sacrifice with the seven substances—such as <term>Amrita</term> <note>Tinospora cordifolia, a medicinal herb.</note> and others—repeating the offering 144 times for each, the total becomes 1,008 offerings. There are various other methods for this sacrifice as well. These should be learned from those who possess true spiritual knowledge. || 38 ||

**Regarding "Pacification" etc. ||** "Pacification" means the calming of disease and the like. "Nourishing" means that which brings prosperity. Excellent...

## Now the Houses are examined.

->The houses, such as children and others, should be declared even for an absent inquirer;<-
->They are easily spoken of once the age is known, for which reason that age is now explained. || 1<-
->If the Lord of the Ascendant is Mars, or if the Moon is in its infant stage, the age is not yet five years;<-

By this it is understood that even if fewer Brahmins are fed than the number of offerings made—according to one's means—there is no sin or transgression. The principle is that one should perform religious duty according to their capacity. The word "Thus" <note>original: "iti"</note> signifies the conclusion of the authoritative statement. || 39 ||

**This** : This refers to what has been demonstrated in this chapter.
| Thus ends the thirteenth chapter in the Path of Inquiry. |

**Now** || The sense is that after describing everything useful for determining longevity in the manner previously stated, the description of the Houses <term>Bhavas: the twelve astrological houses representing different life areas</term> is now undertaken in the fourteenth chapter, following the intended order. ||

Because attempting to describe matters like children for an infant would be a cause for ridicule, the age of the inquirer must be determined. The word "therefore" should be understood to follow "for which reason." || 1 ||

**If the Lord of the Ascendant** | The Moon is considered an "infant" <note>original: "bala"</note> until the fifth day of the bright fortnight. After the eighth day of the dark fortnight, it is considered "old." The phrase "years are not full" should be applied everywhere. If Mercury <note>original: "Induja"</note> is the Lord, eight years are not full, and so on. "Ten times seven" equals seventy. This applies if an "old" planet is in the Ascendant. One older than seventy is "very old." Regarding the "Serpent" <note>original: "Phanini"; referring to Rahu</note>, this applies when Rahu is rising, as it has no lordship over signs. When it is said the infant Moon is five and the old planet in the Ascendant is seventy...

# Chapter Fourteen

When Jupiter is at thirty degrees and the Sun is present, the strength is tenfold; likewise, the Moon's strength increases by sevenfold. Wisdom is greatly increased when Saturn or Rahu <note>original: "phani" - the serpent/North Node</note> are present, or when they are in the ascendant. || 2 ||

The excellence of the body, health, physical stature, prosperity, fame, happiness, victory, and the physical form—all these must be considered from the First House <note>original: "vilagna" - the ascendant</note>. || 3 ||

Those to be supported <note>original: "bhartavyam" - dependents or family members</note>, all wealth, speech, the right eye, and various types of knowledge—all this is to be considered from the Second House. || 4 ||

Courage, valor, wicked thoughts, the prowess of siblings, the right ear, and helpers—these are to be considered from the Third House. || 5 ||

Mother, friends, maternal uncles and nephews, landed property, happiness, vehicles, seating, elegance, water, bedding, growth, cattle, and the house of birth are considered from the Fourth House. || 6 ||

Wisdom, creative intuition, retentive memory, the power of discrimination, merit earned in past lives, sacred chants, ministers, and children—as well as peace of mind—are to be considered from the Fifth House. || 7 ||

---

It is understood that from the fifth day of the bright fortnight until the eighth day of the dark fortnight, the "age" <note>a technical measure of planetary strength</note> of the Moon should be calculated using the rule of three. When the Moon is in the sign of Cancer and situated in the ascendant, its age-measure must be determined according to its specific position at that time. || 2 ||

**Regarding the body:** "Excellence" means being endowed with auspicious marks. "Health" means freedom from disease. "Stature" refers to the specific physical build. "Victory" refers to success in legal disputes and similar matters. || 3 ||

**Regarding what is to be supported:** "Those to be supported" refers to the group of dependents. The connection is specifically to the "right eye." "Various types of knowledge" implies scholarship in the scriptures and skill in the arts. || 4 ||

**Regarding courage:** There is a slight difference between "valor" and "prowess." "Valor" is the possession of enthusiasm. "Prowess" is the habitual disposition to overcome enemies. "Right ear" refers to the organ of hearing on the right side. || 5 ||

**Regarding the mother:** "Elegance" means being approachable or pleasing. "Landed property" refers to fields and such. "Vehicles" include elephants, horses, chariots, carts, and so on. "Bedding" refers to cots and similar furniture. || 6 ||

**Regarding wisdom:** "Creative intuition" <term>pratibha: the faculty of immediate insight or "flash" of understanding</term> is the ability to perceive things at the right moment. "Retentive memory" <term>medha: the ability to hold and recall information</term> is the intellect that retains. "Discrimination" is the knowledge that distinguishes between merits and flaws, or between what should and should not be done. "Past merit" is the virtue earned in a previous birth. "Peace of mind" includes mental satisfaction and an inclination toward performing good deeds. || 7 ||

# The Path of Radiance

->**The Sixth House**<-

Thieves, enemies, obstacles, mental anguish, and diseases, as well as injury to the body;
Death by water or weapons should indeed be considered from the **sixth house**. || 8 ||

->**The Seventh House**<-

Marriage, passion, sight, the union of wife and husband;
The bed, sexual intercourse with women, and lost property are also from the **seventh house**. || 9 ||

->**The Eighth House**<-

Total destruction, calamities, and infamy;
The cause and location of death, and servants;
Monasteries and similar dwellings, diseases, and obstacles
Should again be considered by the **eighth house**. || 10 ||

->**The Ninth House**<-

Fortune, righteousness, compassion, merit, penance, and grandsons;
Charity, worship, good character, and teachers are from the **ninth house**. || 11 ||

->**The Tenth House**<-

Temples, cities, assemblies, roads, shelters, servants, and all works;
Command and support—all this is indeed to be considered by the **tenth house**. || 12 ||

->**The Eleventh House**<-

The arrival of all desired things, the elder brother, and children already born;
The left ear and the gain of wealth—these are to be considered by the **eleventh house**. || 13 ||

***

**Regarding "Thieves" etc.** || Mental anguish <note>original: "adhi"</note> refers to the sorrow of the mind. The phrase "by water or weapons" <note>original: "varishastrena"</note> is the correct word-break. The word "or" <note>original: "va"</note> here is used in the sense of "and." The phrase "should be considered" <note>original: "chintaniyam"</note> follows a grammatical rule <note>original: "napumsakamanapumsakena..."</note> where a neuter singular form is used to represent a group of mixed genders. || 8 ||

**Regarding "Marriage" etc.** || For men, the union with a wife; for women, the union with a husband. "Union" <note>original: "samagama"</note> here does not only refer to the relationship between husband and wife, but also to association with other people. Some say it also refers to coming and going <note>travel</note>. "Lost property" refers to wealth taken by thieves and the like. || 9 ||

**Regarding "Total" etc.** || The cause and location of death. "Monasteries and similar" <note>original: "mathadikam"</note> refers to dwellings for students and others; it implies the buildings that house them. The phrase "should be considered" <note>original: "vichintaniyah"</note> is connected here with the nearby word "obstacles." For the other terms, the gender and number should be adjusted accordingly to fit the grammar. || 10 ||

**Regarding "Fortune" etc.** || "Children of children" <note>original: "sutatmajāḥ"</note> means grandsons. "Good character" <note>original: "saushilyam"</note> means having virtuous conduct. || 11 ||

**Regarding "Temples" etc.** || "Road-shelters" <note>original: "margalayah"</note> refers to places like water-stalls or rest-houses. "Command" <note>original: "ajña"</note> refers to the power of authority, and "support" <note>original: "alambanam"</note> refers to one's refuge or basis. || 12 ||

**Regarding "All" etc.** || "Born" <note>original: "jatah"</note> refers to those already in existence, not those yet to be born. The latter <note>future children</note> are to be considered from the fifth house alone. || 13 ||

# Chapter Fourteen

One should consider sin, expenditure, downfall, hell, the left eye, loss of position, and physical disability from the **twelfth house**. || 14 ||

**"The Form" (Murti)**: This verse demonstrates the specific matters to be considered regarding questions about eating <term>Bhukti-prashna: a branch of divination concerning meals and consumption</term>. "The Form" refers to the physical condition of the eater. "The Vessel" <note>original: "amatram"</note> refers to the plate or bowl used for the meal. "The Rest" refers to lying down after the meal. These matters should be considered specifically in the twenty-seventh chapter regarding questions on dining. || 18 ||

# Prashna Marga
<page-num>194</page-num>

> The physical form, the treasury, the archers <note>referring to the army or warriors</note>, the vehicles,
> the counsel, the enemy, the path, the lifespan, and the mind;
> the business, the gains, and the losses—in this manner,
> the houses from the Ascendant <term>Lagna; the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon</term> are to be considered for a sovereign ruler. || 19 ||

> These houses are said to be of two kinds: external and internal.
> The external ones are known as 'Tanu' <note>Body</note> and so forth, while the internal ones are 'Kalya' <note>Health/Well-being</note> and so forth. || 20 ||

> Whatever is to be considered from the Ascendant and other houses, when associated with their respective lords,
> all that should be known as 'internal'; otherwise, it is 'external'. || 21 ||

> The head, face, throat, shoulders, heart, belly, pelvis, and the private parts;
> the thighs, knees, shanks, and the feet—these are the houses in order starting from the Ascendant. || 22 ||

> The shortness or length of the limbs should be declared based on the zodiac signs occupying the Ascendant and other houses.
> This [method] is generally utilized for such descriptions. || 23 ||

---

**Regarding 'The physical form'** || The physical form refers to the King's body. The treasury is the storehouse of wealth. The archers are the warriors. Vehicles include elephants, horses, chariots, carts, and so on. Counsel refers to the deliberation of affairs. The path refers to roads and routes. Lifespan is the duration of the King's life. The mind refers to the King's mental state. Business refers to the collective activities regarding the governance of the kingdom. Gain is the arrival of wealth and resources. Loss <note>original: 'aprapti'</note> is the failure to receive taxes; because the prefix 'a-' denotes the opposite, it also implies expenditure. These should be specifically considered in the section on Royal Queries in the twenty-fourth chapter. || 19 ||

**Regarding 'External'** || The 'Tanu' and others refer to the sequence: Body, Wealth, Siblings, Relatives, Children, Enemies, Spouse, Death, Fortune, Profession, Gains, and Loss. The 'Kalya' and others refer to: Health, Assets, Valor, Home, Intelligence, Injury, Desire, Vulnerability, Teacher, Honor, Income, and Expenditure. <note>These are two different traditional lists of house names used in Sanskrit astrology.</note> || 20 ||

**Regarding 'Whatever'** || Internal refers to what is mentioned in the 'Kalya' list. External refers to what is mentioned in the 'Tanu' list. || 21 ||

**Regarding 'The head'** || By this, the assignment of body parts to the houses starting from the Ascendant is made. The Ascendant is the head. The second house is the face. In this way, the twelfth house represents the feet. || 22 ||

**Regarding 'The limbs'** || In whichever limb a 'long' zodiac sign is placed, that limb is long. Where a 'short' sign is placed, it is short. The shortness or length of the signs should be understood from the words of Varahamihira <note>A famous 6th-century Indian astronomer and polymath</note>: "In the first half, the measures are five and so on multiplied by four, and then the reverse." This arrangement of body parts in the houses mentioned in the previous verse is used only for this consideration of shortness and length, and not elsewhere.

# Chapter Fourteen

The rising sign <term>Lagna: the zodiac sign ascending on the eastern horizon at the time of inquiry</term> represents the inquirer himself. The second and subsequent houses represent his wealth and other related matters. The growth or loss of these houses is determined by the presence of auspicious or inauspicious planets. || 24 ||

On this point, the *Fifty Verses on Horary Astrology* <note>original: "Shatpanchashika," a classic 6th-century Sanskrit text on divination by Prithuyashas</note> states:

> Whichever house is aspected by or occupied by its own lord, or by benefic planets, that house will flourish. Conversely, if it is influenced by malefic planets, the loss of that house should be understood, whether in a query or at birth. || 25 ||

And from the *Seventy Verses in Arya Meter*:

> Whichever house is occupied or aspected by its lord, or by Jupiter, Mercury, and Venus, the well-being of that house should be predicted. || 26 ||

> In whichever house benefic planets are situated in the second, twelfth, or seventh positions from it, that house flourishes; the same applies to those situated in the tenth and fourth positions. || 27 ||

---

This is generally applicable. By the word "generally," it is suggested that this may apply elsewhere, and other methods of arrangement might occasionally be used here as well. || 23

**The rising sign...** The construction here implies that the inquirer is represented by the self <note>the first house</note>. Through connection with auspicious planets, there is growth for the inquirer’s wealth and other factors represented by those houses; through connection with inauspicious planets, there is loss. || 24 ||

**On this point...** The following verse is located in the *Fifty Verses on Horary Astrology*.

**Whichever...** The "lord" refers to the planetary ruler of the house. It is implied that the house is either aspected by or joined with benefic planets. Similarly, if a house is aspected or joined by malefic planets, it suffers. This should be considered without distinction in both natal horoscopy <note>original: "Jataka"</note> and in inquiry-based astrology <note>original: "Prashna"</note>. || 25 ||

**The Seventy Verses...** The following two verses are from that work.

**Whichever...** Similarly, if joined or aspected. "Of that house" refers to its well-being or growth. "Situated in the second, twelfth, or seventh..." The intent is that if there are benefics on both sides <note>forming a protective "hem" around the house</note>, it is considered an auspicious influence. "In that house" refers to the specific house being analyzed. The locative case is used here to express the intended grammatical relationship <note>original: "vivakshatah karakani," a linguistic principle where the speaker's intention determines the grammatical case</note>. Growth also occurs if benefics are in the tenth or fourth positions. It is established that if benefics are in the "centers" <term>Kendra: the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses, considered the pillars of a chart</term> relative to a house, that house is strengthened. By the principle of remaining logic <note>original: "parishesya-nyaya"</note>, it is as good as said that connection with malefic planets in the same manner results in loss. || 27 ||

It cites classical authorities like the Shatpanchashika to emphasize that these rules apply to both birth charts and immediate divinations.</summary>

Following the previous: *Courage* <term>sattvam: strength, valor, or fortitude</term> and bravery. *Mind* <term>cit: consciousness or intellect</term> is knowledge. *Vehicle* means a carriage or mount. Saturn is the significator <term>karaka: the planet that acts as the 'doer' or indicator of a specific life area</term> of death, disease, and so on. || 31 ||

**Regarding "The soul and others" ||** When the Sun is strong, the power of the soul and the father become stronger. Similarly, when Venus is strong, women, enjoyment, and vehicles are more powerful. *The opposite for Saturn*: when Saturn is strong, there is a weakening of death, disease, and the like <note>A strong Saturn protects against the very miseries it signifies</note>. Likewise, when the Sun and others are weak, the soul and other factors are weak. But when Saturn is weak, there is a strengthening of death, disease, and so on. || 32 ||

**Regarding "In the Sun's portion" ||** This refers to all the things mentioned in the Chapter on Livelihood <note>original: "Karmajivadhaya"</note> in the verse "In the Sun's portion, by grass, gold, wool, medicine, etc.," and in the Chapter on the Results of Planetary Periods <note>original: "Dashaphaladhaya"</note> in the verse "By the Sun: wealth, sacrifice, teeth, skin, gold, etc.," and in the subsequent verse "And the father." || 33 ||

**Regarding "Fortune" ||** In the verse "From the Ascendant, in the house of the son or wife, when reached by the Lord of the Auspicious," the intent is that just as there is a compound for "Auspicious ones and the Lord," there is also a possessive compound meaning "The Lord of the Ninth House <note>The 9th house is the house of Fortune/Luck</note>." The heart of the matter is that the word "Auspicious" <term>shubha</term> refers by power to the ninth house, but by indication, it also embraces other desired houses.

**Regarding "Givers of good" ||** The meaning is that one should contemplate this according to the saying, "The strong one performs what is desired." || 35 ||

**Regarding "A malefic in the fifth"**: By this authoritative statement, the meaning stated in the previous verse is confirmed through illustration. **Regarding "In the houses"**: Here, the phrase "in its own or an enemy's sign" means in its own <term>Navamsha</term><note>The ninth-part divisional chart.</note> or an enemy's <term>Navamsha</term>. By the terms "own sign" and "one's own," the <term>Navamsha</term> of a friend should also be included. Here, friendship and enmity are not natural, but temporary <note>Based on the planets' current positions relative to each other in the sky.</note>, because of the inclusion of neutral <term>Navamshas</term>. This verse is also an authoritative quote. || 38 ||

**Regarding "The Lord"**: Of whichever house. "Situated in favorable houses" means relative to the Ascendant. "Capable of being experienced" means it becomes an object of experience. What need is there to speak of the experience itself? If the result does not manifest, how could it be experienced? This is a logical necessity <note>original: "arthapatti"; a method of proof where a fact is assumed to explain an otherwise inexplicable circumstance.</note>. || 39 ||

<header>Chapter Fourteen</header>

# Chapter Fourteen

->If both the significator <term>Karaka: a planet that naturally represents a specific area of life, like Venus for marriage</term> and the lord of a house are weak and situated in the twelfth or eighth houses,<-
->that house will not manifest its results for the person;<-
->what story can there be of experiencing its fruits? || 39 ||<-

->If the significator and the lord are in their signs of exaltation or friendly signs,<-
->but are placed in the eighth or other unfavorable houses,<-
->that house may be pure in its potential, but people will not experience its benefits.<-
->If they are in their signs of debilitation but are strong <note>original: "balau" - referring to other types of strength like directional or temporal</note> and placed in favorable houses like the eleventh,<-
->even if that house is impaired, its fruits will still be experienced. || 40 ||<-

->If one between the lord and the significator is strong and in a favorable house,<-
->and the other is otherwise, then by mixing these conditions,<-
->one should determine the results according to the logic already stated. || 41 ||<-

->When the lord is well-placed from its own house, the house prospers; otherwise, it does not.<-
->Some say that the actual experience of these results should be judged from the Ascendant <term>Lagna: the rising sign at the time of birth</term>. || 42 ||<-

---

**Regarding "If in exaltation..." etc. ||** The meaning is that the strength of the lord and the significator causes the fullness of a house, while their weakness causes its deficiency. Furthermore, their placement in favorable houses is the cause for experiencing the results, while placement in unfavorable houses causes the lack of experience. || 40 ||

**Regarding "The lord and..." etc. ||** This should be inferred: there is neither a total absence of results nor total fullness; neither a total lack of experience nor a complete experience <note>This refers to the "mixed" results when one factor is strong and the other is weak</note>. || 41 ||

**Regarding "From the house..." etc. ||** "Otherwise" means when the lord of a house is poorly placed (in the 6th, 8th, or 12th positions) relative to that house. If the lord of a house is well-placed from the Ascendant, there is experience of that house's fruits. If the lord is poorly placed from the Ascendant, there is no experience. It should be understood that the word "Lord" here also implies the "Significator." This is because both the lord and the significator are equally responsible for granting the prosperity or ruin of a house, as well as the experience or non-experience of its fruits. This has been explained in the following three verses and is the method practiced by the most eminent and authoritative experts in horary astrology <term>Prashnika: an astrologer specializing in questions</term>; such is the instruction of the Teacher. || 42 ||

<summary>This page explains the distinction between a house's inherent strength and the individual's ability to experience its benefits, based on the placement of the house lord and its natural significator. It emphasizes that while exaltation creates potential, favorable placement relative to the Ascendant is required for that potential to manifest in a person's life.</summary>

## Here is a citation from another text.

> Whichever house <note>Bhava</note> is connected to the Ascendant <note>Lagna</note> or to the Lord of the Ascendant through aspects, conjunctions, placement in centers <note>Kendras</note>, or movement, the fruits of that specific house will be experienced by the seeker. || 43 ||

## The favorable and unfavorable houses for planets are now stated.

> For the gentle planets <note>Saumyas; benefics like Jupiter, Venus, Mercury, and the Moon</note>, the 12th, 8th, 6th, and 3rd houses are not desired; the others are favorable. For the cruel planets <note>Papas; malefics like Mars, Saturn, and the Sun</note>, the 6th, 3rd, and 11th houses are favorable; the others are not. Among these houses, the body <note>the 1st house/Ascendant</note> is primary, while the houses of fortune <note>9th</note> and progeny <note>5th</note> are equal to it. In these three, one should recognize the increased results of good or evil from the gentle and cruel planets respectively. || 44 ||

> Even if the "harsh" planets <note>malefics</note> grant gains of their respective items like copper or gold, they are considered unfavorable in inquiries regarding illness because they produce disease when located in the 6th house <note>the house of enemies and sickness</note>. || 45 ||

---

## Here is the commentary from the "Brief Birth Chart" <note>Swalpajataka</note>.

**Regarding "Here":** The following verse is located in another text.

**Regarding "Whichever":** By the word "etcetera" <note>original: "adi"</note>, connections such as trinal relationships are to be understood. A connection with the Ascendant occurs when the Lord of a house is situated in the Ascendant, in its centers, or aspects it. Otherwise, the connection of the houses to the Ascendant would be considered fixed and unchanging <note>which would make the reading static rather than dynamic</note>. || 43 ||

**Regarding "Of the planets":** This is explained in the following two verses.

**Regarding "For the gentle":** "Abhimati" refers to the enemy or the 6th house. Among these twelve houses, "Fortune and Progeny" refer to the 9th and 5th houses. In those three—the 1st, 5th, and 9th—the results of good or evil are felt; good results from the gentle planets and evil results from the cruel ones. If the 1st, 9th, and 5th houses are joined by benefics, there is nourishment even for other houses like wealth. If these three are pierced by malefics, there is generally a loss of prosperity. || 44 ||

**Regarding "Copper...":** This means that even though malefics are said to be "desired" in the 6th house <note>because they destroy enemies</note>, they are unfavorable in an inquiry regarding disease. However, in inquiries regarding business or general tasks, they remain auspicious. || 45 ||

**Regarding "Here":** In the context of contemplating the state of the houses <note>Bhavachintana</note>.

### Chapter Fourteen

->Benefic planets nourish the auspicious houses,<-

**Regarding "They nourish..."** || "Destroyers of enemies" means they do not nourish the enemy. "All" refers to both benefics and malefics. || 46 ||

**Regarding "Results of the periods..."** || Inauspicious results refer to those mentioned regarding wife, children, etc. Auspicious results refer to those mentioned as "wealth, nails, teeth, and skin" <note>original: "svam nakha-danta-carma"</note>. When a planet is in a favorable house like the eleventh (gain), auspicious results should be applied. When in an unfavorable house like the eighth, inauspicious results should be applied. || 47 ||

**Regarding "Favorable..."** || If the Sun is giving inauspicious results, there are things like the wrath of the king, the wrath of Shiva, loss of copper, and bone diseases. If giving auspicious results, there are honors from the king, the grace of Shiva, gain of copper, and strength of the bones. || 48 ||

"When" refers to the time of planetary transit. "Their own" refers to each specific house. "Occupied by" refers to those situated in the second, twelfth, or eighth from that house. "Calamity" should be applied to each division. "Certainly" means with certainty. <term>In the head and other parts</term> <note>Sanskrit: varāngādiṣu</note> implies the concept that the Ascendant (Lagna) represents the head, the second house the face, and so on. For example: when the fifth house is joined by its <term>own eighth-house lord</term> (the lord of the twelfth house) or by Saturn...

# Prashna Marga
## Page 272

->Even when there are no specific planetary combinations in the Ascendant and other houses, the results should be gathered together.<-
->For the ease of the questioner, the method for declaring the results is described hereafter. || 50 ||<-

> If a malefic <note>A planet with a harmful influence, such as Mars or Saturn</note> is situated in the Ascendant <term>Lagna: the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at the time of the query</term>, the results are defeat, diseases of the head, sorrow, ill-repute, loss of position, destruction of wealth, general physical ill-health, and a miserable existence. If a benefic <note>A planet with a favorable influence, such as Jupiter or Venus</note> is in the Ascendant, the questioner should be told the results are happiness, victory, health, acquisition of wealth, fame, and the attainment of special positions. || 51 ||

> If a malefic is in the second house <term>Vitta: the house of wealth and speech</term>, there is the destruction of wealth accumulated in the past, diseases of the mouth, illness among dependents, ailments of the right eye, harsh speech, and loss of worthy associates. If a benefic is in the second house, the questioner will experience the growth of previously earned wealth, the acquisition of worthy associates, and the happiness of pleasing those who depend on them. || 52 ||

If a person is undergoing a specific planetary period <term>Dasha: a period of time ruled by a specific planet</term>, and during that time there is an unfavorable sub-period <term>Apahara: a minor planetary cycle within a Dasha</term> of a malefic planet that rules the 8th house <note>The house of death and obstacles</note>, or if the sub-period belongs to the lord of the 10th, 4th, or 12th houses situated in those same houses, then the loss of a son and stomach diseases will certainly occur at that time. Similar logic should be applied to other houses. || 49 ||

**Regarding "Lagna and others" (Verse 50):** "Gathered together" means combining the various influences into one conclusion. The section starting from "If a malefic is in the Ascendant" up to "should be declared after careful thought" deals with the favorable and unfavorable combinations of the houses. || 50 ||

**Regarding "If a malefic" (Verses 51-53):** By saying "this should be known," it is implied that the results mentioned are examples, and other similar results can also be predicted. "Previously earned" refers to wealth acquired by one's ancestors or oneself in the past. "Dependents" refers to the family. "Eye" refers specifically to the right eye. "Harsh speech" refers to defects in speaking. By the word "etcetera," one should also include special happiness or health regarding the chest, shoulders, and the right ear. || 51-53 ||

# Chapter Fourteen

-> If a malefic <note>A "malefic" or "cruel" planet, such as Mars or Saturn, which typically brings challenges.</note> is placed in the house of siblings <note>The third house, which governs brothers, sisters, and courage.</note>, there is a loss of support, <-
-> illness among siblings and the like, <-
-> ailments of the chest, neck, and right ear, <-
-> as well as mental distress and a loss of courage. <-
-> If a benefic <note>A "benefic" or "gentle" planet, such as Jupiter or Venus, which typically brings auspicious results.</note> is placed in the house of siblings, there is support from brothers, <-
-> gains in health and more, <-
-> the dawning of right intellect, and the possession of courage; <-
-> these are the results for those who inquire. || 53 || <-

-> If a malefic is placed in the house of happiness <note>The fourth house, governing the mother, home, and comforts.</note>, there is misfortune for the <-
-> mother, maternal uncle, sister's son, and friends; <-
-> for cattle, the home, beds, seats, <-
-> and fields, as well as for vehicles; there is also pain in the body. <-
-> There is contamination of water in wells and such. If a benefic is in the house of happiness, <-
-> one gains vehicles, <-
-> fields, cattle, beds, and seats; <-
-> indeed, there will be the gain of happiness from these. || 54 || <-

-> If a malefic goes to the fifth house <note>The house of children, intelligence, and past merit.</note>, then due to that fault, <-
-> there is illness or death of a child through dullness or similar causes; <-
-> the destruction of ancient merit, a barren wife, and a dullness of mind. <-
-> There is anger, illness of ministers, and so on. But if a benefic is there, <-
-> there is the gain of a son, or rather, <-
-> health, the dawning of intellect and genius, <-
-> satisfaction of the mind, and the rise of merit. || 55 || <-

**Regarding the mother...** "Fields" refers to paddy fields and the like. By the word "and such" in "wells and such," ponds and other water bodies are included. || 54 ||
**Regarding the malefic...** "Of this" refers to the malefic situated in the fifth house. "Due to the fault of dullness and so on"—the sense is that if the fault is slight, there is illness; if the fault is great, there is death. "Dullness of mind" refers to a lack of enthusiasm or a bitter disposition. || 55 ||

# Chapter Fourteen

->If a malefic planet <note>a planet with a harmful influence, such as Mars or Saturn</note> enters the eighth house, there is illness for servants,<-
->obstacles to work, and diseases of the private parts;<-
->there is conflict with people, and the theft of wealth and property<-
->by thieves, kings, or by water.<-
->There are illnesses beginning with a loss of appetite, and even<-
->death is to be feared.<-
->But if a benefic planet <note>a planet with a helpful influence, such as Jupiter or Venus</note> enters the eighth house, there is freedom from disease<-
->and a long duration of life. || 59 ||<-

->If a malefic is situated in the eighth, there is also slander and the loss of a monastery <note>original: matha; can also refer to a school or religious estate</note>.<-
->A benefic located here may even bring about the acquisition of monasteries and temples. || 60 ||<-

->If a malefic is situated in the ninth house <note>the house of fortune and dharma</note>, there is illness for elders, fathers, and grandsons,<-
->and a loss of fortune;<-
->one should know there is a loss of the favor of the Lord of Dharma, of merit, and of penance, as well as a lack of compassion.<-
->If a benefic is situated in the ninth house, there is the favor<-
->of the minds of elders and fathers, and of the Lords;<-
->there is an increase in fortune and righteousness, and of auspicious penances,<-
->as well as a tenderness of heart and happiness regarding grandsons. || 61 ||<-

---

Regarding the verse "If a malefic enters the eighth": <term>Obstacle</term> <note>original: pratyūha</note> means a hindrance to one's work. <term>Conflict</term> <note>original: vigrahaṇa</note> means a quarrel. The theft of wealth etc. is caused by the three agents mentioned: thieves and so on. <term>Freedom from disease</term> means the attainment of health. <term>Located here</term> <note>original: atragah</note> means situated in the eighth house. || 59, 60 ||

Regarding the verse "If a malefic is situated in the ninth": <term>One should know</term> <note>original: vedyam</note> is used here as a neuter singular collective. <term>The minds of elders and fathers</term> is a compound word expressing a collection. It should be interpreted as an "increase in auspicious penances." <term>Tenderness</term> refers to the mind; it means a disposition of compassion. <term>Happiness regarding grandsons</term> refers to the happiness of the grandsons themselves and one's own happiness caused by them. || 61 ||

->If a malefic <note>a naturally "harsh" planet like Mars or Saturn</note> is placed in the tenth house, there is failure in action,<-

->destruction of servants and support,<-
->pain in the knees, and wandering abroad.<-

**Regarding "If a malefic is in the tenth":** "Failure" means obstacles. To connect the singular verb "would be" with the various subjects, one should supply the phrase "all of this." Alternatively, one can treat them as separate sentences: "There would be ill-repute; there would be failure in action." "Wandering" refers to living away from one's own country. Regarding "paths and sheds": through a compound construction, this refers to both the road and the rest-house <note>original: "paddhati-mandapa"</note>. "House of the Immortals" means a temple. || 62 ||

**Regarding "If a malefic is in the eleventh":** "Of that" refers to the malefic planet situated in the eleventh house <term>Labha-bhava: the house of gains</term>. Regarding the phrase "gain of copper and such," some suggest a reading of "loss of copper." However, since the eleventh house—like the third and sixth—is considered a favorable house even for malefics, the reading "gain" is more appropriate and follows tradition. The phrase "Chapter on Definitions and others" includes the "Chapter on Livelihood" and the "Chapter on the Results of Planetary Periods." This refers to the gain of copper and such mentioned in the Definitions; the arrival of kingdoms and such; the grass, gold, and agriculture mentioned in Livelihood; and the nails, teeth, sugarcane, and milk mentioned in the Results of Periods. The word "others" also includes the substances of the three worlds, such as minerals. || 63 ||

->If a malefic <note>a planet with a harmful influence, such as Mars or Saturn</note> is in the twelfth house, there will be wicked expenses,<-

**Regarding "If a malefic is in the twelfth..." :** "Loss of position" means being removed from one's place. "A fall" refers to an accidental slip or mistake. "Distribution" means giving in charity. || 64 ||

**Regarding "The good and bad..." :** "General results" refers to the uniform effects of malefics like the Sun and Mars, and benefics like the Moon and Mercury. "In the *Hora*" refers to the *Brihat Jataka*. "In this context" refers to the subject of the results of the houses. The "specific results" are those spoken of in the verses beginning with "The Brave..." <note>referring to Brihat Jataka 18.1</note>. These should be "carefully considered" or well-deliberated as appropriate. In the discussion of the houses, these should be spoken. Regarding the phrase "In the *Hora* here," some read it as "In the *Hora* also." In the current reading, the word "again" essentially indicates a collection of these points. || 65 ||

**Regarding "In the *Hora*..." :** "In the *Hora*" refers to the work composed by Varahamihira. || 66 ||

**Regarding "Sickly..." :** "With a sibling" <note>referring to the third house results</note>. Because of the grammatical option "enemies or a foe," it takes the second case ending. "Fear of enemies" is a compound in the fifth case <note>a technical Sanskrit grammatical explanation of how the words for "fear" and "enemy" are joined</note>. || 67 ||

->destroys the spouse, and is excessively lustful. || 68 ||<-
->In the eighth house, one is intelligent but plagued by many diseases, short-lived,<-
->and meets death through poison, fire, or weapons.<-
->In the ninth house, one is devoid of virtue, penance, and sacred chants.<-
->In the tenth, one gains great fame and is devoted to the service of others. || 69 ||<-
->In the eleventh, one is manly, possesses wealth, vehicles, and assets,<-
->is powerful, and has many servants.<-
->In the twelfth, one has bad dreams, deformed nails, and is physically impaired.<-
->Thus are the results of Mandhi <note>also known as Gulika, a "shadow planet" considered the son of Saturn</note> in the houses starting from the Ascendant. || 70 ||<-
->The placement in the Ascendant and other houses<-
->causes the increase or decrease of the body and other factors, whether auspicious or inauspicious.<-

---

**Regarding "Elders and others":** "One with colic" means suffering from the disease of sharp abdominal pain. "Hating one's own" means either hating their own relatives or being hated by them. "Poisonous gaze" refers to one whose very look causes everything to perish in an instant. || 68 ||

**Regarding "Intelligent":** "Short-lived" means having a brief lifespan. "Devoid of virtue, penance, and chants" means lacking these qualities; "chants" <note>original: "manu"</note> refers here to the repetition of sacred mantras. "In the sky-standing" refers to the tenth house. || 69 ||

**Regarding "One should do":** By the word "thus," it is understood that these four verses—beginning with "The diseased, the wounded," etc.—have been extracted from another text and joined here. The intention is to show there is no room for suspicion of the fault of plagiarizing another's work. This principle should be understood to apply in other similar instances as well. || 70 ||

**Regarding "Placed in the Ascendant":** This refers to the increase or decrease of the "body" and other factors mentioned in the sequence of "Body, Family, Siblings," etc. <term>Upachaya</term> <note>increase or improvement</note> is caused by auspicious planets, and <term>Hani</term> <note>decrease or loss</note> is caused by inauspicious ones, respectively. The opposite is also true: for example, an auspicious planet in the sixth house causes a "decrease in disease," while an inauspicious one causes an "increase in disease." This is the opinion of Satyacharya <note>an ancient, highly respected authority in Vedic astrology</note>. || 71 ||

# Chapter Fourteen

->In the sixth house, there is fear of enemies and physical impairment;<-

...from water there is fear. Or, if the reading is "fear and mantras," it means the person is timid and a practitioner of spells. In the eighth house, the interpretation is that one wanders manifesting dullness, bound by excessive desires. "Meager clothing" means one suffers from a poverty of garments. || 77 ||

**In the eleventh house...** In the twelfth, the interpretation is exile due to the anger of the lord of the land (the king). The section starting with "Now" (Atha) gives the results of Ketu. "Bald-headed" (Vikesha) means one is losing hair. When Ketu is in the second house, there is weakness and nasal speech. Some say "weakness" connects to the previous house (the first), while others say "nasal speech" connects to the following. We, however, believe the term "nasal speech" applies to both by the "rule of the middle gem" <note>a Sanskrit grammatical rule where a word in the middle of a sentence illuminates both what precedes and follows it</note>. This is because the second house is the place of speech, and the word "both" is used later. It is appropriate that "weakness" connects to the first house, as that represents the body. Alternatively, the word "Giri" <note>referring to the number two or the second house</note> can have a dual meaning through technical application. Thus, when Ketu is in the second house, there is weakness of speech. "Fragrant" (Surabhi) means always possessing a good scent due to musk and such. In the heart (the fifth house), one is "Shuli," meaning one has "shula" <term>Shula: a sharp, piercing colic or lancinating pain</term>. If the subject is a woman, she is a "bearer of twins." Here, some explain "Shuli in the heart" as having heart disease, and they intend this result for Ketu in the fourth house. In their view, the description of Ketu's result in the fifth house would be like a "flower in the sky" <note>an Indian idiom for something that does not exist</note>; they simply do not remember the sequence. Since the following verse shows the results for the sixth house onwards, one must assume "in the heart" carries a double meaning for Ketu...

# Prashna Marga
## Page 212

->A person dies blind if the planet is in the twelfth house; by suffocation if in the eighth;<-
->by robbery or intoxication if in the seventh;<-
->by eating poison if in the sixth; by a violent or unnatural death<-
->if in the ninth house.<-
->One may die by being struck by a tree or by falling from a tree<-
->or from the sky <note>likely meaning a high place or lightning</note> if in the tenth.<-
->In the eleventh house, there is a loss of wealth and fortune, and<-
->suffering due to a lack of comfort in sleep. Thus it is said. // 79 //<-

->Regarding the gain or loss of all the houses mentioned here,<-
->when exactly that might happen—the timing is now explained. // 80 //<-

->The timing, such as the half-year period <term>Ayana: the six-month movement of the sun north or south</term>, is determined by the planet<-
->by which the attainment of the result is predicted. Multiply that period by the number of the specific division <term>Navamsha: a 1/9th sub-division of a zodiac sign</term> occupied by the planet to declare the time of fulfillment. // 81 //<-

->Depending on how many degrees have risen in the Ascendant, multiply the period<-
->associated with the lord of that division to predict the time for victory over enemies and other such matters. // 82 //<-

If a planet is situated in the heart <note>referring to specific astrological placements affecting the chest</note>, a man will suffer from sharp pains in the heart or heart disease. If the commentators had fulfilled their desire to prove the specific nature of heart disease here, it would have been appropriate; but let us not dwell on this further. // 78 //

**Regarding "A person dies blind" etc.** !! The word "dies" is applied to the phrases "by robbery" and "by eating poison." The word *Shevadhi* means a treasure or fund. // 79 //

**Regarding "Gain" etc.** !! This is explained in the following eight verses beginning with "The attainment of results." // 80 //

**Regarding "The attainment of results" etc.** !! This is determined by the planet that indicates the gain or desired outcome. The "half-year period and so on" refers to the time measures mentioned in the *Hora* <note>a foundational text of Vedic astrology</note> such as half-years and moments. "Multiply by the number of the division occupied": if the planet giving the result is in the first ninth-part <term>Navamsha</term> of the sign it occupies, the time is simply that planet's assigned period. If it is in the second ninth-part, the time is double that period, and so on. In the fulfillment of the result !! The instruction here is that one should use the rule of three <note>mathematical proportion</note> based on the degrees already passed and those yet to be covered in the current ninth-part to find the exact portion of the period. // 81 //

**Regarding "In the Ascendant" etc.** !! The meaning is this: If the first ninth-part is rising in the Ascendant, the time is the period of the lord of that rising division. If the second part is rising, the time is twice the period of the lord of that second division. And so on for the rest.

->In whatever number sign from the Ascendant a malefic planet is placed, in that same number of years, months,<-

**Regarding "From the Ascendant"** (Verse 83): In whatever number—meaning the numerical count. In the sign. A malefic—such as Saturn, <note>original: "manda-māndyādikaḥ"</note> Mandi, and others. In that same number—the numerical count. In the time period such as a half-year <note>original: "ayanādi-kāle"</note> mentioned by the Lord of the Ascendant. Distress—meaning inauspiciousness such as disease. By that malefic planet, whatever inauspiciousness is to be predicted, that is the meaning. In the same way, auspicious results should also be stated by means of a benefic planet. || 83 ||

**Regarding "By another way"** (Verse 84): That is the timing described by a different method. || 84 ||

**Regarding "From the House"** (Verse 85): The six houses starting from the Ascendant are the invisible half <note>the "invisible hemisphere" refers to the portion of the sky below the horizon at the time of birth</note>. The six starting from the seventh are the visible half. If, when examining wealth, the Lord of Wealth is in the visible half—meaning in the six houses starting from the eighth—then the gain of wealth is immediate. If it is in the six houses starting from the second <note>the "invisible" side relative to the house of wealth</note>, it is delayed. Thus, "Furthermore from the House"—its Lord, the ruler of that house. In whatever number sign the Lord of Wealth is situated from the House of Wealth, in that same number of months or days. "When the Moon reaches the sign occupied by the Lord of the House"—when the Moon, by its transit, enters the sign where the Lord of Wealth is placed, there is gain of wealth. This is the method. || 85 ||

**Regarding "The Ascendant"**: The Ascendant <note>original: "lagnam-ārūḍham"</note> or the <term>House of the Result-Giver</term> <note>The specific planet designated to deliver a particular outcome based on its favorable position</note>—the sign owned by whichever planet is the giver of results due to its placement in a favorable house. The exaltation sign of that result-giver. The result-giver—the planet itself. That result, by that planet...

# Prashna Marga
<note>The Path of Inquiry: a 17th-century classical treatise on Horary Astrology</note>

->Whether in the past or in the future, whenever<-
->the Ascendant is joined by malefic planets,<-
->at that time, one should predict inauspicious results; likewise, with<-
->benefic associations, good results occur for the querents. || 86 ||<-

->There are specific times for the fruition of results for all<-
->the wanderers of the sky <note>planets</note>;<-
->there are also certain others, which are being written down now. || 87 ||<-

->The time is defined by one's own asterism, day, and season; when<-
->the Sun, Moon, Jupiter, and others are in their own houses;<-
->for all, during their own major and minor planetary periods,<-
->and also at the time of their rising.<-
->For the Sun and Moon, the northern and southern<-
->solstices are also considered here.<-
->The resulting fruits of merit or fault should be<-
->deduced by the wise through all these factors. || 88 ||<-

---

The result should be stated. "Association with malefics" refers to the past or future conjunction of malefic planets with the *Arudha* <note>the sign corresponding to the questioner's position</note> through their transits. "At that time, inauspicious"—this is the phrase. Inauspiciousness refers to loss of wealth, disease, and so on. When there is a "benefic association," whether in the past or future, through the transit of a benefic planet over the *Arudha*, one should predict auspicious results such as health and prosperity. || 86 ||

**Regarding the fruition...** || They are being written—meaning, by the verse that follows. || 87 ||

**Regarding the time...** || For all planets, "Time" includes their own *Riksha* or birth star <term>Nakshatra: the 27 lunar mansions</term>. For the Sun, these are Krittika, Uttara Phalguni, and Uttara Ashadha. For the Moon, they are Rohini, Hasta, and Shravana, and so forth. "Day" refers to the day of the week. "Season" refers to the cycle starting with *Shishira* <note>late winter</note> as assigned to Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, etc. For the Sun, it is *Grishma* <note>summer</note>, as it is said: "Summer belongs to the Sun." "Staying in their own houses" refers to the time when the Sun, Moon, and Jupiter stay in the zodiac signs they rule during their transits. "Rising" refers to ascending the peak of the eastern mountain <note>becoming visible</note>. "Setting" refers to falling into the ocean from the western mountain. All these are common to all planets. For the Sun, the Northern Progress <term>Uttarayana: the period after the winter solstice</term> is significant; for the Moon, the Southern Progress <term>Dakshinayana: the period after the summer solstice</term>. This is their specific distinction. This applies equally to the giving of good results and bad results. || 88 ||

# Chapter Fourteen

What was previously stated in brief regarding the favorable and unfavorable results of the planetary periods <note>Dasha-phala: the predicted outcomes during a planet's specific time of influence</note> will now be explained here in detail. || 89 ||

When the Sun <note>original: "Martanda," a name for the Sun meaning "born from a dead egg"</note> is unfavorably placed, there is suffering from the anger of the King, the god Shiva, or the father; diseases of the heart, chest, and eyes; bone discharge, bile ailments, and fear of fire or animals; and loss of copper and personal distress.

There is acquisition of wealth through blankets, travel, grass, gold, and medicines, as well as a spirit of industriousness. || 90 ||

When the Moon is unfavorably placed, there is anger from the King and the mother, as well as illness. There are diseases of phlegm, wind <note>referring to the humors of Ayurveda: Kapha and Vata</note>, and blood; enmity with powerful relatives and anger; and the loss of agricultural wealth and fame.
When the Moon is favorably placed, there is joy from the Queen, the Goddess Durga, and the mother. Wealth is gained through subtle prayers <term>Anu: the repetition of mantras</term>, sesame, molasses, clothing, ghee, Brahmins, women, cattle, boats, and gems; there is also an increase in agricultural wealth and fame. || 91 ||

---

"Virtuous disposition" <gloss>Sattvik-tva</gloss> means the absence of excessive joy or grief in the face of pleasure or pain. "Industriousness" <gloss>Udyama</gloss> means a nature characterized by enthusiasm. || 90 ||

**Regarding the verse beginning with "Kopa":** The word "also" in "illness also" connects it to "anger." There is anger from and illness to the mother. There is enmity with those of one's own kin who are more powerful <gloss>Viryavat-svaih</gloss> than oneself. "Relating to Durga" <gloss>Daurgah</gloss> means pertaining to the Goddess Durga. "Progenitress" <gloss>Prasu</gloss> means mother. "Subtle" <gloss>Anu</gloss> refers to the chanting of mantras. "Covering" <gloss>Acchadanam</gloss> means clothing. || 91 ||

# Prashna Marga
## Page 216

When **Mars** <note>original: "Bhauma"</note> is situated in an unfavorable position, there is hatred with siblings and others, the loss of land and gold, and fear from fire, thieves, and enemies. There is the wrath of the Commander of the Gods <note>Skanda/Kartikeya</note> and of the army, as well as diseases of the blood, fever, and eye ailments. One may suffer the breaking of vessels or injury to limbs by weapons. Conversely, if Mars is in a favorable position, there is the acquisition of land, gold, and weaponry. The Commander of the Gods is pleased, and wealth is gained through the destruction of enemies, from siblings, and from the king. || 92 ||

When **Mercury** <note>original: "Jña"</note> is in an unfavorable position, there is anger from Vishnu <note>original: "Hari"</note>, young men, and kings; harsh speech; and distress from thieves. But when he is in a favorable position, there is the gain of horses, gold, land, friends, and wealth from Brahmins <note>original: "Avani-deva"</note> and teachers. Wealth comes through diplomacy <note>original: "Dautya"</note> and craftsmanship; one receives praise from the learned and an increase in intellectual capacity. There is success in religious acts, wealth from writing and mathematics, and the grace of the Son of the Cowherd <note>Lord Krishna</note>. || 93 ||

When **Jupiter** <note>original: "Jiva"</note> is in an unfavorable position, there are ear ailments and troubles for one's children, the wrath of Brahmins and the gods, and enmity with those devoid of righteousness. But if he is in the other <insert>favorable</insert> position, there is an increase in the qualities of the intellect...

---

**Regarding "Hatred" etc.:** "Siblings and others"—the word "others" includes sons, friends, and so on. "Commander" refers to Skanda <note>the deity of war</note> and the leader of the army. There is the "wrath of blood" <note>blood disorders</note> and of those two. "Breaking of vessels" means the destruction of pots or utensils. "Injury to limbs by weapons" means the production of a wound on the body by a blade. "In the other" means situated in a favorable position. "Pleasure of the Commander" refers to the satisfaction of the war deity. || 92 ||

**Regarding "Mercury" etc.:** "There" refers to Mercury. The phrase "Horses etc." should be read as a compound. "Of the learned" is in the subjective genitive case. "Intellectual capacity" refers to the power of critical reflection. "Son of the Cowherd" is Shri Krishna. || 93 ||

# The Path of Inquiry

->The results for Saturn apply to Rahu, as do those of the sign it occupies,<-
->and those specifically attributed to Rahu itself. For Ketu, the results<-

->Death, incurable disease, the loss of one's<-

**Regarding "The results for Saturn..." :** The specific results attributed to Rahu, such as "Rahu causes bodily heat and leprosy," <note>original: "svarbhānustanutāpakuṣṭha..."</note> and the results for the priestly or warrior classes <unclear>...</unclear> should be applied. || 97 ||

**Regarding "If only defects..." :** The construction here is: "If in the inquiry only defects are present." In the case of a mixture of merits and defects, the idea is that if merits are greater, there is prosperity; if defects are greater, there is misfortune. "Or perhaps the result of the defects alone" is an alternative view. The phrase "lacking in good fortune" serves as the reasoning for this. "People" refers to the general public. These three verses starting from here explain the method of declaring results. || 98 ||

**Regarding "Death..." :** "Departure" <note>original: niryāṇam</note> means death. "Difficult illness" refers to a chronic or manageable but incurable disease. <term>Burning of the house</term> <note>original: gṛhaploṣaṇam</note> means a fire in the home. "Theft of wealth" means the taking of money by thieves. These are determined by looking at the planets and the houses that provide "defects" (negative influences). For example, if the Sun is the provider of the defect, there is "anger of the king" (trouble with authorities). If the fourth house is associated with a fire-producing planet, there is "burning of the house." This is the intended meaning. || 99 ||
