# Prashnamarga
<page-num>220</page-num>

->Whether due to the anger of a deity, the curse of a scholar <note>original: "shrutivibudha," referring to a learned Brahmin</note>, the black magic of enemies, or the public outcry of the people, this suffering may be either "unyielding" <note>fixed/driddha</note> or "yielding" <note>removable/adriddha</note>. This is how the two types should be understood. || 102 ||<-

->This suffering arises from the mind, speech, or actions. If the planet causing the affliction is situated in the divisional charts of the Moon <note>the Hora, etc.</note>, it yields a "fixed" result. If the planet is in the transit path of the Sun, the result is "removable." The ripening of merit <note>punya</note> or its opposite <note>sin/karma</note> is known through these paths. In the triad of the mind, speech, and action, whichever house is occupied by a weak or malefic planet, the experience of the defect arises from that source. || 103 ||<-

->When malefic planets occupy the houses of mind, speech, and action, then through those three—<-

The increase of bad deeds <term>Dushkrita: the accumulation of negative karma from past actions</term> should be declared. In that regard, there are four causes respectively: the anger of a deity, the curse of a Brahmin, the black magic of enemies, and public outcry. In the phrase "of enemies," the grammatical case implies an action directed toward them. The sense is that the bad deed has increased through black magic performed by oneself against enemies. In the practice of black magic, causes of sin such as violence are to be expected. Alternatively, it implies the black magic performed by enemies against the person asking the question <note>the querent</note>. If one asks how another's action can cause one's own sin, it is resolved by the same logic as the anger of a deity. Just as a bad deed is the root cause for a deity's anger or a Brahmin's curse, the same applies here. A harsh act committed by the querent serves as the cause for enemies to perform black magic or for the public to cry out in protest. That is the nature of the bad deed. || 102 ||

**Regarding "Mind, Speech...":** Among the divisional charts <note>vargas</note>, the Hora <note>a 15-degree division</note> is the most important in this context. If the planets causing the bad deed are strong in the Moon's divisions, the result is "fixed" <note>difficult to remedy</note>. If they are in the Sun's divisions, the result is "removable." The phrase "in the transit path" applies to the following: for auspicious planets, the transits are the nine houses excluding the 12th, 6th, and 7th; for inauspicious planets, they are the six houses excluding the centers <term>Kendras: 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses</term> and trines <term>Trikonas: 1st, 5th, and 9th houses</term>. "Otherwise" means when they are in unfavorable transits. Regarding "of the other," it refers to other sins. Regarding "in the mind, etc.": if a malefic is in the 5th house, the defect is of the mind; in the 2nd house, it is a defect of speech; in the 10th house, it is a defect of action. "Ripening" refers to the experience of the results. || 103 ||

**Regarding "In the Mind...":** Through those three—mind, speech, and action—if there is a connection with a benefic, it is a general action; if there is a connection with a malefic, it is an affliction. If a malefic is only in the mind (the 5th house), then a lack of faith in performing duties is the cause of the bad deed. That defect...

This provides the detail for the "nature of the sign" mentioned in the previous verse. || 110 ||

# Prashna Marga <note>The Path of Inquiry: a classic 17th-century Sanskrit treatise on Vedic astrology</note>

Whatever has been stated regarding auspicious or inauspicious signs, or whether a house is dilapidated or renovated, all of that should be applied logically to every aspect of life. || 121 ||
| Thus ends the fourteenth chapter in the Prashna Marga. ||

---

## Now begins the Fifteenth Chapter

Now, the favor of the gods and other related matters are described.

->Whether the suffering is caused by the Gods, the Dharma-deities <note>deities protecting righteousness</note>, the Serpents, the Ancestors, the Gurus,<-
->the Brahmins, or the spirits of the deceased;<-
->whether that suffering manifests through the body or through speech;<-
->whether it arises from poison or is caused by enemies;<-
->the causes of these afflictions and their respective remedies<-
->are now being declared for the benefit of the inquirers. || 1 ||<-

---

One should obtain <note>results based on planetary positions</note>. If Saturn is in the seventh house, one gets a wife older than oneself or a mature woman. If the Moon is in the descendant <note>the seventh house</note>, the wife will always appear youthful. If Mars is in the seventh house, the wife may fall into fire <note>metaphor for accidents or a fiery temperament</note>. If Venus is in the second house, one's speech is sweet. All such things should be applied appropriately. || 121 ||
|| Thus ends the fourteenth chapter in the Prashna Marga. ||

**Now...** Following the determination of the houses as previously intended in the sequence of the inquiry, this follows in its proper order.
**By the Gods...** The characteristics, causes, and remedies for the eleven types of afflictions—beginning with the anger of the Gods—are described in sequence. || 1 ||

->Having considered whether divine favor is helpful or hindering,<-
->and finding that there is opposition,<-
->one must perform the prescribed rites to gain that favor;<-
->therefore, that subject is now being explained. (2)<-

->The presence of the Supreme Lords is always found within Jupiter <note>original: "dhishana"; a name for Jupiter, the preceptor of the gods</note>;<-
->therefore, when Jupiter is favorable,<-
->nearly all the gods are favorable.<-
->But if he is in opposition, they are not favorable. (3)<-

->The Sun is said to be Shiva <note>original: "Shambhu"</note> among all the planets.<-
->If the Sun is in a dual sign <note>Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, or Pisces</note>,<-
->in the first decan <note>a 10-degree subdivision of a zodiac sign</note>, he is said to be Skanda <note>original: "Guha"; the warrior god</note>;<-
->in the middle decan, he is Ganesha <note>original: "Vighneshvara"; the remover of obstacles</note>.<-
->The Moon is Durga if strong; if weak, she is Kali;<-
->and if she is even weaker and placed in the house of Mars,<-
->she is Chamunda and other deities associated with the quality of darkness <note>original: "tamo-guna"; the quality of inertia or destruction</note>. (4)<-

->Mars is Skanda <note>original: "Kumara"</note> or Bhairava depending on the sign he occupies.<-
->If he is situated in an even sign, he represents<-
->Chamunda, Bhadrakali, and others. (5)<-

**Regarding divine favor:** To gain that favor, specifically divine favor. The "rite" <term>vidhi: a ritual performance or remedy</term> refers to the countermeasure for opposition. That favor is what is being described and defined. (2)

**Regarding the Supreme Lords:** Of all the Supreme Lords, meaning all the gods such as Shiva, Vishnu, and others. "Presence" refers to their agency or power. "Nearly" means for the most part. "In his opposition" means when Jupiter is in a state of hostility. They are not favorable, meaning they are in opposition. (3)

**Regarding the Sun:** Among all the planets, excluding the first and second decans of dual signs. Here, in a dual sign. That Moon... (4)

**Regarding Skanda:** By virtue of the sign occupied, in the pure <note>original: "sattvic"</note> odd signs, he is Subrahmanya. Only Leo and Sagittarius are considered pure. In the other odd signs—Aries, Gemini, Libra, and Aquarius—he is Bhairava and others. By the word "others," deities like Ghantakarna are included...

### If Mercury is in the final decan <note>A 10-degree division of a zodiac sign</note> of a fixed sign, the deity is Vishnu in the form of Rama or other incarnations. In other signs, it indicates the Child Krishna (the Cowherd).
### If Mercury is in the final decan, it is Vishnu; however, Jupiter is said to represent Maha-Vishnu, the Lord of All. The distinction between these forms should be understood through the planet's association with specific zodiac signs. || 6 ||

### Venus represents Annapurneshwari, Lakshmi, or a Yakshi. Saturn represents deities such as Shasta. Rahu is remembered as the host of Serpents. || 7 ||

### If the planets from the Sun onwards become the lords of the "Obstruction Houses" <term>Badhaka-sthana: specific houses in a chart that indicate karmic blockages</term> and are placed in unfavorable positions, they indicate suffering caused by the wrath of their respective deities. || 8 ||

---

...are taken as two. That Mars, even there, is predominantly *Sattva* <note>pure/harmonious</note> in the signs of Cancer and Pisces; predominantly *Rajas* <note>active/passionate</note> in Taurus and Virgo; and predominantly *Tamas* <note>dark/inert</note> in Scorpio and Capricorn. || 5 ||

**Regarding "Sri Rama..." :** In "other signs" refers to movable and dual signs. The "Cowherd" refers to the image of the Child Krishna. Here, in a fixed sign, it is Vishnu—meaning Vishnu in a general sense without specific distinction. This "Lord of All" reminds us of the principle: "The presence of the Lord of All is eternal in the position of Jupiter." The distinction is known by the planet's relation to the Sun's signs or its conjunction/aspect with the Sun, which points to Shiva. Connection with the Moon points to Durga, and so on. Connection with Mars points to Subrahmanya, and so forth. Here, the phrase "Jupiter is indeed Maha-Vishnu" forms one sentence. The word "indeed" denotes fame or established tradition. He shows the reason for this fame by saying "He is called the Lord of All." This refers back to the previous statement regarding the "Lord of All." || 6 ||

**Regarding "Annapurneshwari..." :** She is Annapurneshwari <note>The Goddess of Nourishment</note> when in her own sign. She is Lakshmi in other auspicious signs. She is a Yakshi <note>a nature spirit, sometimes malevolent</note> in inauspicious (malefic) signs. Alternatively, one should consider her Annapurneshwari in the signs of *Sattvic* planets, Lakshmi in the signs of *Rajasic* planets, and a Yakshi in the signs of *Tamasic* planets. This is because these three goddesses are famous for the predominance of those respective qualities. Furthermore, if Venus is placed in an odd sign or associated with masculine planets, tradition establishes it as a significator for Vighneshvara (Ganesha). This should be understood as a tradition passed down by elder astrologers. The term "Shasta and others" includes forms like Kirata-Murti <note>Shiva as a hunter</note>. Although the determination of serpent-afflictions will be discussed later, the "host of serpents" is mentioned here for consistency with the current topic. || 7 ||

**Regarding "Obstruction..." :** The "Obstruction Houses" (*Badhaka-sthanas*) will be explained in the section on visible afflictions. "Unfavorable positions" refers to the Obstruction house, the 6th, 8th, and 12th houses. These are unfavorable. For benefic planets, the 3rd house is also unfavorable. Here, being the lord of an Obstruction house while situated in an unfavorable position is cited as the cause of "Deity Affliction" (*Deva-pida*). Nevertheless, the placement in an unfavorable position is the primary factor. Therefore, the anger of a deity may be indicated by that placement alone, not solely by the lordship of an Obstruction house. Indeed, the lordship of an Obstruction house is a fixed attribute of the chart.

# Chapter Fifteen

->The cause of anger and the remedy for pacifying that anger.<-
->Now, the specific placements of the planets and the resulting states of the deities are described. || 9 ||<-

->If a malefic planet is situated in the twelfth house from the Sun or other planets,<-
->there will be a physical defect in the body of the deities associated with them,<-
->or perhaps the touch of a water-snake.<-
->In conjunction with Mandi or Rahu, or if joined with Saturn,<-
->there is decay or impurity.<-
->In conjunction with Mars, the destruction of protection is declared,<-
->arising from a rift in the minds of the protectors. || 10 ||<-

->When a planet joined with a malefic is situated in the Ascendant,<-
->a defect in the icon should certainly be declared here—<-

<note>The commentator explains that the number of deities and their specific states are determined by the number of Navamshas (nine-fold subdivisions of a sign) traversed by the planet indicating the anger.</note> But the lord of the sign is not the only factor. The number of deities is indicated by the number of Navamshas traversed by the planet through which the divine anger is foretold. The specific type of deity and their particular condition are determined by the lords of those Navamshas; this is the traditional method established by those skilled in logical inference and deliberation. || 8 ||

Regarding the "cause of anger": This is explained starting with the verse "Of the Sun and others..." and ending with "The signs are indeed movable, etc." || 9 ||

**Of the Sun and others**: This refers to the planets that cause divine anger. "Physical defect" means a state of impairment. "In conjunction" means occupying the same zodiacal sign as the planets causing the anger. The word "water-snake" <note>original: *dundubha*</note> is an umbrella term for various types of serpents, including hooded cobras. Regarding the "body," the word does not refer only to the idol <note>original: *arca*</note>. Rather, as it is said in the collective teachings: "The temple and the idol are the gross and subtle bodies of the Lord of the Universe," thus it also refers to the temple structure itself. "Decay" refers to either the site or the icon. "Impurity" is used here as a primary quality, meaning the state of being unclean. "Rift in the minds" refers to a lack of unanimity <note>likely referring to the temple priests or trustees</note>.

The general statement made—"If a malefic planet is situated in the twelfth house, there is a physical defect in the body of the deities"—is now shown through specific details such as "the touch of a water-snake," and so on. Some commentators, explaining the subsequent three phrases, argue: "The terms 'conjunction,' 'union,' and 'association' only refer to the placement in the twelfth house, not to occupying the same sign as those specific planets. The touch of a snake, decay, impurity, and loss of protection are simply internal variations of the 'physical defect'." However, in their view, the specific causes would not be explained when the anger-causing planets are in the same sign as Mandi, Rahu, etc. This would narrow the scope of the science. Therefore, the previously stated interpretation is superior. || 10 ||

**Situated in the Ascendant**: When the planet causing divine anger is in the Ascendant <note>the first house or rising sign</note>. "Defect in the icon": Such a defect is of two kinds, such as being chipped or cracked—

->If the icon is broken, it is caused by Mars;<-
->impurity is caused by other planets.<-
->Indeed, a new icon should be offered for the pleasure of the deity<-
->when a malefic planet occupies the house of the temple.<-
->If the temple is old, let it be renovated;<-
->otherwise, provide a different dwelling. || 11 ||<-

->If a planet is in the seventh house in the sign of Mars or the Sun, dance is prescribed;<-
->if in the sign of Venus or the Moon, a lamp is remembered.<-
->If in the sign of Venus or the Moon, milk-porridge,<-
->milk, or ghee should be offered.<-
->In Mercury’s sign, sandalwood; in Jupiter’s sign,<-
->garlands or flowers.<-
->In Saturn’s sign, ornaments and clothing<-
->should be given for the deity's pleasure. || 12 ||<-

There is not just one type of defect. There is another arising from the connection to impurity. The author distinguishes between them. With the phrase "If the icon," etc., the remedy for cracks or breaks is stated. It says, "Indeed, a new icon should be offered for the pleasure of the deity." Here is the specific rule: if a part of the icon is broken that corresponds to a limb where a human would die if it were severed, then a completely new icon must be manufactured and consecrated. However, if other limbs are broken, it is sufficient to perform a renewal process by stabilizing the part with plates made of gold, silver, or other metals. In the case of "impurity," the specific purification of the icon <term>Bimba-shuddhi: a ritual cleansing of the idol</term> as favored by the Tantric practitioners should be performed. "In the house" refers to the fourth house of the horoscope. The condition of being "joined with a malefic" also applies here. The phrase "let it be renovated" is in the active voice, while "should be given" is in the passive; this shift in syntax is noted. The possibility of the Ascendant and the fourth house being unfavorable locations arises if they happen to be the <term>Badhaka-sthana: a specific house in a chart that acts as an 'obstructing' or harmful place for a particular sign</term>, so there is no room for objection. || 11 ||

**Regarding "Dance" etc. —** "Dance" refers to the performance of dance. "Lamp" refers to the lighting of lamps. "Milk-porridge" refers to the offering of that food. One should infer similar meanings elsewhere as appropriate. Here, the word "remembered" is used in the masculine gender to agree with "lamp." In the case of "dance" and other terms, it should be connected by changing the gender, and for "flowers" and "ornaments," by changing both gender and number. Some commentators connect the phrase "in the sign of Mars or the Sun" with "situated in the seventh house" through grammatical coordination <term>Samanadhikaranya: the relationship of referring to the same object</term>. That is incorrect. Because the seventh house is not inherently unfavorable; it only becomes unfavorable if it is the "obstructing house" <note>original: "Badhaka-sthana"</note> as previously stated—

# Chapter Fifteen

->If the planet is in the eighth house <note>the house of longevity and obstacles</note> or the tenth house <note>the house of action/career</note>, then worship or the offering of oblations should be performed.<-
->If it is in the twelfth house <note>the house of loss, also called 'Rispha'</note>, then singing and instrumental music should be offered for the pleasure of the deity. || 13 ||<-

Here is a passage from another text:

->From the Ascendant onwards, the remedies are: giving an image of oneself, chanting prayers, worship,<-
->building a temple, satisfying others with food,<-
->rituals for healing, counter-measures, dance, offerings, and<-
->devotional service, in that order.<-
->When the planet is in the final house <note>the 12th</note>, an offering placed on the shoulder of an elephant<-
->and the offering of water should be done.<-
->If an affliction is mentioned but its lord is in the twelfth, there is no affliction;<-
->therefore, nothing is prescribed for the twelfth house in that case. || 14 ||<-

->When the Sun, or a planet situated in the Sun's sign <note>Leo</note>, is in an unfavorable position,<-
->the worship of the deity should be performed for those seeking relief from disease. || 15 ||<-

As will be stated later in the phrase "the remedy should be known from the chanting of these," and because of the capacity to prescribe remedies here as well, it is not proper to assume that a planet in the seventh house also causes divine wrath. Since the explanation is logically satisfied by connecting the effects to different locations, it is unnecessary to resort to complicated interpretations involving the <term>Navamsha</term> <note>the ninth divisional chart used for fine-tuning astrological strength</note> or other factors. || 12 ||

**Regarding "In the eighth house" etc. (Verse 13):** Even for the tenth house, it is only considered unfavorable if it functions as a <term>Badhaka-sthana</term> <note>a specific "obstructing" house that varies based on the zodiac sign of the Ascendant</note>. "Worship" refers to specific rites performed at sunrise, sunset, and other times. "Oblations" refers to the "Victory Offering" and similar rituals. || 13 ||

**Regarding "From the Ascendant onwards" etc. (Verse 14):** "Giving an image" means creating a likeness of oneself out of gold, silver, wood, or clay according to one's means and offering it before the deity. "Building a temple" refers to the construction of a house for the god. If the reading is "Garden," it means establishing a park dedicated to the deity. "Satisfying others" means pleasing the devotees of the god by providing food, oil for baths, and so on. "Counter-measure" refers to specific offerings or fire sacrifices intended for the deity. "Offering" includes the Victory Offering, the <term>Shri-bhuta-bali</term> <note>an offering to the elemental spirits</note>, or festival offerings. "Elephant" refers to the offering placed on an elephant's shoulder to please the deity. If the text says "affliction is mentioned but its lord is in the twelfth," it means there is no affliction. The meaning is as before: "its lord" refers to the Lord of the Affliction <note>the <term>Badhakesha</term></note>. Therefore, nothing is prescribed for the twelfth house because of the absence of affliction. "Nothing" refers to the gifts of images and so on. || 14 ||

**Regarding "The Sun" etc. (Verse 15):** "Worship of the deity" is done by offering handfuls of flowers and the like. The prescription of gruel <note>Yavagu</note> for specific castes...

-> When the Moon is in the Ascendant or in its own sign <note>Cancer</note>, one should offer barley gruel. <-
-> One should also perform a ritual bath for the Deity using a conch shell and a continuous stream of water. || 16 || <-

-> When Mars is in the Ascendant or its own sign <note>Aries or Scorpio</note>, one should offer lamps and perform fire sacrifices to the Deity. <-
-> When Mercury is in the Ascendant or its own sign <note>Gemini or Virgo</note>, one should arrange for a dance performance. <-
-> When Jupiter is in the Ascendant or its own sign <note>Sagittarius or Pisces</note>, one should provide two meals and offer gold and other valuables to the Deity. <-
-> When Venus is in the Ascendant or its own sign <note>Taurus or Libra</note>, one should distribute a large quantity of food to cure diseases. || 17 || <-

-> When Saturn is in the Ascendant or its own sign <note>Capricorn or Aquarius</note>, or when a planet is in an unfavorable position, <-
-> one should give food to the lowly <note>the marginalized or destitute</note> and donate land to pacify suffering. || 18 || <-

-> If the Sun and other planets are in the Ascendant along with benefics, one should declare the favor of the respective Deities. <-
-> However, if the Lord of the 9th House <note>the house of fortune and piety</note> is in the House of Affliction <note>Badhaka-sthana</note>, it indicates that some deity was worshipped long ago, <-
-> but is now being neglected; therefore, there is divine wrath. One should advise the querent to worship at the feet of that Deity for their well-being. || 19 || <-

---

The offering of barley gruel is made without regard for <unclear>wealth/status</unclear>. "Ritual bath with a conch and stream" — the word "and so on" includes bathing the deity with milk and offering milk-porridge. "Fire sacrifice" refers to rituals such as the *Mrityunjaya* <note>Conqueror of Death</note> homa. "Arranging for dance" means organizing a performance by dancers in the presence of the Deity. "Gold and others" refers to ornaments made of gold. "Large quantity of food" means giving as much food as possible to all, regardless of caste. "To the lowly" refers to those such as the *Chandalas* <note>outcastes</note>. || 15--18 ||

**Regarding "If in the Ascendant"**: "Along with benefics" means accompanied by auspicious planets. "The respective Deities" refers to the deities associated with the Sun and others, such as Shiva. "That" refers to the Lord of the 9th House. Alternatively, because the text previously said "some deity," there is no specific requirement for a particular god. In that case, it refers to any deity whose worship has been neglected. According to the *Amarakosha* <note>a famous Sanskrit lexicon</note>, the word *Daivata* <note>Deity</note> can be masculine; thus the reading "this deity" is also correct. || 19 ||

->When a planet that is the lord of an unfavorable house, such as the <term>Badhaka</term><note>A "Badhaka" is a planet that acts as an obstructer or causes interference based on the zodiac sign of the ascendant.</note>, is placed in the eleventh or second house,<-
->the wrath of that specific deity occurs due to the misappropriation of the deity's property. || 20 ||<-

->The cause is declared to be "Mineral" when a movable sign<-
->or a "Mineral" planet is rising;<-
->it is "Vegetable" in a fixed sign or with a "Vegetable" planet; in a dual sign,<-
->it is "Animal" when an "Animal" planet is present.<-
->"Vegetable" refers to things arising from the earth like trees;<-
->"Minerals" are metals like gold;<-
->"Animals" include humans, four-legged creatures, and the like;<-
->and these correspond to the nature of the zodiac signs. || 21 ||<-

->When the cause is "Animal," it is due to not offering to the Lord<-
->the animals and such that were intended by oneself...<-

**When a planet... (Commentary on Verse 20):** By the word "and such" in the phrase "Badhaka and such," the sixth and eighth houses are included. The phrase "that specific" means relating to the planet that is causing the wrath. || 20 ||

**The cause... (Commentary on Verse 21):** When a movable sign—Aries, Cancer, and so on—is rising, or when a "Mineral" planet is rising (meaning it is situated in the <term>Ascendant</term><note>The zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at a specific moment.</note>), then the cause of the divine wrath or the resulting illness is "Mineral" (inanimate matter). The classification of planets into Mineral, Vegetable, and Animal will be explained later. In this section, in the <note>original: "Tamrak"</note> vernacular language, it is seen that: if a Mineral sign is in the first or second house; or if a Mineral planet is in the first or second house; or if the lord of the first or second house is a Mineral planet; or if the <term>Badhaka</term> planet is in a Mineral sign or associated with a Mineral planet, then a mineral substance is the cause of the disease. The same logic should be applied to "Vegetable" and "Animal" causes. It should be understood that other parts of this text have been gathered from different treatises. The second half of the verse distinguishes between "Vegetable" and others. By saying "correspond to the signs," it should be considered that Gemini and Virgo represent humans, Pisces represents fish, the latter half of Sagittarius represents animals, and so on. By the word "rising," prominence is indicated here. Nevertheless, the tradition is that the <term>Arudha Lagna</term><note>A calculated point in a horoscope used for specific predictions about status and perception.</note> is also examined. || 21 ||

**When the cause is Animal... (Commentary on Verse 22):** This refers to animals and such that were intended for the Lord for the sake of one's children and family, but were withheld. The word "and such" includes elephants, horses, and so on. By "misappropriation," it refers to the theft or withholding of these animals.

# Prasna Marga
## Chapter 15: On Divine Wrath

->The anger of the deity arises from the theft of property,<-
->or from the failure to offer items promised for the sake of one's life.<-
<note>Verse 22</note>

->In the case of Mineral causes, it is due to not giving promised gold,<-
->or the misappropriation of the deity's possessions.<-
->In the case of Vegetable causes, it is due to the theft of land or grain;<-
->such sins provoke the anger of the God.<-
<note>Verse 23</note>

->The Moon, Mars, Saturn, and Rahu; the Sun and Venus; and Mercury and Jupiter;<-
->along with the Moveable, Fixed, and Dual signs respectively,<-
->represent the Mineral, the Vegetable, and the Animal kingdoms.<-
<note>Verse 24</note>

->Regarding this, the Krishniyam states:<-

->The Moon, Mars, Rahu, and Saturn represent the Mineral;<-
->The Sun and Venus represent the Vegetable;<-
->Jupiter and Mercury represent the Animal.<-
->Beginning with Ashwini, the constellations follow the same order.<-
<note>Verse 25. The Krishniyam is an ancient authoritative text on horary astrology often cited in this work.</note>

---

**For the sake of one's life:** This refers to the preservation of one's own life or the lives of one's kin. **Promised items:** This refers to objects other than living beings that were pledged verbally. **Failure to offer:** This means not fulfilling the pledge through the actual act of giving. It should be understood that the phrase "for the sake of life" connects to the act of "offering." Even if the grammar seems complex, the meaning is resolved by recognizing the constant dependency of these terms in the context of a vow. <note>Verse 22 commentary</note>

**In the case of Mineral:** Regarding the non-giving of gold and such. **Not giving promised gold:** This refers to failing to hand over gold, silver, or other valuables that were mentally resolved or pledged to be given. **Misappropriation:** The word "and such" in the text implies the theft or misuse of items that belong to the deity. <note>Verse 23 commentary</note>

**The Moon, etc.:** By the grouping mentioned, the planets and the Moveable, Fixed, and Dual signs <term>Rashi: the twelve signs of the zodiac</term> correspond respectively to the Mineral, Vegetable, and Animal categories. This correlation is established through a figure of speech where the indicator and the indicated are treated as identical. This principle—as seen in phrases like "The Sun is declared to be Shiva"—should be applied appropriately throughout this science. <note>Verse 24 commentary</note>

**Regarding this:** Concerning the definition of the Mineral, Vegetable, and Animal categories.

**The Moon, etc.:** Regarding the constellations: Ashwini represents the Mineral <term>Dhatu: inanimate matter or minerals</term>; Bharani represents the Vegetable <term>Mula: roots or plant life</term>; Krittika represents the Animal <term>Jiva: living beings or souls</term>. This cycle continues in the same order for the remaining constellations. <note>Verse 25 commentary</note>

### This section concerns the determination of obstacles caused by the gods of Dharma. Now, the obstacles caused by serpents are described.

->If Jupiter is the Lord of Obstacles and is situated in the twelfth, eighth, or sixth house,<-

**"This" refers to:** These three verses. The description begins with "If Jupiter..." and continues until the instruction to perform a sanctification ceremony.

When Jupiter is the Lord of Obstacles and is located in the twelfth, eighth, or sixth houses, and simultaneously occupies a quadrant from Rahu or Mandi, this is the definition of serpent-affliction. Specifically, if he is in a quadrant from Rahu, it is an affliction from a "superior" serpent <note>divine or high-caste serpents like Ananta</note>. If he is in a quadrant from Mandi <note>a sensitive mathematical point in the chart associated with Saturn and toxicity</note>, it is an affliction from an "inferior" serpent. Regarding the term <term>Uragas</term> <note>literally "those who go on their chests" — serpents</note>, their high or low status is linked to the Moon and Sun respectively. Through association, aspect, or placement in quadrants or trines, the specific nature is determined. If associated with both, both types are considered. || 31 ||

**Regarding "When Rahu":** An offering <term>Serpent-Bali</term> <note>a ritual food offering to appease spirits or deities</note> should be performed for the pleasure of the serpents. The "Chitrakuta" ritual refers to the <term>consecration of a Chitrakuta stone</term> <note>a traditional stone platform or shrine used in Kerala for serpent worship</note>. "Sudha-payo-vitaranam" refers to the distribution of "Sudha," which is a <term>special edible offering</term> that brings delight to the serpents, along with milk.

...[this interpretation] is not proper. Because there is a break caused by the word "situated in the middle" following "situated in a movable sign." Furthermore, no connective word is seen. Moreover, the joining of these two when situated in a dual sign is not pleasing to the mind, due to the lack of proximity. The completion of the meaning of "the two" by taking the meaning of the sentence to be spoken hereafter is only appropriate in the work of a bad poet. However, the path shown [here] is seen to be unobstructed and appealing to the hearts of all. Therefore, enough of this boldness in distressing the intentions of great men. Regarding the phrase "Having fashioned," the word "to be given" <note>original: "deyani"</note> follows the grammatical rule of "the neuter remains when combined with non-neuter" <term>napumsaka-ekashesha: a Sanskrit grammatical rule where the neuter gender takes precedence in a compound</term>. For the lower snakes, [the offerings are] of copper. For the higher snakes, of gold. This is the application. || 34 ||

Regarding the verse beginning with "From Mandi": In the phrase "the lord and significator of that," the word "that" refers to the houses of siblings and so forth. A similar calculation should be applied to the divisional portions. || 46 ||

Regarding the verse "Moon and others": The age is "one, two, nine, twenty, eighteen, eighteen, and fifty years respectively for the Moon, Mars, Mercury, Venus, Jupiter, Sun, and Saturn," as per the established rule. He provides an alternative view for determining age via the Moon: "Some say..." etc. If the Moon is in its infant stage (New Moon), the spirit is of an infant age, and so on. || 47 ||

# Prashnamarga
<page-num>144</page-num>

->If there arises a desire to know the caste or class of the deceased spirit,<-
->one should indicate the caste based on the zodiac sign and the divisional sign occupied by Gulika. <note>original: "Mandhi" (Gulika), a sensitive mathematical point in Vedic astrology associated with Saturn and often linked to ancestral spirits.</note> || 48 ||<-

->Having understood that there is an affliction from a deceased spirit, a remedy must certainly be performed.<-
->If one is in distress, the following authoritative words should be applied for the spirit's satisfaction. || 49 ||<-

->The anger of a deceased spirit may cause the loss of children,<-
->diseases, and other calamities.<-
->To please them, one should perform the Parvana and other rites—<-
->the Shraddha ceremonies that satisfy the minds of the ancestral host.<-
->One should also offer the Kshetra-pinda, perform the burnt offering of sesame seeds,<-
->and provide a feast for the Brahmins.<-
->When these spirits are satisfied by these acts, they bestow all<-
->prosperity and the continuation of the lineage. || Thus || 50 ||<-

**Regarding the spirit:** The caste of the signs and divisional signs is to be understood by the rule: "Pisces is the Brahmin; Aries is the King (Kshatriya); Taurus is the Merchant (Vaishya); Gemini is the Servant (Shudra); and their respective trines follow the same pattern," as will be explained later. There is an alternative reading: "the caste of the lord of the sign." In that view, the <term>caste of the planets</term> <note>Graha-jati: the classification of planets into social/functional classes (e.g., Jupiter and Venus as Brahmins)</note> should be followed: "Venus and Jupiter are Brahmins; Mars and Saturn are Warriors; the Moon is a Merchant; and Mercury is a Servant." The word "sign" also implies the divisional sign (Amsha). Here, in the determination of spirit affliction, some also consider the trines and quadrants to be unfavorable positions for Gulika. The number of spirits is also determined by the degrees traversed by Gulika. Their caste and state are determined by the lords of those divisions. Their count is also made based on their positions in exaltation, divisional strength, and so on. All of this should be accepted according to what is appropriate for the situation. || 48 ||

**Regarding the affliction:** The phrasing "if one is in distress" connects here. "For their satisfaction" means for the satisfaction of the ancestors. "Authoritative words" refers to the verse that follows. || 49 ||

**Regarding the anger:** "To please them" means for the satisfaction of the deceased spirit. <term>Shraddha-karma</term> <note>Ritual offerings made to ancestors to facilitate their journey or well-being in the afterlife.</note> refers to the Parvana and other rites. By the word "and others," the Ashtaka, Pinda-pitru-yajna, and annual rites are included. The <term>Parvana</term> <note>A specific Shraddha rite performed on the new moon.</note> is to be performed on the New Moon day. So too is the <term>Pinda-pitru-yajna</term> <note>An ancient Vedic ritual of offering rice balls to the paternal ancestors.</note>. The <term>Ashtaka</term> rites are performed during the Ashtaka periods <note>Specific lunar days in the winter months.</note>. The <term>Abdika</term> <note>The annual death anniversary rite.</note> is to be performed every year on the lunar day of death, or when the news of death was heard. They are satisfied by these Parvana and other rites. || 50 ||

<header>Chapter Fifteen</header>

# Concerning the Determination of These Afflictions

Now, the afflictions arising from the "gaze" <note>Sanskrit: *dṛṣṭi*; refers here to the malevolent glance of spirits or planetary aspects</note> are described. I shall proclaim those men or women who, according to the Shastras <note>Sacred scriptures or systematic treatises</note>, are liable to be afflicted by the planets. || 51 ||

## Here follows the Compendium of Essence (Sarasangraha)

-> The greedy, the cruel, the fear-stricken, the over-excited, the extremely deceitful, <-
-> those bound by ancient enmities, <-
-> those who have lost wealth, the lonely, the defeated, the impure, <-
-> those whose "time has come," the diseased, <-
-> those blinded by laughter, those with beautiful bodies, those who squander treasures, <-
-> the cowardly, those with adorned limbs, <-
-> and the man who is alone at night— <-
-> the attendants of the Destroyer of Kama <note>An epithet for Lord Shiva; his attendants are the Ganas or spirits</note> seize him. || 52 ||

---

**"These..."** || This refers to what was stated starting from the section on the "pairs" of afflictions.

<margin>In the verses starting with "greedy," etc., the masculine gender is used as a collective term to include both men and women <note>original: "pumān striyā"; a grammatical rule where the masculine form represents both sexes</note>. || 51 ||</margin>

**"Now..."** || This means "now, after the determination of afflictions by ghosts (Pretas)." They are described according to the sequence of the intended topic.

**"Here..."** || The *Compendium of Essence* (Sarasangraha) is a specific text concerning the subject of divination.

**"The greedy..."** || Greedy means possessing excessive desire for some obtainable object. Cruel means having a heart devoid of mercy. Over-excited means having a mind thrilled by pleasures such as sexual enjoyment. <gloss>In the reading "thirsty," it means possessed of thirst.</gloss> "Bound by ancient enmity" refers to one who harbors long-standing grudges. "Cowardly" means lacking mental fortitude. The term "whose time has come" <term>Prāptakālam: the destined moment for an event to occur</term> is applied in common relation to all the preceding terms like "greedy," etc. By this, it should be understood that even if greed or cruelty are present, an affliction of the gaze might not occur if the timing is not favorable for it—so say some. And this is logical. Otherwise, one would have to accept that the greedy and others would *always* suffer from the affliction of the gaze. Yet, we see many greedy people who are free from such afflictions. This qualification ("whose time has come") applies to the earlier list (greedy, etc.) and the later list (diseased, etc.) according to the "Rule of the Middle Jewel" <note>Sanskrit: *madhyamaṇi-nyāya*; a logic rule where a central word in a sentence qualifies both what precedes and follows it, like a central gem in a necklace</note>. Alternatively, the term "whose time has come" is mentioned separately to show that an affliction may occur even without causes like greed, if the time is ripe. Or, one might resolve this by saying there is a "negative concomitance" <note>Sanskrit: *vyatireka-vyāpti*; the rule that if the effect is present, the cause must have been present</note>—that without these factors, the affliction won't happen—rather than a "positive concomitance" <note>Sanskrit: *anvaya-vyāpti*; the rule that if the cause is present, the effect must follow</note>—that if greed exists, the affliction *must* follow. But enough of this unnecessary elaboration. "Seize" means they afflict. || 52 ||

It draws from the Sarasangraha to list traits like greed, fear, and impurity as catalysts for these malevolent influences.</summary>

### One who is anointed with oil, one who has recently given birth,
### one who is addicted to drinking wine,
### one who is naked, one who is pregnant <note>original: "utpanna-sattvam"</note>, one who is overwhelmed by harsh arrows <note>likely referring to intense grief or physical pain</note>,

### Guhyakas <term>Guhyakas: a class of hidden supernatural beings or spirits, often attendants of Kubera, who can cause affliction</term>. || 53 ||

### The reasons why these spirits cause suffering,
### and the places they frequent, are now described so that they may be avoided from a distance. || 54 ||

### Disrespect, debt, enmity, obstacles, the reversal of fortune,

---

**Regarding "Anointed with oil" etc.** || "One who has produced a being" means a pregnant woman. "Shringataka" means a crossroads where four paths meet. By the adjective "cruel" <note>original: "vishama"</note> applied to the Guhyakas, it is understood that not all Guhyakas cause harm, but only those who are cruel by nature. Some consider "cruel" to be a variant reading for the state of the person afflicted, but they rely only on their own logic.

**Regarding "The spirits" etc.** || This is stated for the sake of avoidance—both by not creating the causes of affliction and by keeping away from their haunts. || 54 ||

**Regarding "Disrespect" etc.** || "Disrespect" refers to the reviling of the spirits themselves or their lords, such as Skanda. "Debt" is the failure to offer the worship and sacrifices <term>bali: ritual offerings of food or flowers</term> due to them. "Enmity" is a previous grudge held by them for some reason. "Obstacle" is the disruption of rituals intended for them. "Loss of fortune" is the underlying cause of these four. "The command of the Lord" arises from that. 

Others explain it differently: "Disrespect" is receiving insults from others; "Debt" is money owed to a creditor; "Enmity" is a feeling of hostility toward anyone; "Obstacle" is the interruption of one's own daily work. This interpretation is also appropriate. Generally, people do not go about insulting spirits or their lords, yet spirit-affliction is still observed. While one could argue these causes stem from insults in a previous birth, such a complicated explanation is not strictly necessary, as the second interpretation provides a practical path. Furthermore, these can easily be included under the "reversal of fortune." || 55 ||

# Chapter Fifteen

In caves, rocky peaks, mountain summits, forests, groves, and on mountain ridges; on the banks of rivers, step-wells, lakes, wells, ponds, and the shores of the ocean; 56

->Bathed, fragrant, radiant, joyful, devoted to temples;<-
->Speaking little, with minimal waste, eating sparingly, and free from anger. (69)<-

->Thirsting for water, jaggery, and milk; licking the corners of the mouth;<-
->Crawling on the ground with red eyes, prone to anger, dwelling on mountains. (72)<-

**"Bathed" etc.:** From the word "Bathed" up to "gentle gaze" are the characteristics of one possessed by a Divine Spirit <note>Deva-graha</note>. From "Praising the gods" up to "trembling limbs" are the characteristics of one possessed by a Demonic Spirit <note>Asura-graha</note>. Regarding the term "fragrant," it implies a natural pleasant odor without external application. "Hater of Brahma" <note>Brahmadviḍ</note>—here the word "Brahma" refers to a Brahmin. "Forming Mudras" means displaying specific gestures with the hands. "Eating excessively" means having a habit of consuming large quantities of food. (69-71)

**"Water" etc.:** The "corners of the mouth" <note>Sṛkṇī</note> refer to the edges of the lips. "Singing and dancing" refers to one who is well-versed in or constantly performing song and dance. "Making music with the mouth" means producing the sounds of musical instruments using only the mouth. "Crawling on the ground with red eyes" describes one whose eyes are red and who has a tendency to move along the earth. <margin>There is a variant reading: "Bhuvi-prasarpī," meaning one who is constantly wandering.</margin> "Prone to anger" <note>Krodhālu</note> means having a wrathful nature. <note>The author here engages in a technical grammatical debate regarding the suffix "-ālu" and how the word is formed, suggesting it implies one who "takes hold of anger from all sides."</note> "Moving as fast as thought" means having the habit of moving as quickly as the mind; a very fast walker. "Eyes like a glowing fire" describes eyes that are nearly red, and therefore resemble fire. "Blinded by enjoyments" means one who has lost the faculty of discrimination due to the experience of various pleasures. "Consuming the wind" <note>Gandhavāhāśī</note> means one whose habit is to "eat" the air; implying he may pass many days without any solid food at all. (72-75)

# Prashna Marga
## Page 250

Running about, eating one's own flesh, drinking wine and blood, dwelling in deserted villages, having a copper-colored complexion, being shameless, cruel, and diseased. <note>Verse 76</note>

Hating cleanliness, wandering at night, possessing great strength—these are the signs of one seized by a **Rakshasa** <term>Rakshasa: a powerful, often malevolent celestial or demonic being</term>. Having a smiling face, looking downward, seeing little, and keeping the fists clenched and hidden. <note>Verse 77</note>

Lacking luster, agitated, staring without blinking, remaining silent, and mocking the physician—these are the signs of one afflicted by a **Nistejas** <term>Nistejas-graha: a spirit that robs one of vitality or "tejas"</term>. <note>Verse 80</note>

Speaking incoherent words, full of hatred, having cold limbs, looking askance, discarding ornaments, having a darkened body, yet appearing clean and obsessed with ashes. <note>Verse 81</note>

Offering funeral cakes <term>Pinda: balls of rice or flour offered to ancestors</term> on Darba grass, performing water rites for the dead, and craving sesame, meat, and jaggery; being quiet—this is one seized by a **Pitri** <term>Pitri-graha: the spirit of an ancestor</term>. <note>Verse 82</note>

**Regarding "Running about" etc.:** "Running about" means having a habit of running here and there. "Hating cleanliness" means being impure oneself and unable to tolerate the cleanliness of others. "Clenched fists" refers to holding the fists and hiding them under cloth or similar items. "Terrifying" means frightening others. <note>Commentary on Verses 76-79</note>

**Regarding "Lacking luster" etc.:** "Without blinking" is an adverbial qualification of the act of seeing. <note>Commentary on Verse 80</note>

**Regarding "Incoherent" etc.:** "Speaking incoherent words" refers to sentences whose meanings are disconnected and lack logical relation to one another. <note>Commentary on Verse 81</note>

**Regarding "On Darba grass" etc.:** The word "at the time of" should be understood to complete the sense of the offering. <note>Commentary on Verse 82</note>

**Regarding "Living in solitude" etc.:** "When questioned" means even when asked repeatedly. <note>Commentary on Verse 83</note>

**Regarding "Wiping" etc.:** Here, the afflicted behaviors of the victim are attributed to the seizing spirit. This should be understood through the "metaphor of non-difference" <note>original: "abhedopacāra"</note> between the afflicter and the afflicted. The essential secret to be understood is that in all cases, the victim merely imitates the natural disposition of the seizing spirit. <note>Commentary on Verse 84</note>

# Chapter Fifteen

Breaking his own limbs, with withered body parts, dancing while appearing healthy, laughing suddenly without cause, eating excessively, speaking much—such a person is afflicted by the **Prallapa spirit** <note>The "Prallapa" or "Chattering" spirit causes incoherent or excessive speech.</note>. || 85 ||

With a harsh and rough voice, seeking out empty or broken places, a constant talker, foul-smelling, unclean, and restless—such a person is afflicted by the **Pishacha spirit** <note>Pishachas are often depicted as flesh-eating demons associated with filth and decay.</note>. || 86 ||

Threatening others, with restless red eyes, greedy, smearing himself with feces and mud, eating much, trembling, and speaking in a pitiful voice—such a person is seized by the **Antyaja spirit** <note>Antyaja refers to an "outcaste" spirit; the symptoms reflect a total loss of social decorum and hygiene.</note>. || 87 ||

Eating much, knowing the thoughts of others, craving raw meat, with wandering eyes, behaving without boundaries, smelling like a goat, and having stiff limbs—such a person is seized by the **Yonija spirit**. || 88 ||

Striking people, climbing trees, shouting vulgar words, imitating everyone, and appearing deformed—such a man is seized by the **Bhuta spirit** <note>Bhuta is a general term for a ghost or spirit, here manifesting as violent and erratic behavior.</note>. || 89 ||

Foaming at the mouth, with eyes rolled back, unconscious and fallen on the ground, contracting the hands and feet, with yellow eyes and gnashing the teeth; || 90 ||

Then regaining consciousness and becoming healthy again—such a man possesses the **Apasmara spirit** <note>Apasmara is the traditional term for epilepsy, here categorized as a spiritual seizure.</note>. Desiring white garlands and clothes, reciting the Vedas <note>The sacred scriptures of Hinduism.</note>, holding Kusha grass and similar items; || 91 ||

Performing the rituals of a priest, remaining clean, and worshipping the gods—such a person is seized by a **Dwija spirit** <note>A "Dwija" or "Twice-born" spirit refers to the ghost of a deceased Brahmin/priest.</note>. The **Brahmarakshasa spirit** generally acts with similar behaviors to the Dwija spirit. || 92 ||

---

*Commentary:*
Regarding "Breaking..." etc.: "Suddenly" means occasionally without a specific cause. || 85 ||

Regarding "Harsh..." etc.: "A constant talker" <note>original: "pralāpakaḥ"</note> means one who prattles or speaks nonsense; the word is formed with the suffix *nvul*. || 86 ||

Regarding "Threatening..." etc.: "Greedy" means not spending even when it is necessary. || 87 ||

Regarding "Eating much..." etc.: "People" refers to those who have come near him. "Vulgar words" <note>original: "apaśabdaḥ"</note> refers to speech that has lost its refined grammatical polish. || 88, 89 ||

Regarding "Foaming at the mouth..." etc.: "Possessing the Apasmara spirit" means one afflicted by the seizure-demon called Apasmara. In the clinical description of diseases, the ailment called Apasmara was previously defined by the characteristics: "With distorted limbs, he falls suddenly to the ground, losing consciousness," etc. Some say this disease and this spirit are one and the same. The truth is that this specific spirit is the cause that produces the disease. || 90-92 ||

# The Path of Inquiry

Always delighted by red flowers and similar items, constantly running, leaping, laughing, and writing; patient, performing the actions of a warrior <note>original: "kshatra-cheshta"; referring to the behavior of the Kshatriya or ruling caste</note>, singing, and roaring—such a person is possessed by a **Royal Spirit** <note>original: "Nripa-grahi"; a spirit of the kingly class</note>. || 93 ||

Yawning, laughing, weeping, shouting; acting as a farmer or a merchant; dancing, speaking unspeakable words, becoming angry, and being ill-mannered—such is one afflicted by a **Vaishya Spirit** <note>original: "Visha-atura"; the merchant/agriculturalist class</note>. || 94 ||

Eating feces, urine, and the like; speaking indistinctly; touching the genitals; weeping and laughing; hating priests <note>original: "Vipra-dvit"; those who hate Brahmins</note> and fond of women; having a body that appears unwashed—such a person is possessed by a **Shudra Spirit** <note>original: "Vrishala-grahi"; the laboring class</note>. || 95 ||

The spirits of the **Low-born**, the **Outcastes**, and the **Intermediate Spirits** <note>original: "Nicha-Chandala-Vyantara"</note> are known by a mixture of these signs. One who says, "I will leave, give me something," while singing and laughing softly— || 96 ||

Or one who says, "I will not leave," while harming themselves and speaking harshly—these are the signs of **Gentle** and **Fiery** spirits respectively. One should avoid a patient whom the spirit intends to kill <note>original: "Hantu-kamam"; meaning the case is incurable</note>. || 97 ||

Falling from ramparts or trees; entering fire or deep water; shaking the hair; being delighted for no reason; and speaking only when seeing a physician— || 98 ||

Weeping excessively with blood-red eyes—this man is possessed by a spirit intending to kill. Looking all around with anxiety, suffering from piercing pain, burning sensations, and fever— || 99 ||

Afflicted by hunger and thirst, suffering from head diseases, and repeatedly saying "Give! Give!"; being anxious, yet playing in a woman's body, speaking kindly and not causing harm <note>This describes a more benign possession or a specific subtype of spirit</note>. || 100 ||

---

**Commentary:**
Regarding "Red...": A "farmer" is one who promotes agriculture through speech and action. A "merchant" is one who mimics the activities of trade. || 93, 94 ||

Regarding "Feces...": "Hater of priests" means one who feels enmity toward Brahmins. || 95 ||

Regarding "Mixed signs...": The meaning is that for the three types—the Low-born and so on—one sees a mixture of the symptoms previously described for the twenty-four types of spirit afflictions. The half-verse beginning "I will leave" describes those afflicted by **Gentle Spirits** <note>original: "Saumya-graha"</note>, while the half-verse "I will not leave" describes those afflicted by **Fiery Spirits** <note>original: "Agneya-graha"</note>. "One should avoid the one he intends to kill" implies that such a case is incurable. || 96, 97 ||

Regarding "Falling...": "Ramparts, trees, etc."—the word "etc." includes mountains and similar heights. "Fire and deep water"—deep water refers to wells, tanks, and the like. <note>The commentator notes a specific grammatical compound here: a Bahuvrihi-Uttarapada-Dvandva-Samasa</note>. "Delighted" means being happy spontaneously without a cause. "Physician" refers to the one performing the remedy or the practitioner of mantras. "Seeing" is used here as a present participle denoting the cause. "Spoken to..." <insert>The commentary continues to explain the conditions under which the patient speaks</insert>

# Here begins the Summary of Essentials <note>Sanskrit: Sarasamgraha</note>

->To the Sun belong the Rudra-Ganas <note>fierce attendants of Shiva</note>, the fierce deities, and the lords of the serpents;<-

...performing [the ritual]. The characteristics of the "one desiring offerings" <note>Balikama</note> are described by the verse beginning with "Looking..." The characteristics of the "one desiring pleasure" <note>Rantukama</note> were not explicitly stated by the verse beginning with "Agitated..." The phrase should be read as "seeks, being impure." **By these behaviors:** This refers to the different types of spirits such as Gods <note>Devas</note>, Demons <note>Asuras</note>, etc., their classification as mild or fiery, and the three categories such as those desiring offerings. This is the meaning. **With appropriate rituals:** meaning those rituals suitable for the specific Devas, Asuras, mild or fiery spirits, and those desiring offerings. **With a steady mind:** with a mind solely focused on the task. **Through rituals:** through offerings, worship, and so on. || 102 ||

**Of the planets:** The **relationship to the planets** means "this specific spirit is to be understood through this specific planet." This is the intent. || 103 ||

**Here:** Regarding the subject of the relationship to the planets.

**To the Sun:** The word "fierce" <note>Ugra</note> is an adjective for both the spirits <note>Bhutas</note> and the lords of the serpents. The Moon's section ends with "planetary serpents." These are also associated with the Bhairava deities, as per the previous arrangement. **Attala** refers to specific types of buildings. **Benefic planets** refer to the Gods, Vinayakas, and others. Regarding the term **Nisteja-samjna** <note>literally "named lusterless"</note>: although the word *Nistejas* usually ends in a consonant, it is treated here as ending in 'a' for the sake of a name. Alternatively, it refers to those whose names contain "lusterless" syllables. This is how "lusterless" should be interpreted.

If one asks: "Some of the deities and spirits mentioned in these two verses are included in the twenty-seven varieties of spirits, while others are not; how then can the specific type of spirit be determined?" The answer is true: through the connection with the mentioned planets, only a general understanding arises. A distinct knowledge of whether it is a god or a demon does not arise from this alone. That must be determined by the specific characteristics mentioned previously.

The word "indeed" <note>original: "hi"</note> is used for emphasis. It should be understood that the classification of these groups of Rudra and others is based on the specific natures of the Sun and other planets as specified in the chapters on definitions. Thus, to bring consistency here, a somewhat difficult path of interpretation must be relied upon. For fear of becoming too lengthy and because it is not absolutely essential, it is not elaborated further. || 104, 105 ||

# Prashna Marga
## Page 256

The verses beginning with "Pitta-ushna" <note>referring to verses describing physical temperaments like bile and heat</note> which were previously mentioned in the *Prashna Anushthana Paddhati* <note>a manual on the practice of horary astrology</note> regarding the subjects already discussed, should also be considered here. || 114 ||

Let us return to the main subject.

If the Lord of Obstructions <term>Badhakadhipati: a specific planet designated as the 'obstacle-maker' based on the rising sign</term> aspects the Ascendant <term>Lagna: the rising sign at the time of inquiry</term> or the Lord of the Ascendant, even through a partial aspect like the "three-ten" aspect, an affliction caused by that "gaze" (sight) will occur. || 115 ||

When the Lord of Obstructions occupies the house of obstacles, or when there is a conjunction or mutual aspect between the Lord of the Ascendant and the Lord of Obstructions, one must declare an affliction arising from that sight. || 116 ||

On this matter, the *Santana Deepika* <note>The "Lamp of Progeny," a classical astrological text</note> states:

If the Ascendant is in a Moveable Sign <term>Chara Rashi: Aries, Cancer, Libra, or Capricorn</term> and Mars is in the seventh house, and the Ascendant is conjoined with a malefic planet, illness occurs due to the "sight of a deity." || 117 ||

If the Ascendant is conjoined with a malefic, Saturn is in the seventh house, and the Moon is aspected by malefic planets, illness occurs due to the "sight of a ghost" <term>Pishacha: a type of spirit or entity</term>. || 118 ||

***

**Regarding "Pitta..."** || These refer to the afflictions shown therein, such as those caused by the spirits of Shiva's attendants or epilepsy. || 114 ||

**Regarding "The main subject..."** || This refers to the explanation of afflictions caused by planetary aspects (sight).

**Regarding "Lord of Obstructions..."** || Concerning the "three-ten" aspect <note>original: "tri-dasha-dikshanena"</note>, there are two schools of thought. One is that Saturn has a special 3rd and 10th house aspect, Jupiter has a trine aspect, and Mars has a square aspect. The other is that all planets possess these partial aspects. The second view is also accepted here in accordance with traditional lineage. The intention is that if the Lord of Obstructions aspects the Ascendant or its Lord—whether the aspect is full or partial—it indicates an affliction of sight. A full aspect indicates a strong affliction, while a partial aspect indicates a weak one. This distinction is necessary to determine the appropriate remedial measures. || 115 ||

**Regarding "Obstructions..."** || Here, the word "aspect" <note>original: "drishti"</note> refers specifically to the full seventh-house aspect, not the partial "three-ten" aspects. || 116 ||

**Regarding "On this matter..."** || Regarding the determination of afflictions caused by sight.

**Regarding "In a Moveable Sign..."** || "Due to the sight of a deity" means the cause of the affliction is the gaze of a divine entity. Some read the text as "the Lord of the Ascendant conjoined with a malefic." The established conclusion is that it applies whether the malefic is with the Ascendant or its Lord. || 117 ||

**Regarding "Malefic..."** || "Due to the sight of a ghost" refers to an affliction caused by a planet designated as such. || 118 ||

**Regarding "If the Arudha..."** || The phrase "placed and given" should be applied everywhere, such as "in the leaves of the betel vine." "Nagavalli" refers to the betel vine. "In buttermilk or curds" means in either one of them. "Placed and given" is an illustration; it also includes poison that has become mixed [with food] and consumed by the turn of fate. || 133 ||

**Regarding "This..."** || Affliction by enemies was mentioned last in the list of objectives.

**Regarding "Humors..."** || The construction is: "arising solely from the three humors." Even in the case of an external affliction, there is an imbalance of the humors caused by it. This marks the beginning of the promised description of enemy-induced afflictions. || 135 ||

->The Path of Inquiry<-

The son of the Earth <note>Mars</note> without a sacred thread is like a King; while the son of the Moon <note>Mercury</note>, if learned but without a sacred thread, is called a servant of the Gods <note>Devadasa</note>. || 149 ||

Depending on the specific positions of Saturn, from its exaltation to its lowest point, the social classes are remembered to range from the servant of the Gods down to the outcaste <note>Chandala</note>. || 150 ||

### Here follows the Madhaviya:

Jupiter and Venus are the Priests <note>Brahmins</note>; Mars and the Sun are the Sovereigns <note>Kshatriyas</note>; the Moon is the Merchant <note>Vaishya</note>; the son of the Moon <note>Mercury</note> is the Laborer <note>Shudra</note>; and the son of the Sun <note>Saturn</note> is the lowest outcaste. || 151 ||

### And the Krishniya:

Venus and the Teacher of the Gods <note>Jupiter</note> are the two Priests; the Day-maker <note>Sun</note> and the Earth-born <note>Mars</note> possess the nature of the Sovereigns; Mercury and the Moon are the two Merchants; and Saturn is the creator of the Laborer and the mixed classes. || 152 ||

### And the Sarasamuccaya:

For the Sun, the status is either a Priest or a King or a Laborer who is a provincial ruler. For the Moon, it is a Priest or a Merchant. For Mars, it is a twice-born <note>Brahmin/Kshatriya/Vaishya</note> or a Laborer. || 153 ||

Regarding "The son of the Earth": He is like a King, similar to the Sovereign class; the distinction here is "without a sacred thread" <note>original: "anupaviti"</note>. || 149 ||

Regarding "Exaltation": From the point of exaltation onwards—in exaltation he is a servant of the Gods; in his primary domain <note>mula-kshetra</note> he is a provincial Laborer; in his own domain he is equal to that, and so forth. This is the intended meaning. || 150 ||

Regarding "The Priests and others": In Varahamihira’s view, Saturn represents the intermediate classes. In Madhava’s view, he represents the lowest outcaste <note>original: "chandala"</note>. This is the only difference. || 151 ||

Regarding "The two Priests": The phrase "possessing the nature of Sovereigns" <note>original: "kshatriya-bhavau"</note> is a complex compound where the two terms have different grammatical relations. This is established by the rules of grammar regarding "the locative in a descriptive compound." It means those who possess the status of the Sovereign class. It should not be forgotten that the correctness of such usage is managed by treating the indicator and the indicated as non-different. A "mixed class" <note>original: "sankara-jati"</note> is one born of parents of different classes. This is of two types: "with the grain" <note>original: "anuloma," where the father is of higher status</note> and "against the grain" <note>original: "pratiloma," where the mother is of higher status</note>. The word "iti" marks the end of Krishna’s opinion. || 152 ||

Regarding "Of the Sun": A "provincial ruler" <note>original: "mandaladhipa"</note> is one who holds regional authority regardless of specific caste. The "lowest born" is the outcaste. For Jupiter <note>Jiva</note>, it is the Priest; there is no alternative option here. For women, the status is independent of caste.

By the phrase "In debilitation or enemy signs," the author shows the distinctions arising from specific planetary placements. <term>Low caste</term> <note>nīcajāti</note> means reaching a degraded state because of not performing the duties prescribed for one's own caste. The original author himself explained: "Among the priests and others mentioned for the Sun, etc., designate them as 'low caste' [if poorly placed]." It should be understood that in the phrase "in debilitation, enemy signs, or combust," the word "enemy" refers to the sign of an enemy planet, and "combust" refers to the state of being too close to the Sun. Alternatively, one can consider the metaphorical identity between the state of being "combust" and the planet itself. Some who cannot tolerate this interpretation read the text as "debilitation, enemy signs, or <term>Māndya</term>" <note>a specific mathematical point in a horoscope</note>. However, that is contrary to the traditional reading and is not strictly necessary. Even with that assumption, the difficulty of interpreting the "enemy sign" remains the same. Alternatively, the word "combust" <note>mūḍha</note> is derived from the root *muh* (to be bewildered or faint); through grammatical suffixes, it directly expresses the meaning of "combustion" or "obscuration." Therefore, accepting the trouble of inventing an alternative reading for this section stems only from an ignorance of these grammatical rules. Enough on this. || 151, 152 ||

**Regarding the description of the caste of the one employing enmity:** The connection is that the cause of enmity and the alternative opinion on the matter are now being written. || 153 ||

**The caste of the lord of the sixth house:** He states the cause "here," meaning in the verse to follow. "Wealth and fruits" is a compound of two distinct items. "Clothing, grain, and four-legged animals" connects to the following verb. "Venus" is referred to here as the "Bright One." "Outcast, slave, and weapon" is a collective compound, hence its singular form. In the Sun's house, the causes are copper and so on. || 154, 155 ||

# Path of Inquiry

If the lord of the house of enemies <note>the 6th house</note> is situated in the Ascendant <term>Lagna: the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at the time of inquiry</term>, or if it is in the 10th house or the 7th house; or if the Ascendant is joined with or aspected by Mars, then one should declare that malevolent magic is present. || 164 ||

If Ketu <note>the South Node of the Moon</note> is placed in the 4th house or the 10th house; or if the Ascendant is joined with or aspected by Mars, then one should declare that malevolent magic is present. || 165 ||

If Ketu is in the 4th house or the 10th house, and Gulika <note>also called Mandi, a sensitive mathematical point in the chart associated with Saturn</note> is situated in a quadrant <note>the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses</note>, the disease is caused by "minor" malevolent magic <term>Kshudra-Abhichara: specifically refers to buried charms or substances like powders intended to cause harm</term>. || 166 ||

Now, the method for recovering powders and other materials placed by enemies for the purpose of killing, driving someone away, or other such ends, is described. || 167 ||

When Gulika is situated in a quadrant from the Ascendant, the Arudha <note>the sign rising at the moment the question is asked</note>, or the Moon, and is joined with or aspected by Saturn, one should declare that minor magic has been performed by an enemy. || 168 ||

If Gulika is placed in the 4th house or in the 4th division <term>Navamsha: a one-ninth sub-division of a zodiac sign</term>, the magic is said to be in the house; if it is in a water sign or a water division, it is in the water. || 169 ||

If Gulika is in its best division <term>Vargottama: when a planet occupies the same sign in both the main chart and the ninth-division chart</term>, it should be said to be in both places <note>inside the house and in the water</note>. If Gulika or Saturn is joined with Rahu <note>the North Node of the Moon</note>, it is near a serpent shrine. || 170 ||

If Mars is in a quadrant from them <note>Saturn and Gulika</note>, it is near a withered tree or a field; if Jupiter is there, it is in the house itself; if Venus is there, it is in the bedroom. || 171 ||

**On the 4th house placement**: The definition of "minor magic" is given in the last verse mentioned. The others refer to malevolent magic in general. || 164–166 ||

**On killing, etc.**: By the word "etc." in "driving away, etc.," one includes the creation of mutual strife, the paralyzing of the intellect or senses, the causing of madness, the destruction of wealth, the burning of the house, and the performance of subjugation rituals. "The method of recovery" refers to the way of retrieving those powders and other materials. || 167 ||

**On the Ascendant, etc.**: It should be understood that describing the symptoms is not inconsistent with the promised topic, as recovery is only possible if the object actually exists. || 168 ||

**On Gulika**: "In the house" means in the interior of the house. || 169 ||

**On the best division**: "In that" refers to Gulika. "In both" means both inside the house and in the water. "Near a serpent" means near a grove dedicated to serpents. This refers to the "minor magic" <note>the physical charm</note>. || 170 ||

**In a quadrant from them**: "In a quadrant from them" means in a quadrant from both Gulika and Saturn. || 171 ||

# Chapter Fifteen

If Mandi <note>A mathematical point in the sky, also called Gulika, considered the son of Saturn and often associated with malefic influences</note> is situated in a place suitable for the disposal of waste such as excrement or urine, and if Mandi is located in the trine of Aries <note>Aries, Leo, or Sagittarius</note> or in the Navamsha <note>The ninth divisional chart</note> of those signs: || 172 ||

The object is placed within a skull, or it is the bone of a tiger or a cat. If in the trine of Taurus <note>Taurus, Virgo, or Capricorn</note>, it is in a water pot. If in the trine of Gemini <note>Gemini, Libra, or Aquarius</note>, it is in a bamboo stalk or similar hollow wood. || 173 ||

If Mandi is in the trine of Cancer <note>Cancer, Scorpio, or Pisces</note>, it is placed in a skull <note>specifically a coconut shell, as clarified in the commentary</note>. If Mandi is situated in a "destruction" star <note>Samhara Nakshatras, such as Krittika</note>, a doll should be declared. || 174 ||

If located in a "creepy-crawly" sign <note>Scorpio</note>, a mystical diagram <term>Yantra: a geometric diagram used in rituals</term> or a bone with four corners is indicated. The quantity of these items should be known as equal to the number of degrees passed by Mandi. || 175 ||

One should indicate the direction based on the sign and Navamsha occupied by Mandi. This is one tradition; now another is being told. || 176 ||

If the Lord of Obstacles <term>Badhakadhisha: the planet ruling the house of hindrance</term> is in an "upward-looking" sign, the object is placed atop a tree. If in a "downward-looking" sign, it is buried in the earth. If in a "sideways-looking" sign: || 177 ||

One should say it is placed between stones or trees, or that it is a powder or similar substance. The type of tree and the specific location are determined by the element and the moon-sign of the Lord of Obstacles. || 178 ||

---

**Regarding "Manda" etc.** !! "Manda" here refers to the center of Mandi. "In the trine of Aries" means situated in Aries, Leo, or Sagittarius. The phrase "In the trine of Gemini" follows the same logic. "Vamsha" means bamboo. || 172, 173 ||

**Regarding "Karkata" (Cancer)** !! "In a skull" refers to a coconut shell. Starting from the verse "If Mandi...", the nature of the hidden object is being described. The "destruction stars" are Krittika and others. The words should be split as "Hi Putrika." "Putrika" is a human figurine made of wood. Some suggest the reading "Ahiputrika" <note>original: "अहिपुत्रिका"</note>, but that is not correct, as the original author has explained it according to the former method. || 174 ||

**Regarding "Keeta" (Scorpio)** !! This should be applied when Mandi is in the sign of Scorpio. "Of these" refers to the small objects used in sorcery. "By the degrees passed by Mandi" refers to the Navamshas consumed within that sign. In another school of thought, it refers to the Navamshas counted from Aries. Although the number would not exceed nine in the first case or twelve in the second, the number increases when multiplied by the strength (exaltation, etc.) of the lords of those divisions. || 175 ||

**Regarding "Mandi"** !! This pertains to determining the location of the sorcery. "Another tradition" is the remaining part of the explanation. ||

**Regarding "Urdhvasya" (Upward-facing)** !! When situated in an upward-facing sign. "Nihitam" means deposited or placed. ||

The quality of the location—whether superior or inferior—is determined by whether the planet is in a beneficial or malefic sign. The number of trees present is indicated by the number of Navamshas <note>A Navamsha is a 1/9th division of a zodiac sign, used for fine-tuning predictions</note> the Lord of Obstructions <term>Badhakadhipati: the specific planet designated as the 'obstructor' for a given chart</term> has traversed in its current sign. || 179 ||

The specific types of trees are determined by the lords of those traversed Navamshas. The hidden object causing the affliction is located either within the tree associated with the Lord of Obstructions <term>Badhesha: another term for the Lord of Obstructions</term> or in a tree nearby. || 180 ||

If the Lord of Obstructions is situated in a Water Sign, the object is on the bank of an ocean or river. Whether it is thrown into the water or buried in the earth is told by the direction the sign is facing (Upward-facing, etc.). || 181 ||

If the Sun is the Lord of Obstructions or is joined with him, the object is near a temple. If it is the Moon or a planet joined with the Moon, it is in a watery place or on salty/barren soil. || 182 ||

If it is Mars or a planet joined with Mars, it is in a cremation ground, near a fire, or on a battlefield. If it is Mercury or a planet joined with Mercury... || 183 ||

...it is in a place of learning or a recreation ground. If it is Jupiter or a planet joined with Jupiter, it is in a foreign land or a treasury. If it is Venus or a planet joined with Venus... || 184 ||

...it is in a bedroom or at the edge of a village. If it is Saturn or a planet joined with Saturn, the "Churna" <note>Churna refers to consecrated powder or a 'buried charm' used in sorcery</note> is located in a place where waste and scraps are thrown. || 185 ||

**Regarding the trees:** "Above the trees" refers to the trunk, branches, or upper parts of the trees. "In the earth" refers to the ground. "Facing sideways" refers to the Lord of Obstructions being in a Sideways-facing sign. The quality is judged by the signs: if a beneficial planet is in a malefic sign, it indicates a noble tree in a lowly place. If a malefic planet is in a beneficial sign, it indicates a lowly tree in a noble place. The types of trees are those mentioned in the verse beginning "The Sun produces trees with internal strength..." <note>A reference to a standard astrological classification of flora by planetary lordship</note> among those trees, it is specifically the tree of the Lord of Obstructions or one standing near it.

**Regarding the Lord of Obstructions:** If the water sign occupied by the Lord of Obstructions is "Upward-facing," the object is buried on the bank. If "Downward-facing," it is buried beneath the water. If "Sideways-facing," it has been thrown into the water. Some commentators suggest that Downward-facing means thrown in and Sideways-facing means buried, but that is not according to tradition and is contrary to logic. It is more reasonable that a Downward-facing sign indicates the act of burying. Enough on this. || 181 ||

**Regarding the Sun, etc.:** "Near the gods" means in the vicinity of a temple. And so on for the others. || 182-185 ||
